Let $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ be a holomorphic germ with $f(z)=Az+O(\|z\|^2)$, where $A\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ has distinct eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ satisfying the nonresonance condition
$$\lambda^k-\lambda_j:=\lambda_1^{k_1}\cdots\lambda_n^{k_n}-\lambda_j\neq 0\quad\text{for all } j\in\{1,\dots,n\}\text{ and all } k=(k_1,\dots,k_n)\in\mathbb{N}^n\text{ with }|k|=k_1+\cdots+k_n\geq 2.$$
Under this condition, $f$ is formally linearizable: there is a unique formal power series tangent to the identity that conjugates $f$ to its linear part $A$. Say that $f$ is analytically linearizable if this formal conjugacy converges in a neighborhood of $0$.

Determine the optimal arithmetic condition on the eigenvalues $(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ that guarantees the analytic linearizability of every such germ $f$, and decide whether this optimal condition can be obtained via a direct majorant-series argument.

representations.normalized: A geometric progression of integers is a set of the form $\{a r^k : k = 0, 1, 2, \dots\}$, where $a$ and $r$ are integers with $|r| \geq 2$ and $a \neq 0$. Determine whether there exists a positive integer $n$ and geometric progressions of integers $G_1, G_2, \dots, G_n$ such that every positive integer belongs to at least one of $G_1, \dots, G_n$. Equivalently, can the set of positive integers be written as the union of finitely many integer geometric progressions?

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The answer is negative and follows from a simple counting/density argument: a single geometric progression $\{a r^k\}$ with $|r|\geq 2$ contains at most $O(\log N)$ elements up to $N$, so any finite union contains $O(\log N)$ integers up to $N$, which cannot cover all $N$ positive integers up to $N$ for large $N$. This is a well-known elementary observation.

Let $K$ be a non-trivial virtual knot. By a theorem of Kuperberg, $K$ admits a representative as a knot in a thickened orientable closed surface $N = \Sigma_g \times I$ (where $I = [0,1]$) of minimal genus $g$, and this minimal-genus thickened-surface representative is unique up to homeomorphism of the thickened surface and isotopy of the knot. Such a representative is called a minimal realization of $K$.

An embedding $\iota \colon N \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$ of the thickened surface into 3-space is called unknotted if it extends to an embedding of a standardly embedded (unknotted) handlebody of genus $g$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Given any embedding $\iota \colon N \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$ and a knot $k \subset N$, one obtains a classical knot $\iota(k) \subset \mathbb{R}^3$.

Prove or disprove: for every non-trivial virtual knot $K$, there exist a minimal realization $k \subset N = \Sigma_g \times I$ of $K$ and an unknotted embedding $\iota \colon N \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$ such that the resulting classical knot $\iota(k) \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ is non-trivial.

Let $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ denote the circle, and for $\beta \in \{r, s\}$ with $1 \le s \le r \le \infty$ or $r = s = \omega$, let $\mathrm{Diff}^{\beta}_+(\mathbb{T})$ denote the group of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{T}$ of class $C^{\beta}$ (with $C^{\omega}$ meaning real-analytic). For $\alpha \in \mathbb{T}$, let $R_\alpha \colon x \mapsto x + \alpha$ be the rigid rotation by $\alpha$, and for $F \in \mathrm{Diff}^{\beta}_+(\mathbb{T})$ let $\rho(F) \in \mathbb{T}$ denote its rotation number.

Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and exponents $1 \le s \le r \le \infty$ (or $r = s = \omega$). Define the global arithmetic class
$$
C^{k}_{r,s} = \{(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k) \in \mathbb{T}^k : \text{every commuting $k$-tuple } (F_1,\dots,F_k) \in (\mathrm{Diff}^{r}_+(\mathbb{T}))^k$$
$$\text{with } F_i F_j = F_j F_i \text{ and } \rho(F_i) = \alpha_i,\ 1 \le i \le k,\text{ is simultaneously } C^{s}\text{-linearizable}\},
$$
i.e.\ there exists $h \in \mathrm{Diff}^{s}_+(\mathbb{T})$ with $h F_i h^{-1} = R_{\alpha_i}$ for all $i$. Define the local arithmetic class $C^{k,\mathrm{loc}}_{r,s} \subseteq \mathbb{T}^k$ by the same condition restricted to commuting $k$-tuples for which each $F_i \circ R_{\alpha_i}^{-1}$ is sufficiently $C^{r}$-close to the identity.

Determine the sets $C^{k}_{r,s}$ and $C^{k,\mathrm{loc}}_{r,s}$ explicitly in arithmetic terms (for all admissible pairs $(r,s)$ and all $k \ge 1$).

Let $V$ be a compact $C^\infty$ manifold and let $\mathrm{Diff}^\infty(V)$ denote the group of $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms of $V$, equipped with its standard $C^\infty$ topology. Fix $f \in \mathrm{Diff}^\infty(V)$ and let $U \subset \mathrm{Diff}^\infty(V)$ be a $C^\infty$ neighborhood of the identity. Define the local conjugacy class
$$O_{f,U} = \{\, g \circ f \circ g^{-1} : g \in U \,\} \subset \mathrm{Diff}^\infty(V).$$
A translation $T_\alpha$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^n = \mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$ is the map $x \mapsto x+\alpha \pmod{\mathbb{Z}^n}$, and $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is called Diophantine if there exist constants $C>0$ and $\tau \geq 0$ such that $|\langle k,\alpha\rangle - m| \geq C|k|^{-\tau}$ for all $k \in \mathbb{Z}^n \setminus \{0\}$ and $m \in \mathbb{Z}$.

Prove or disprove: If $O_{f,U}$ is a (smoothly embedded) submanifold of $\mathrm{Diff}^\infty(V)$ of finite codimension, then $V$ is diffeomorphic to a torus $\mathbb{T}^n$ and $f$ is $C^\infty$-conjugate to a Diophantine translation of $\mathbb{T}^n$.

representations.normalized: Consider a hypothetical model of physical space that is spatially unbounded (infinite in extent). Within such a model, is the supremum of admissible propagation speeds of physical signals or particles necessarily infinite? More precisely: formulate conditions on a space-time framework (a set X representing space, with an associated notion of distance and a notion of motion/trajectory together with an assignment of an instantaneous speed) under which the assumption that X has infinite diameter forces the supremum of allowed speeds over all admissible trajectories to be infinite. Determine whether the implication "space infinite ⟹ maximum speed infinite" holds, and if so identify a minimal set of axioms that yield it; if not, exhibit a counterexample (a model with infinite spatial extent but finite maximum speed).

representations.normalized:
A symplectic Lefschetz fibration over the 2-sphere $S^2$ is a smooth map $f\colon X\to S^2$ from a compact symplectic 4-manifold $(X,\omega)$ whose generic fiber is a smooth symplectic surface of genus $g\ge 0$ and whose finitely many critical points are modeled in local complex coordinates by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto z_1^2+z_2^2$, with the symplectic form restricting nondegenerately to the smooth fibers. Such a fibration is called holomorphic if $X$ admits an integrable complex structure compatible with $\omega$ in which $f$ is holomorphic onto $\mathbb{CP}^1$. Given two Lefschetz fibrations $f_1\colon X_1\to S^2$ and $f_2\colon X_2\to S^2$ of the same fiber genus, their fiber sum $f_1\#_f f_2\colon X_1\#_f X_2\to S^2$ is the Lefschetz fibration obtained by removing tubular neighborhoods of a regular fiber from each $X_i$ and gluing the resulting boundaries by a fiber-preserving diffeomorphism.

Question: Does there exist, for every genus $g$, a finite collection $\mathcal{H}_g$ of holomorphic Lefschetz fibrations of genus $g$ over $S^2$ such that for every symplectic Lefschetz fibration $f\colon X\to S^2$ of genus $g$, after fiber-summing $f$ a sufficient number of times with appropriately chosen members of $\mathcal{H}_g$, the result is isomorphic (as a Lefschetz fibration) to a holomorphic Lefschetz fibration?

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The question has been substantially addressed. Auroux's "A stable classification of Lefschetz fibrations" (math/0412120) shows that, for each genus, there is a universal Lefschetz fibration such that any two Lefschetz fibrations with matching numerical invariants become isomorphic after enough fiber sums with it. In genus 2, combined with the Siebert–Tian holomorphicity result for genus-2 Lefschetz fibrations with only irreducible singular fibers, this implies that every genus-2 Lefschetz fibration becomes holomorphic after fiber sum with a suitable holomorphic fibration. Thus the question is essentially resolved in the stable sense (and fully in genus 2), though a complete holomorphicity statement in all genera reduces to further open holomorphicity questions.

representations.normalized:
A symplectic 4-manifold is a smooth closed 4-manifold $X$ equipped with a closed non-degenerate 2-form $\omega$. Call such $(X,\omega)$ integral if the cohomology class $[\omega] \in H^2(X;\mathbb{R})$ lies in the image of $H^2(X;\mathbb{Z})$. Associated to $(X,\omega)$ are the Chern numbers $c_1^2[X]$ and $c_2[X]$ of the almost complex structure compatible with $\omega$, together with the symplectic invariants $c_1(X,\omega)\cdot[\omega]$ and $[\omega]^2$.

A Luttinger surgery on $(X,\omega)$ is the following operation: choose an embedded Lagrangian torus $T\subset X$ (whose tubular neighborhood is symplectomorphic to a neighborhood of the zero section in $T^*T^2$), choose an essential embedded loop $\gamma\subset T$, remove a tubular neighborhood of $T$, and reglue $T^2\times D^2$ by a diffeomorphism of the boundary 3-torus that performs a Dehn twist along $\gamma$ together with an integer number of meridional twists. The resulting 4-manifold carries a canonical symplectic structure extending $\omega$ outside the surgery region.

Question: Let $(X_1,\omega_1)$ and $(X_2,\omega_2)$ be two integral compact symplectic 4-manifolds satisfying
$$c_1^2[X_1]=c_1^2[X_2],\quad c_2[X_1]=c_2[X_2],\quad c_1\cdot[\omega_1]=c_1\cdot[\omega_2],\quad [\omega_1]^2=[\omega_2]^2.$$
Is it always possible to obtain $(X_2,\omega_2)$ from $(X_1,\omega_1)$ by a finite sequence of Luttinger surgeries?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is a well-known open problem posed as a conjectural picture for symplectic 4-manifolds. Subsequent work has used Luttinger surgery to construct many exotic small symplectic 4-manifolds and to relate symplectic manifolds with the same Chern numbers, but no general affirmative or negative answer to the surgery-equivalence question has been established. Recent papers (e.g., on unchaining surgery and exotic 4-manifolds via Luttinger surgery on Lefschetz fibrations) continue to investigate the question without resolving it.

Let $A=\mathbb{T}\times[0,1]$ (or $A=\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}$) be the closed (or infinite) annulus, with universal cover $\widetilde A=\mathbb{R}\times[0,1]$. A diffeomorphism $f:A\to A$ is called an area-preserving twist map if it preserves Lebesgue area, preserves boundary components, and a lift $\widetilde f(x,y)=(X(x,y),Y(x,y))$ to $\widetilde A$ satisfies the twist condition $\partial X/\partial y>0$. A rotational invariant curve for $f$ is an essential simple closed curve $\Gamma\subset A$ (i.e., homotopic to $\mathbb{T}\times\{0\}$) with $f(\Gamma)=\Gamma$; by Birkhoff such a $\Gamma$ is the graph of a Lipschitz function. The rotation number of $f|_\Gamma$ is the Poincaré rotation number of the induced circle homeomorphism. The map $f|_\Gamma$ is topologically transitive if it has a dense orbit in $\Gamma$.

Question: Does there exist a $C^3$ area-preserving twist map of the annulus possessing a rotational invariant curve with irrational rotation number on which the restriction of $f$ is not topologically transitive (equivalently, by Denjoy-type considerations, on which $f$ is conjugate to a Denjoy counterexample rather than to an irrational rotation)? Furthermore, does the same hold for every regularity class $C^r$ with $r\ge 3$, and even in the real-analytic category?

Setup and definitions.

(a) For a square matrix A with real entries, A is called stable (positive stable) if every eigenvalue of A has strictly positive real part.

(b) A real n×n matrix A is said to be weakly sign-symmetric if for every pair of index subsets α, β ⊆ {1,…,n} of equal cardinality with |α△β| ≤ 2, the product of the corresponding minors A[α|β]·A[β|α] is nonnegative. A real square matrix A is called a GKK matrix if every principal minor of A is positive and A is weakly sign-symmetric.

(c) A real square matrix A is called a τ-matrix if every principal minor of A is positive and, for every principal submatrix A[α] of A, the smallest real eigenvalue (the Perron-type root) of A[α] is at least the smallest real eigenvalue of A. (Equivalently, A is a nonsingular matrix whose principal minors are positive and which satisfies the eigenvalue-monotonicity property τ(A[α]) ≥ τ(A) for all principal submatrices, where τ(M) denotes the minimum of the real parts of the eigenvalues of M.) A GKK τ-matrix is a matrix that is simultaneously a GKK matrix and a τ-matrix.

(d) For positive integers n, k and a real parameter t ∈ (0,1), define the n×n Toeplitz–Hessenberg matrix A_{n,k,t} by
  (A_{n,k,t})_{ij} = 1 if i = j,
  (A_{n,k,t})_{ij} = −t^{(j−i+1)k} if j ≥ i+1 (entries above the diagonal arranged as in a Hessenberg/Toeplitz pattern with parameter t and exponent depending on k),
  (A_{n,k,t})_{ij} = c_{i−j} if i > j, where the subdiagonal entries are chosen so that the matrix lies in the τ-matrix / GKK class for the relevant ranges of parameters (the standard Toeplitz–Hessenberg construction parametrized by k and t producing GKK matrices for all t ∈ (0,1) and τ-matrices for n ≤ 2k+2 and small t > 0).

For a class C of square matrices, let C_n denote the set of all matrices in C of order at most n.

Question. For each of the following classes C, determine the largest integer n such that every matrix in C_n is stable:
 (i) C = the class of all matrices A_{n,k,t} with positive integers n, k and t ∈ (0,1);
 (ii) C = the class of all GKK τ-matrices;
 (iii) C = the class of all GKK matrices;
 (iv) C = the class of all τ-matrices.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Subsequent work ("Not all GKK τ-matrices are stable") provided explicit unstable examples A_{2k+2,k,t} for sufficiently large k and small t > 0, refuting the earlier stability conjectures and giving upper bounds on the largest n for which all matrices in each class are stable. Fix positive integers $d$, $N$, a nonnegative integer $\kappa$, and an integer $\nu$. Consider pairs $(D,\theta)$ where:

(a) $D \subset \mathbb{CP}^2$ is a symplectic curve of degree $d$ whose only singularities are transverse double points (nodes) and complex cusps; the nodes are split into $\nu_+$ positive nodes and $\nu_-$ negative nodes with $\nu_+ - \nu_- = \nu$, and the number of cusps is $\kappa$;

(b) $\theta\colon \pi_1(\mathbb{CP}^2 \setminus D) \to S_N$ is a compatible monodromy homomorphism, i.e.\ it sends each positively oriented meridian (geometric generator) around a smooth branch of $D$ to a transposition in $S_N$, and the relations imposed by the local models at the nodes and cusps are satisfied.

Define an admissible regular homotopy between two such pairs $(D_0,\theta_0)$ and $(D_1,\theta_1)$ to be a one-parameter family $(D_t,\theta_t)$ of pairs of the above form, where $D_t$ is a regular homotopy of symplectic immersed curves (so that generically $D_t$ has only nodes and cusps, with finitely many degenerations along the way), $\theta_t$ varies continuously with $t$, and the only permitted node creation/annihilation moves are those for which the two local geometric generators meeting at the created/annihilated node pair are mapped by $\theta_t$ to transpositions acting on disjoint pairs of sheets of the $N$-fold cover.

Problem. Classify all such pairs $(D,\theta)$ up to admissible regular homotopy, in terms of the fixed data $(d,\nu,\kappa,N)$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is posed as an open classification problem. A related result of Auroux–Kulikov–Shevchishin establishes that irreducible symplectic cuspidal curves in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ of fixed degree with prescribed numbers of (positive) nodes and cusps are regular homotopic, which addresses the case without the monodromy datum $\theta$ and without negative nodes. No source found that classifies the pairs $(D,\theta)$ in the general admissible setting; the problem appears to remain open.

$$L_V(x, v, t) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,g_x(v,v) - V(x, t), \qquad (x,v,t) \in TM \times \mathbb{T},$$
where $g$ is the Riemannian metric on $M$. Let $\Phi^t_V$ denote the associated (time-dependent) Euler–Lagrange flow on $TM \times \mathbb{T}$, and define the kinetic energy along a trajectory $(x(t), \dot x(t))$ by $K(t) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,g_{x(t)}(\dot x(t), \dot x(t))$.

Question: Does there exist a residual subset $\mathcal{R} \subset C^r(M \times \mathbb{T})$ (in the sense of Baire category) such that for every $V \in \mathcal{R}$ the Euler–Lagrange flow of $L_V$ admits at least one trajectory $(x(t),\dot x(t))$ with
$$K(t) \longrightarrow \infty \quad \text{as} \quad t \to \infty\,?$$

This is a well-known question of J. Mather concerning generic energy growth (a form of Arnold diffusion) for mechanical Lagrangian systems with time-periodic potentials. Partial results are known: Mather announced existence of orbits with unbounded energy growth in specific settings, and quantitative/structural results by Bolotin–Treschev, Gelfreich–Turaev, Cheng–Xue–Zhang, and others establish energy drift in particular classes (e.g., perturbations of uniformly hyperbolic systems, certain low-dimensional cases). representations.normalized:
Work in the complex projective plane $\mathbb{CP}^2$ equipped with its standard Fubini–Study symplectic form. A symplectic plane curve is a (possibly singular) 2-dimensional subset $D \subset \mathbb{CP}^2$ that is a smooth symplectic submanifold away from finitely many singular points, each of which is locally modeled on a positive node (transverse intersection of two smooth symplectic branches with positive intersection number) or a positive cusp (locally modeled on $\{z_1^2 = z_2^3\}$ in suitable symplectic coordinates).

Two such curves $D_1$ and $D_2$ are said to have the same combinatorial type if they have the same degree, the same number of nodes, and the same number of cusps.

A braiding operation along an embedded Lagrangian annulus is defined as follows. Suppose $A \subset \mathbb{CP}^2 \setminus D$ is an embedded Lagrangian annulus whose two boundary circles lie on $D$, each parallel to a local symplectic branch of $D$. In a Weinstein neighborhood of $A$, identified with $T^*A$, the curve $D$ locally consists of two parallel sheets near $\partial A$; the braiding operation cuts out a neighborhood of these two parallel sheets and reglues them as a half-twisted band (replacing the trivial braid $(-1,1) \times \{\pm 1/2\}$, viewed in $A \times (-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ modulo the $S^1$-factor, by a half-twist $\widetilde{\Gamma}$), producing a new symplectic curve with the same combinatorial type. On the double (or branched) cover this operation corresponds to a Luttinger surgery along an embedded Lagrangian torus.

Question: Given any two symplectic plane curves $D_1, D_2 \subset \mathbb{CP}^2$ with only positive nodes and cusps and with the same combinatorial type, must $D_2$ always be obtainable from $D_1$ by a finite sequence of braiding operations along embedded Lagrangian annuli?

representations.normalized:
Consider the Newtonian N-body problem in the plane with one dominant mass $m_0 = 1$ at the origin and $N-1$ further bodies of masses $m_1, \dots, m_{N-1} > 0$. Fix $N-1$ pairwise distinct positive radii $r_1, \dots, r_{N-1}$ and consider, for $m_0 = 1$ and $m_j$ sufficiently small ($1 \le j \le N-1$), the Keplerian limit in which each body $j$ moves on a circular orbit of radius $r_j$ around $m_0$, all orbits being coplanar and traversed in the same direction. View the dynamics on phase space (with the center of mass and total linear momentum reduced) and let $W$ denote any open neighborhood of the set of phase-space points corresponding to such configurations of distinct coplanar concentric circular orbits with common direction.

A wandering domain for a flow $\Phi^t$ on a phase space is a non-empty open set $U$ such that the sets $\Phi^{t}(U)$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$, are pairwise disjoint for an unbounded sequence of times (equivalently, $U$ is contained in the wandering set of $\Phi^t$).

Question: For all sufficiently small $m_1, \dots, m_{N-1}$, does every neighborhood $W$ as above contain a wandering domain of the planetary N-body flow?

A complex n×n matrix A is called a GKK matrix if (i) every principal minor of A is positive (so all principal submatrices have positive determinant) and (ii) A is weakly sign-symmetric, meaning that for every pair of index sets α, β ⊂ {1,…,n} with |α∩β| = |α|−1 = |β|−1, the product A[α∪{i}|β∪{i}]·A[β∪{i}|α∪{i}] of the two corresponding almost-principal minors (where {i} is the symmetric difference) is nonnegative. A GKK matrix A is called a τ-matrix if, in addition, for every principal submatrix B of A the spectral radius of B is an eigenvalue of B and equals the largest real eigenvalue of B (the "eigenvalue monotonicity" condition: ρ(A[α]) ≤ ρ(A[β]) whenever α ⊂ β).

For an n×n matrix A and an integer 0 ≤ j ≤ n, define
   c_j(A) = (1 / C(n,j)) · Σ_{α ⊂ {1,…,n}, |α|=j} A[α],
the average of all principal minors of A of order j (with c_0(A) = 1 and c_n(A) = det A).

Question: Does every n×n GKK τ-matrix A satisfy Newton's inequalities
   c_j(A)^2 ≥ c_{j−1}(A) · c_{j+1}(A)  for every j = 1, …, n−1 ?

Newton's inequalities are known to hold for M-matrices and inverse M-matrices (Holtz, Proc. AMS 2005). Subsequent work showed that GKK τ-matrices need not be stable, disproving several long-standing conjectures, but no source located explicitly resolves whether the Newton inequalities c_j^2 ≥ c_{j−1} c_{j+1} hold for all GKK τ-matrices. Status appears unresolved in the available literature.

Let $B_d$ denote the Artin braid group on $d$ strands, acting on the free group $F_d = \pi_1(D^2 \setminus \{p_1,\dots,p_d\})$ via the standard (right) action $b \mapsto b_*$ on the punctured-disk fundamental group. Fix a surjective homomorphism $\theta : F_d \to S_n$ to the symmetric group on $n$ letters that sends each meridian generator $x_i$ to a transposition, and define the liftable braid group
$$LB_d(\theta) = \{\, b \in B_d : \theta \circ b_* = \theta \,\}.$$
A factorization in $LB_d(\theta)$ is an ordered tuple $F = (b_1,\dots,b_r)$ of elements $b_i \in LB_d(\theta)$, each lying in a prescribed conjugacy class (the "type" of $b_i$); its product is $b_1 \cdots b_r \in LB_d(\theta)$. Two factorizations of the same length are Hurwitz-equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a finite sequence of Hurwitz moves
$$(\dots,b_i,b_{i+1},\dots) \leftrightarrow (\dots, b_i b_{i+1} b_i^{-1}, b_i, \dots), \qquad (\dots,b_i,b_{i+1},\dots) \leftrightarrow (\dots, b_{i+1}, b_{i+1}^{-1} b_i b_{i+1},\dots).$$
Concatenation of factorizations is denoted by $\cdot$. The Kharlamov–Kulikov stabilization theorem asserts: there exists a fixed standard factorization $F_0$ in $B_d$ such that for any two factorizations $F, F'$ in $B_d$ of the same element and with the same multiset of factor types, there exists an integer $n \ge 0$ for which $F \cdot F_0^n$ and $F' \cdot F_0^n$ are Hurwitz-equivalent.

Question: Does the analogous statement hold inside $LB_d(\theta)$? That is, does there exist a standard factorization $F_0$ (in $LB_d(\theta)$) such that, for any two factorizations $F, F'$ in $LB_d(\theta)$ of the same element of $LB_d(\theta)$ and with the same multiset of factor types, some integer $n \ge 0$ makes $F \cdot F_0^n$ and $F' \cdot F_0^n$ Hurwitz-equivalent within $LB_d(\theta)$?

Consider the one-dimensional discrete quasiperiodic Schrödinger operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$ defined by
$$(H_{\varepsilon,\omega,\theta}\psi)(n) = \psi(n+1) + \psi(n-1) + \varepsilon^{-1} v(\theta + n\omega)\,\psi(n),$$
where $v:\mathbb{T}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a non-constant real-analytic function on the circle, $\omega\in\mathbb{R}$ is a Diophantine frequency, $\theta\in\mathbb{T}$ is a phase, and $\varepsilon>0$ is a small coupling parameter (so that $\varepsilon^{-1}$ is large, i.e. the operator is in the strong-potential / "localized" regime). Let $\alpha(E)$ denote the integrated density of states (equivalently, the rotation number) of $H_{\varepsilon,\omega,\theta}$ at energy $E\in\mathbb{R}$, viewed as a function $E\mapsto \alpha(E)$.

Determine the regularity of the map $E\mapsto\alpha(E)$ in this large-$\varepsilon^{-1}$ regime. In particular, decide whether the distributional derivative $d\alpha/dE$ (the density of states measure) is singular continuous or absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$.

Setting. Consider a Hamiltonian partial differential equation written in the form
  u_t = J ∇H(u),
where u(t) belongs to a scale of Hilbert spaces, J is a (possibly unbounded) symplectic operator, and H is a smooth Hamiltonian functional. Assume that this equation possesses a nondegenerate one-parameter family

  {u_λ(t) : λ ∈ I ⊂ ℝ}

of time-periodic solutions with periods T(λ) depending on the parameter λ. Nondegeneracy is to be understood in a suitable Floquet/transversality sense (e.g. T'(λ) ≠ 0 and the linearized period map at u_λ has trivial kernel apart from the directions forced by symmetry).

Now perturb the Hamiltonian: replace H by H_ε = H + εK, where K is a smooth Hamiltonian functional and ε > 0 is small.

Problem. Establish a Lyapunov-type persistence theorem, not relying on Kolmogorov–Arnold–Moser (KAM) techniques (i.e. avoiding Diophantine small-divisor iterations on Cantor-like sets of frequencies), under reasonable hypotheses on H, K, and the family {u_λ}, asserting that for sufficiently small |ε| a set of parameters λ ∈ I of large measure (in the sense that its complement has measure tending to zero as ε → 0) gives rise to time-periodic solutions of the perturbed equation u_t = J ∇H_ε(u) close to u_λ.

In other words: identify natural functional-analytic and nondegeneracy hypotheses on Hamiltonian PDEs under which the classical finite-dimensional Lyapunov center / persistence-of-periodic-orbits theorem extends, so that most periodic orbits in a nondegenerate one-parameter family survive small Hamiltonian perturbations, with a proof method that is not of KAM type.

representations.normalized:
For an open cover U of a topological space X, recall the selection principle U_fin(O, O): X has this property (the Menger property) if for every sequence (U_n) of open covers of X there exist finite subfamilies F_n ⊆ U_n such that ⋃_n F_n is a cover of X. The space X has the Hurewicz property U_fin(O, Γ) if, moreover, the finite subfamilies F_n can be chosen so that the sets V_n := ⋃ F_n form a γ-cover, i.e., every point x ∈ X belongs to V_n for all but finitely many n (equivalently, {V_n : n ∈ ω} is eventually a cover at every point).

Working in ZFC alone (without additional set-theoretic axioms beyond ZFC), does there exist a set of real numbers X ⊆ ℝ that has the Menger property U_fin(O, O) but does not have the Hurewicz property U_fin(O, Γ)?

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The problem was solved in the affirmative by Tsaban and Zdomskyy ("Scales, fields, and a problem of Hurewicz", J. Eur. Math. Soc., 2008), who constructed in ZFC a set of reals that is Menger but not Hurewicz, providing a uniform (non-dichotomic) solution to Hurewicz's 1927 question.

Let $p$ be a prime, and let $G \subseteq S_n$ be a transitive subgroup. Fix an $r$-tuple $\sigma = (\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_r)$ of nontrivial conjugacy classes of $G$ satisfying the product-one condition (so that there is an associated Hurwitz space $H(\sigma)$ parametrizing isomorphism classes of Galois covers $f: X \to \mathbb{P}^1$ whose monodromy at the $r$ branch points has cycle types prescribed by $\sigma$). Let $H(\sigma)$ denote this Hurwitz space (over $\mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbb{Z}[1/|G|]$ or, more generally, the moduli stack of such covers), and let $M_g$ be the moduli stack of smooth projective curves of genus $g$, where $g$ is the genus of any cover of type $\sigma$ (determined by Riemann–Hurwitz). There is a natural forgetful morphism
$$\phi_\sigma: H(\sigma) \longrightarrow M_g, \qquad (f: X \to \mathbb{P}^1) \mapsto X.$$
Consider the base change $H(\sigma) \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{F}_p$, and let $f: X \to \mathbb{P}^1$ be a cover of type $\sigma$ corresponding to a generic geometric point of $H(\sigma) \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{F}_p$.

Compute the rank of the induced linear map on tangent spaces
$$d\phi_\sigma|_f: T_{H(\sigma), f} \longrightarrow T_{M_g, X}.$$

Consider the Korteweg–de Vries equation
  u_t + u_{xxx} - 6 u u_x = 0,  x ∈ T^1 = R/Z,
under periodic boundary conditions, regarded as an infinite-dimensional integrable Hamiltonian system on the Sobolev spaces H_0^m(T^1) = { u ∈ H^m(T^1) : ∫_{T^1} u dx = 0 }, m ≥ 1. By means of the Birkhoff coordinates (action–angle variables built from the periodic spectrum of the associated Hill operator), every such Sobolev space H_0^m(T^1) is foliated by invariant tori of arbitrary (possibly infinite) dimension; in particular, H_0^m(T^1) is filled by almost periodic solutions of KdV (solutions whose action vector has infinitely many nonzero components, corresponding to invariant tori of infinite dimension).

Question: For a generic small Hamiltonian perturbation
  u_t + u_{xxx} - 6 u u_x + ε ∂_x ∇ K(u) = 0
of the KdV equation (with K a sufficiently smooth Hamiltonian on H_0^m(T^1) and ε sufficiently small), does most of the family of almost periodic solutions of unperturbed KdV — i.e., a subset of the corresponding infinite-dimensional invariant tori of positive measure in an appropriate sense — persist as almost periodic solutions of the perturbed equation?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Available literature confirms the persistence of finite-gap (quasi-periodic, finite-dimensional torus) solutions of KdV under small Hamiltonian and quasi-linear perturbations, and recent works (e.g. on large KAM tori for quasi-linear perturbations of KdV, and on almost periodic solutions for derivative NLS) extend KAM techniques. However, surveys note that results on almost periodic (infinite-dimensional torus) solutions, especially for KdV-type equations with unbounded perturbations, remain sparse, and no result establishing persistence of "most" almost periodic KdV solutions under general small Hamiltonian perturbations has been found. The problem appears to remain open.

[{"title": "Large KAM tori for quasi-linear perturbations of KdV", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.08768", "snippet": "Persistence of space periodic multi-solitons (finite-gap solutions) of arbitrary size under quasi-linear Hamiltonian perturbations.", "claim": "Persistence is established for finite-dimensional (finite-gap) tori, not for almost periodic (infinite-dimensional) tori."}, {"title": "On the construction of almost periodic solutions for the derivative NLS", "url": "https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23202", "snippet": "Investigations into almost periodic solutions, especially in settings involving unbounded perturbations, are remarkably sparse.", "claim": "Almost periodic KAM results for KdV-type equations with unbounded perturbations remain largely undeveloped."}, {"title": "Hamiltonian PDEs (Kuksin, Handbook chapter)", "url": "https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~sergei.kuksin/p/06_handbook.pdf", "snippet": "Persistence of finite-gap solutions of KdV under small Hamiltonian perturbations established via KAM; almost periodic case posed as a problem.", "claim": "Question of persistence of almost periodic KdV solutions stated as an open problem."}]

Let $\mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and consider the space $Z$ of all nondecreasing functions $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$ such that whenever $f(n)<\infty$ one has $f(n)<f(n+1)$. Endow $Z$ with the subspace topology inherited from $(\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\})^{\mathbb{N}}$, where $\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$ is the one-point compactification of the discrete space $\mathbb{N}$; then $Z$ is a Cantor-like (compact metrizable, zero-dimensional) space. For each finite strictly increasing sequence $s=(s_0,\dots,s_{k-1})\in\mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$, define $q_s\in Z$ by $q_s(i)=s_i$ for $i<k$ and $q_s(i)=\infty$ for $i\geq k$; let $Q=\{q_s:s\text{ a finite strictly increasing sequence in }\mathbb{N}\}$, a countable dense subset of $Z$.

Let $\mathfrak{b}$ denote the bounding number, i.e., the minimal cardinality of a $\leq^*$-unbounded subset of $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, where $f\leq^* g$ means $f(n)\leq g(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$. A $\mathfrak{b}$-scale is a family $\{f_\alpha:\alpha<\mathfrak{b}\}\subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ which is $\leq^*$-unbounded and satisfies $f_\alpha\leq^* f_\beta$ whenever $\alpha<\beta<\mathfrak{b}$. Fix such a scale $B=\{f_\alpha:\alpha<\mathfrak{b}\}$ consisting of strictly increasing functions in $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}\subseteq Z$, and set $H = B\cup Q\subseteq Z$.

An open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of a topological space $X$ is called a $\gamma$-cover if $\mathcal{U}$ is infinite and for every $x\in X$ the set $\{U\in\mathcal{U}: x\notin U\}$ is finite. The selection principle $S_1(\Gamma,\Gamma)$ states: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of open $\gamma$-covers of $X$ one may choose $U_n\in\mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{U_n:n\in\mathbb{N}\}$ is a $\gamma$-cover of $X$.

Question: Must the set $H$ defined above satisfy $S_1(\Gamma,\Gamma)$?

The problem is a known question of Bartoszyński and Tsaban (also listed as a problem of Tsaban). Subsequent work by Miller and Tsaban ("Point-cofinite covers in the Laver model", arXiv:0910.4063) establishes related consistency results about sets of size $\mathfrak{b}$ satisfying $S_1(\Gamma,\Gamma)$ (e.g., the existence of an unbounded tower implies there is a set of reals of cardinality $\mathfrak{b}$ satisfying $S_1(\Gamma,\Gamma)$, and consistently every such set has cardinality $<\mathfrak{b}$), but no source located confirms a definitive resolution of whether the specific set $H = B\cup Q$ must satisfy $S_1(\Gamma,\Gamma)$. The status appears to remain unresolved based on available sources.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $X$ be a smooth projective connected curve over $k$. Let $G$ be a finite group and $\rho:G\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Aut}_k(X)$ a faithful action of $G$ on $X$. Consider the equivariant deformation functor $D_{X,\rho}$ on the category of complete local Noetherian $W(k)$-algebras with residue field $k$, which assigns to such a ring $A$ the set of isomorphism classes of pairs $(\mathcal{X},\tilde\rho)$ where $\mathcal{X}$ is a smooth proper relative curve over $\mathrm{Spec}\,A$ equipped with a $G$-action $\tilde\rho$, together with a $G$-equivariant isomorphism of the special fiber with $(X,\rho)$. This functor admits a versal deformation ring (hull) $R(X,\rho)$, a complete local Noetherian $W(k)$-algebra. Define the characteristic
$$\nu(X,\rho)=\mathrm{char}\big(R(X,\rho)/\mathfrak{m}_{R(X,\rho)}^{\,?}\big)$$
to be the characteristic of $R(X,\rho)$, viewed as an element of $\{0,p,p^2,p^3,\dots\}$ (so $\nu(X,\rho)=0$ if $R(X,\rho)$ has characteristic zero, and $\nu(X,\rho)=p^n$ if $p^n\cdot 1 = 0$ in $R(X,\rho)$ but $p^{n-1}\cdot 1\neq 0$).

Exhibit an explicit example of a pair $(X,\rho)$ as above for which
$$\nu(X,\rho)=p^n\quad\text{with }1<n<\infty,$$
or prove that no such example exists.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of whether typical solutions of NLS exhibit unbounded growth of Sobolev norms or weak decay to zero is widely regarded as open. Partial results exist showing the existence of particular solutions with growing Sobolev norms (Bourgain, Kuksin, Colliander–Keel–Staffilani–Takaoka–Tao, Guardia–Kaloshin, Hani, Guardia–Hani–Haus–Maspero–Procesi, and many others), and unbounded growth has been established on irrational tori and other settings, but the genericity statement about typical initial data remains unresolved.

Consider the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation under periodic boundary conditions,
  u_t + u_{xxx} - 6 u u_x = 0,  x ∈ T = R/Z,
viewed as an integrable infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian system. Its phase space (e.g. a Sobolev space H^s(T) of zero-mean functions) is foliated by invariant finite-gap tori, i.e. compact invariant tori obtained from finite-dimensional reductions of the integrable hierarchy.

Let ε > 0 be a small parameter and consider an ε-perturbation of KdV of the form
  u_t + u_{xxx} - 6 u u_x = ε F(u),
where F is a sufficiently regular (say smooth, Hamiltonian) perturbation.

Question: Does there exist a constant a > 0 such that, for every M > 0, there is a constant C_M > 0 with the following property? For every sufficiently small ε > 0 and every solution u(t) of the perturbed equation (with initial data in a suitable bounded region of phase space), one has
  dist(u(t), T_{ε}) ≤ ε^a   for all 0 ≤ t ≤ T_ε,
where T_ε is some finite-gap torus (possibly depending on the solution) and the time scale satisfies
  T_ε ≥ C_M ε^{-M}.

In other words, in the spirit of Nekhoroshev's theorem, does every solution of the ε-perturbed KdV equation stay ε^a-close to some finite-gap torus on time intervals longer than any prescribed inverse polynomial power of ε?

Let $X$ be a topological space. A cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ by proper subsets is called an $\omega$-cover if every finite subset of $X$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{U}$, and a $\gamma$-cover if $\mathcal{U}$ is infinite and every point of $X$ belongs to all but finitely many members of $\mathcal{U}$. Let $B_\Omega(X)$ denote the family of all countable Borel $\omega$-covers of $X$, and let $B_\Gamma(X)$ denote the family of all countable Borel $\gamma$-covers of $X$.

For families $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ of covers of $X$, define the following selection principles:
- $S_1(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with each $\mathcal{U}_n\in\mathcal{A}$, there exist $U_n\in\mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{U_n:n\in\mathbb{N}\}\in\mathcal{B}$.
- $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with each $\mathcal{U}_n\in\mathcal{A}$, there exist finite $\mathcal{F}_n\subseteq\mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_n\mathcal{F}_n\in\mathcal{B}$.

Say that a class $\Pi$ of topological spaces is closed under taking finite powers if $X\in\Pi$ implies $X^n\in\Pi$ for every positive integer $n$.

Question: Is any of the three classes
$$S_1(B_\Omega,B_\Gamma),\quad S_1(B_\Omega,B_\Omega),\quad S_{\mathrm{fin}}(B_\Omega,B_\Omega)$$
(viewed as the class of spaces $X$ satisfying the corresponding principle) closed under taking finite powers?

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $X$ be a smooth projective connected curve of genus $g\geq 2$ over $k$. Denote by $\pi_1(X)$ the étale fundamental group of $X$, and let $\pi_1^{(r)}(X)$ denote the quotient of $\pi_1(X)$ classifying finite étale Galois covers $Y\to X$ whose Galois group is an $r$-step nilpotent (or, more generally, suitable "level $r$") $p$-group, for a fixed integer $r\geq 1$. Let $J_X$ be the Jacobian variety of $X$; recall that $J_X$ is called ordinary if its $p$-rank equals $g$ (equivalently, $J_X[p](k)\cong (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^g$), and non-ordinary otherwise.

Determine the precise relationship between the finiteness of the group $\pi_1^{(r)}(X)$ and the ordinariness of the Jacobian $J_X$. Specifically:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Does $J_X$ being ordinary imply that $\pi_1^{(r)}(X)$ is infinite (or finite) for every $r\geq 1$?
\item Conversely, does the finiteness, respectively infiniteness, of $\pi_1^{(r)}(X)$ for some (or all) $r$ force $J_X$ to be ordinary, respectively non-ordinary?
\end{enumerate}
Formulate and prove a sharp statement linking these two properties.

Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane in general position (no four points cocircular). The Delaunay triangulation $\mathrm{DT}(P)$ is the planar straight-line graph on vertex set $P$ in which three points $p,q,r \in P$ form a triangular face if and only if the open disk circumscribing $p,q,r$ contains no other point of $P$. For two points $u,v \in P$, let $d_{\mathrm{DT}(P)}(u,v)$ denote the length of a shortest path from $u$ to $v$ in $\mathrm{DT}(P)$, where each edge is weighted by its Euclidean length, and let $\|u-v\|$ denote the Euclidean distance. The (worst-case) spanning ratio of the Delaunay triangulation is
$$\rho \;=\; \sup_{P}\;\max_{u\neq v\in P}\;\frac{d_{\mathrm{DT}(P)}(u,v)}{\|u-v\|},$$
where the supremum is over all finite planar point sets $P$ in general position.

(a) Determine the exact value of $\rho$, or prove the best possible upper and lower bounds on $\rho$.

(b) Let $\rho_{\mathrm{conv}}$ denote the analogous quantity where the supremum is restricted to point sets $P$ in convex position (i.e., the points of $P$ are the vertices of a convex polygon). Prove or disprove that $\rho_{\mathrm{conv}} < \rho$, and determine the best possible upper bound on $\rho_{\mathrm{conv}}$.

The exact worst-case spanning ratio of the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation remains open. The best known upper bound is approximately 1.998 (Xia, 2013), improving the classical 2.42 bound of Keil–Gutwin (1989); the best known lower bound is approximately 1.5846 (disproving the long-standing π/2 conjecture). Let X be an infinite topological space (typically a set of real numbers or a Tychonoff space). An open cover U of X is called an ω-cover if X itself is not a member of U and for every finite subset F ⊆ X there exists U ∈ U with F ⊆ U. An open cover U of X is called a γ-cover if U is infinite and for every x ∈ X the set {U ∈ U : x ∉ U} is finite. Denote by Ω the family of open ω-covers of X and by Γ the family of open γ-covers of X.

For collections A and B of covers, define the following selection principles:
• S_1(A, B): For every sequence (U_n)_{n∈ℕ} of elements of A there exist U_n ∈ U_n such that {U_n : n ∈ ℕ} ∈ B.
• S_fin(A, B): For every sequence (U_n)_{n∈ℕ} of elements of A there exist finite sets F_n ⊆ U_n such that ⋃_{n∈ℕ} F_n ∈ B.

A class C of topological spaces is said to be closed under finite unions if whenever X, Y ∈ C the topological sum (equivalently, the union, when X and Y are subspaces of a common space) X ∪ Y also belongs to C.

Question: Is it consistent with the axioms of ZFC that at least one of the three classes
  S_fin(Ω, Ω),   S_1(Γ, Ω),   S_fin(Γ, Ω)
(viewed as classes of spaces satisfying the corresponding selection principle) is closed under finite unions?

For a finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, a plane geometric graph on $P$ is a straight-line embedded graph with vertex set $P$ whose edges (drawn as Euclidean line segments) pairwise do not cross. For a connected geometric graph $G$ on $P$, define its spanning ratio (or stretch factor) by
$$\mathrm{sr}(G)=\max_{u,v\in P,\ u\neq v}\frac{d_G(u,v)}{\|u-v\|},$$
where $d_G(u,v)$ is the length of a shortest path from $u$ to $v$ in $G$ (using Euclidean edge lengths) and $\|u-v\|$ is the Euclidean distance.

Define
$$\rho^*=\inf\Bigl\{C\ge 1:\ \text{for every finite }P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\text{ there exists a connected plane geometric graph }G\text{ on }P\text{ with }\mathrm{sr}(G)\le C\Bigr\}.$$

Determine the exact value of $\rho^*$.

Work over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p > 2$. For $\lambda \in k \setminus \{0,1\}$, consider the elliptic curve $E_\lambda : y^2 = x(x-1)(x-\lambda)$; call $\lambda$ a "supersingular value" if $E_\lambda$ is supersingular. Let $M$ denote the unique isomorphism type of $\mathrm{BT}_1$ group scheme of rank $p^2$ over $k$ that occurs as the $p$-torsion of a supersingular elliptic curve (so there is a non-split exact sequence $0 \to \alpha_p \to M \to \alpha_p \to 0$). For a smooth projective curve $X$ of genus $2$, the $p$-torsion $J_X[p]$ of its Jacobian is a $\mathrm{BT}_1$ group scheme of rank $p^4$ with a principal polarization; the possible isomorphism types of such a $J_X[p]$ are exactly the four group schemes
$$(\mathbb{Z}/p \oplus \mu_p)^2, \qquad M \oplus (\mathbb{Z}/p \oplus \mu_p), \qquad N, \qquad M^2,$$
where $N$ denotes the unique remaining principally polarized $\mathrm{BT}_1$ group scheme of rank $p^4$ with $p$-rank $0$ and $a$-number $1$.

Let $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3 \in k$ be three distinct supersingular values, and let $X$ be the genus-$2$ hyperelliptic curve with affine model
$$y^2 = x(x-1)(x-\lambda_1)(x-\lambda_2)(x-\lambda_3).$$
Determine which of the four group schemes $(\mathbb{Z}/p \oplus \mu_p)^2$, $M \oplus (\mathbb{Z}/p \oplus \mu_p)$, $N$, $M^2$ can arise as $J_X[p]$ for such a choice of $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3$, and characterize when each occurs.

For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of points in general position, a plane spanning tree of $P$ is a straight-line tree $T$ with vertex set $P$ whose edges (drawn as line segments) are pairwise non-crossing and which connects all points of $P$. For a connected straight-line graph $G$ on $P$, the spanning ratio (also called dilation or stretch factor) of $G$ is
$$\operatorname{sr}(G)\;=\;\max_{u
eq v\in P} rac{d_G(u,v)}{\|u-v\|_2},$$
where $d_G(u,v)$ denotes the length of a shortest path in $G$ between $u$ and $v$ (with edge weights equal to Euclidean lengths) and $\|u-v\|_2$ is the Euclidean distance.

Consider the following decision problem: given a finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{Q}^2$ and a rational number $\delta\geq 1$, decide whether there exists a plane spanning tree $T$ of $P$ with $\operatorname{sr}(T)\leq\delta$. Equivalently, the optimization problem asks to compute a plane spanning tree of $P$ minimizing $\operatorname{sr}(T)$ among all plane spanning trees on $P$.

Prove or disprove that this problem is NP-hard.

The unrestricted (possibly crossing) minimum-dilation spanning tree problem is known to be NP-hard (Cheong, Haverkort, Lee, 2007/2008), and computing minimum-dilation graphs with a bounded number of edges is NP-hard whether or not crossings are allowed. However, the NP-hardness reductions in these works do not enforce planarity of the optimal tree, so the complexity of computing a minimum-spanning-ratio plane spanning tree of a planar point set appears to remain open. No proof of NP-hardness or polynomial-time algorithm specifically for the plane (non-crossing) version has been located.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $\mathbb{F}_p\subset k$ be the prime field. For a polynomial $f(X)\in k[X]$, consider the smooth affine curve
$$C_f:\quad W^p-W=f(X)\subset\mathbb{A}^2_k,$$
a $p$-cyclic (Artin–Schreier) cover of the affine line. Let $\mathrm{Aut}(C_f)$ denote the automorphism group of the smooth projective model of $C_f$ over $k$, and let $G_f\subset\mathrm{Aut}(C_f)$ be a $p$-Sylow subgroup. The cover comes equipped with a canonical Artin–Schreier covering group $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Aut}(C_f)$ generated by $(X,W)\mapsto(X,W+1)$, which lies in $G_f$ and is normal there, giving rise to a central extension
$$1\longrightarrow \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}\longrightarrow G_f\longrightarrow (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n\longrightarrow 1$$
for some $n\geq 0$.

Question: Given any group extension
$$1\longrightarrow \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n\longrightarrow 1$$
that arises in this way as the $p$-Sylow subgroup of $\mathrm{Aut}(C_f)$ for some $f(X)\in k[X]$, does there exist a polynomial $f(X)\in\mathbb{F}_p[X]$ such that the corresponding cover $C_f$ realizes the given extension, with the distinguished kernel $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ identified with the Artin–Schreier covering group of $C_f$?

Setup. Given a finite point set $P$ in the Euclidean plane, the greedy triangulation of $P$ is constructed as follows: order all $\binom{|P|}{2}$ straight-line segments between pairs of points in non-decreasing order of length, and process them in this order, adding a segment to the current edge set whenever it does not properly cross any previously added segment. The resulting plane graph $\mathrm{GT}(P)$ is a triangulation of the convex hull of $P$.

For a real number $\alpha\in(0,\pi/2)$, an edge $e=uv$ of a plane graph is said to satisfy the $\alpha$-diamond property if at least one of the two isosceles triangles having $e$ as base and base angles equal to $\alpha$ contains no vertex of the graph (other than $u$ and $v$) in its interior. A plane graph has the $\alpha$-diamond property if every edge does. Whenever a plane triangulation has the $\alpha$-diamond property, it is a $t$-spanner of the complete Euclidean graph on its vertex set, with stretch factor $t$ bounded by an explicit function of $\alpha$ that decreases as $\alpha$ increases.

It is known that, for every finite point set $P$, the greedy triangulation $\mathrm{GT}(P)$ has the $\alpha$-diamond property for $\alpha=\pi/6$.

Question. Let $\alpha^{*}$ denote the supremum of all $\alpha\in(0,\pi/2)$ such that for every finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^{2}$ the greedy triangulation $\mathrm{GT}(P)$ satisfies the $\alpha$-diamond property. Determine whether $\alpha^{*}>\pi/6$, and if so, give the best possible value of $\alpha^{*}$.

Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane. For a real parameter $\beta \geq 1$, the β-skeleton of $P$ (in the circle-based / "lune-based" definition) is the undirected graph on vertex set $P$ in which two points $p, q \in P$ are joined by an edge if and only if the open region $L_\beta(p,q)$ — defined, for $\beta \geq 1$, as the intersection of the two open disks of radius $\beta\,|pq|/2$ whose centers lie on the line through $p$ and $q$ at distance $(\beta/2 - 1/2)|pq|$ from the midpoint of $pq$ on opposite sides — contains no point of $P \setminus \{p,q\}$. (At $\beta = 1$ this is the Gabriel graph; at $\beta = 2$ this is the relative neighborhood graph.)

The spanning ratio (stretch factor) of a connected geometric graph $G$ on $P$ is
$$\mathrm{sr}(G) \;=\; \max_{p \neq q \in P} \frac{d_G(p,q)}{|pq|},$$
where $d_G(p,q)$ denotes the length of a shortest path from $p$ to $q$ in $G$ (with edges weighted by Euclidean length), and $|pq|$ denotes the Euclidean distance.

For each $\beta \in [1,2]$, let
$$f(\beta, n) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{\mathrm{sr}(\beta\text{-skeleton of } P) \;:\; P \subset \mathbb{R}^2,\ |P| = n\bigr\}.$$

It is known that $f(1,n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n})$ (Gabriel graphs) and that $f(2,n)$ can be as large as $\Omega(n)$ (relative neighborhood graphs). Determine whether one can establish, for $\beta$ ranging over the interval $[1,2]$, a worst-case lower bound on $f(\beta,n)$ as a function of $n$ that depends explicitly and non-trivially on $\beta$ (i.e., a lower bound that strengthens monotonically as $\beta$ increases from $1$ toward $2$, interpolating between the $\Theta(\sqrt{n})$ bound at $\beta=1$ and the $\Omega(n)$ bound at $\beta=2$).

Let $P$ be a finite set of points in general position in the Euclidean plane. For a parameter $\beta\in[0,1]$, the $\beta$-skeleton $\mathrm{BSKEL}_\beta(P)$ is the graph on vertex set $P$ in which two points $p,q\in P$ are joined by an edge if and only if the open lune $L_\beta(p,q)$, defined as the intersection of the two open disks of radius $|pq|/\beta$ passing through both $p$ and $q$ and having centers on the line through $p$ and $q$ (with the convention that for $\beta=0$ the lune degenerates to the open segment $pq$, and for $\beta=1$ it is the open disk with diameter $pq$), contains no point of $P$. Let $\mathrm{DT}(P)$ denote the Delaunay triangulation of $P$. Define the relaxed Gabriel graph
$$\mathrm{RGG}_\beta(P) \;=\; \mathrm{BSKEL}_\beta(P)\,\cap\,\mathrm{DT}(P).$$
For a connected geometric graph $G$ on $P$, its spanning ratio (stretch factor) is
$$t(G) \;=\; \max_{p\neq q\in P}\frac{d_G(p,q)}{|pq|},$$
where $d_G$ denotes the shortest-path distance in $G$ with Euclidean edge weights. Let
$$f(n,\beta) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{t(\mathrm{RGG}_\beta(P)) : |P|=n,\ P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\text{ in general position}\bigr\}.$$
For each fixed $\beta\in[0,1]$, determine whether the currently known asymptotic upper and lower bounds on $f(n,\beta)$ as $n\to\infty$ are tight, i.e., whether they match up to constants (and if not, establish improved matching upper and lower bounds).

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $C$ be a smooth, projective, geometrically connected curve over $k$ of genus $g_C \ge 2$. Let $G \subseteq \mathrm{Aut}_k(C)$ be a finite $p$-subgroup. The pair $(C,G)$ is called a big action if $G$ is non-trivial and the inequality \[ \frac{|G|}{g_C} \;>\; \frac{2p}{p-1} \] holds. For a big action $(C,G)$, fix a point $\infty \in C$ such that $G$ is contained in the wild inertia at $\infty$ (this point is unique), and let $G_i$ ($i \ge 0$) denote the lower ramification filtration of $G$ at $\infty$.

Consider big actions $(C,G)$ satisfying the additional condition that the second ramification group $G_2$ is contained in the center $Z(G)$ of $G$ and that the quotient $G/G_2$ is abelian (this is the condition (N)).

(a) Determine the set $\mathcal{V} \subseteq \mathbb{Q}_{>0}$ of all values that can occur as $|G|/g_C^{\,2}$ for such pairs $(C,G)$ with $g_C \ge 2$.

(b) For each value $v \in \mathcal{V}$, give an upper bound on the dimension of the locally closed subvariety of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_{g}$ (over $k$) parametrizing isomorphism classes of curves $C$ of genus $g = g_C$ admitting a big action $(C,G)$ satisfying condition (N) with $|G|/g_C^{\,2} = v$.

For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of points in the plane, a geometric graph on $P$ is a graph whose vertex set is $P$ and whose edges are straight-line segments between pairs of points of $P$, with edge weights equal to the Euclidean lengths of the segments. Such a graph is called plane if no two of its edges cross. For a real number $t\geq 1$, a geometric graph $G$ on $P$ is a $t$-spanner of $P$ if for every pair $p,q\in P$ the length of a shortest path from $p$ to $q$ in $G$ is at most $t\cdot\|p-q\|$. The maximum degree of $G$ is $\Delta(G)=\max_{v\in P}\deg_G(v)$.

Determine the smallest integer $\Delta^\ast$ with the following property: there exists a constant $t\geq 1$ (independent of $P$) such that for every finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ there exists a plane $t$-spanner $G$ on $P$ with $\Delta(G)\leq \Delta^\ast$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

It is known that 3 is a lower bound on the maximum degree of any plane spanner. Bonichon, Kanj, Perković, and Ravelomanana (2014) proved that maximum degree 4 always suffices, with stretch factor improved by Kanj, Perković, and Türkoğlu (SoCG 2016) to 20. Whether maximum degree 3 suffices for arbitrary point sets remains open; for points in convex position degree 3 is known to be tight.

$$Y^4 \;=\; (1+X)^2 + X^3 \;=:\; F(X).$$
The map $(X,Y)\mapsto X$ realizes $C$ as a $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2$-cyclic Galois cover of the projective line $\mathbb{P}^1$, ramified exactly at the four points $X=x_1,x_2,x_3$ (the three roots of $F$) and $X=\infty$. (iii) the induced action of the full decomposition/monodromy group on the special fiber of the stable model, including its compatibility with the Galois action of $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2$ of the cover.

representations.normalized:
Let $P$ be a finite set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane. A geometric graph on $P$ is a straight-line graph whose vertex set is $P$, with edge weights equal to the Euclidean lengths of the corresponding segments. A geometric graph $G$ is called a plane $t$-spanner of $P$ (for some real constant $t \geq 1$, called the stretch factor) if (i) no two edges of $G$ cross, and (ii) for every pair of points $p, q \in P$, the length of a shortest path from $p$ to $q$ in $G$ is at most $t \cdot \|pq\|$, where $\|pq\|$ is the Euclidean distance.

The total weight $w(G)$ of $G$ is the sum of its edge weights, and $w(\mathrm{MST}(P))$ denotes the weight of a Euclidean minimum spanning tree of $P$. The maximum degree $\Delta(G)$ is the largest number of edges incident to any vertex.

It is known that for every finite point set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ one can construct, in $O(n \log n)$ time, a plane $t$-spanner $G$ of $P$ satisfying simultaneously
\[
\Delta(G) \leq D, \qquad t \leq T, \qquad w(G) \leq C \cdot w(\mathrm{MST}(P)),
\]
for certain absolute constants $D$, $T$, and $C$ achieved by existing constructions.

Question: Are the currently known constants $D$, $T$, and $C$ for the simultaneous bounded-degree, bounded-stretch, low-weight plane spanner problem tight? More precisely, determine matching lower bounds (or improved upper bounds) on the achievable triples $(D, T, C)$ such that every $n$-point set in the plane admits a plane $t$-spanner with maximum degree at most $D$, stretch factor at most $T$, and total weight at most $C \cdot w(\mathrm{MST}(P))$.

Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $K^{\mathrm{tame}}$ denote a maximal tamely ramified extension of $K$ inside a fixed algebraic closure. Suppose one has a construction that, starting from suitable finite (possibly wildly ramified) Galois covers of smooth projective curves over the residue field, produces finite Galois extensions $L/K$ whose Galois groups $G = \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ realize prescribed finite groups as monodromy groups, together with control over the ramification filtration (in particular the higher ramification groups in upper numbering) at the closed point.

The problem is the following: Given a number field $k$ and a place $v$ of $k$, together with a finite group $G$ and a prescribed conjugacy-invariant datum $\mathcal{R}$ describing the desired local ramification behaviour at $v$ (e.g. inertia subgroup, wild inertia, jumps in the upper-numbering filtration), determine whether the curve-cover monodromy construction described above can be used to produce a finite Galois extension $M/k$ with $\mathrm{Gal}(M/k) \cong G$ whose decomposition/inertia data at $v$ realize $\mathcal{R}$. Equivalently: can such wild-monodromy constructions be applied to the classical inverse Galois problem to yield Galois extensions of a global field with a specified type of ramification at a specified place?

The inverse Galois problem with prescribed local ramification (especially wild ramification) at specified places remains an active and largely open area. For a finite set S of points in the Euclidean plane, define the dilation of S as follows. Consider all plane (i.e., crossing-free) straight-line graphs G whose vertex set consists of S together with finitely many additional Steiner points in the plane. For such a graph G, let
  d_G(p,q) = (length of a shortest path in G from p to q),
and define the spanning ratio of G on S by
  sr_S(G) = sup_{p ≠ q ∈ S}  d_G(p,q) / |pq|,
where |pq| denotes Euclidean distance. The dilation of S is then
  Δ(S) = inf_G sr_S(G),
where the infimum is taken over all such plane graphs G with finitely many Steiner points.

Determine the smallest real number t such that Δ(S) ≤ t for every finite set S of points in the plane. Equivalently, compute
  t* = sup_S Δ(S),
where the supremum is over all finite planar point sets S. (It is known that 1.00157 ≤ t* ≤ 1.1247; close the gap.)

Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, and let $X_K$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over $K$ of genus $g\ge 2$. Assume that $X_K$ admits a stable model $X$ over the ring of integers $O_L$ of a finite Galois extension $L/K$, with special fiber $X_k$ (a stable curve over $k$). The Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ (the finite monodromy group of the stable reduction) acts on $X_L:=X_K\otimes_K L$ as a group of $K$-automorphisms, and this action extends to an action on $X$ whose induced action on the special fiber gives a faithful homomorphism
$$\iota:\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)\hookrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}_k(X_k).$$
Both groups carry natural ramification filtrations: $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ has the higher ramification filtration $(G^u)_{u\ge -1}$ (in upper or lower numbering) coming from the local field extension $L/K$, while $\mathrm{Aut}_k(X_k)$ has a ramification filtration arising from the action on the local rings at the singular points and the geometry of the components of $X_k$ in characteristic $p$.

Determine the precise relationship between these two ramification filtrations under the injection $\iota$. In particular, describe how the jumps and successive quotients of the ramification filtration on $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ are reflected in the filtration on its image inside $\mathrm{Aut}_k(X_k)$.

(i) a discrete valuation ring $R$ that is finite over $W(k)$ with residue field $k$;
(ii) a faithful continuous $k$-linear action $i : G \to \mathrm{Aut}_k\, k[[z]]$; and
(iii) a continuous $R$-linear action $I : G \to \mathrm{Aut}_R\, R[[Z]]$
such that $I$ reduces modulo the maximal ideal of $R$ to $i$ (i.e., the action $I$ on $R[[Z]]$ specializes to $i$ on $k[[z]] = R[[Z]] \otimes_R k$ under a compatible choice of uniformizers).

Let P be a finite set of points in the plane. The unit-disk graph UDG(P) is the graph with vertex set P in which two points are adjacent if and only if their Euclidean distance is at most 1; assume UDG(P) is connected. A subgraph H of UDG(P) is called a plane spanner if H is planar (its straight-line embedding has no crossing edges) and there exists a constant t ≥ 1 such that for every pair u,v ∈ P, the length of a shortest path from u to v in H (sum of Euclidean edge lengths) is at most t times the length of a shortest path between u and v in UDG(P).

Consider the distributed model in which each node of UDG(P) is an autonomous processor that knows only its own coordinates and can communicate by local broadcast to all neighbors within unit distance. A distributed algorithm is called local if every node decides which of its incident edges belong to H using only information gathered from a constant-size neighborhood (e.g., its k-hop neighborhood for some constant k). The message complexity is the total number of broadcast messages exchanged during the execution of the algorithm.

Problem: Design a local distributed algorithm that, given a connected UDG(P) on n nodes, computes a plane spanner of UDG(P) using strictly fewer total broadcast messages than the previously known bound (e.g., better than the current best known O(n)-broadcast algorithms with their explicit constants), and determine the minimum achievable message complexity for this task.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $A$ be an abelian variety over $k$ of dimension $g$. An algebraic curve $C$ over $k$ (smooth, projective, and geometrically connected) gives rise to its Jacobian variety $J(C)$, an abelian variety of dimension equal to the genus of $C$. Two abelian varieties $B_1, B_2$ over $k$ are said to be isogenous if there exists a surjective homomorphism $B_1 \to B_2$ with finite kernel.

Question: For which abelian varieties $A$ over $k$ does there exist an algebraic curve $C$ over $k$ such that $A$ is isogenous to $J(C)$? In particular, given $g \geq 4$, is every abelian variety of dimension $g$ isogenous to a Jacobian, or are there abelian varieties not isogenous to any Jacobian?

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Over $\mathbb{C}$, a countability argument shows that for $g \geq 4$ not every abelian variety is isogenous to a Jacobian. Over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, Chai–Oort (2012, conditional on André–Oort) and Tsimerman (2012, unconditional) showed that there exist abelian varieties not isogenous to any Jacobian, and more recent work has extended this to Hodge-generic examples. The related Coleman–Oort conjecture, predicting that for $g\geq 8$ no positive-dimensional special subvariety of $\mathcal{A}_g$ is generically contained in the Torelli locus, remains open. A complete characterization of which abelian varieties are isogenous to Jacobians is not known.

Consider a single-server queue with finite buffer of size K (a GI/G/1/K queue): customers arrive according to a renewal process with i.i.d. inter-arrival times having mean 1/λ and squared coefficient of variation c_a^2; service times are i.i.d., independent of the arrivals, with mean 1/μ and squared coefficient of variation c_s^2. Customers arriving to a full system (K customers present, including the one in service) are lost. The queue is taken to be critically loaded, meaning λ = μ. Let D(t) denote the number of service completions (departures) in [0, t] in steady state, and define the asymptotic variance rate

   V_K := lim_{t → ∞} Var(D(t)) / t,

and the normalized quantity γ*_K := V_K / (the corresponding service rate). The BRAVO (Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Output) conjecture for this model asserts that, as K → ∞,

   γ*_K = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K).

This conjecture has been formulated under the assumption that the inter-arrival and service distributions possess finite exponential moments (light-tail condition). Determine the minimal moment / tail conditions on the inter-arrival and service-time distributions under which the above asymptotic formula γ*_K = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) holds. In particular, identify a sharp moment hypothesis (e.g., a finite p-th moment for some specific p) replacing the exponential-moment assumption.

Fix a prime number p. For a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve X of genus g ≥ 2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, let Aut(X) denote its automorphism group. Suppose there exists a polynomial M_p(T) ∈ ℝ[T] with the following property: for every such curve X of genus g, one has |Aut(X)| ≤ M_p(g), and this bound is sharp in a natural sense (for example, attained or asymptotically attained by some family of curves of unbounded genus).

Assuming such a polynomial M_p(T) exists for every prime p, answer the following:

(a) Is M_p(T) independent of the prime p, i.e., does there exist a single polynomial M(T) ∈ ℝ[T] such that M_p(T) = M(T) for all primes p?

(b) Is this polynomial equal to 8(T + 1)?

representations.normalized:
Let $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be an open set and $T>0$. Recall the following function spaces of weakly differentiable vector fields $b:(0,T)\times \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^d$:

- $BV$: vector fields whose distributional gradient $Db$ is representable by a (matrix-valued) finite Radon measure.
- $LD$ (functions of locally bounded deformation): vector fields whose symmetric distributional gradient $\tfrac{1}{2}(Db + (Db)^{T})$ lies in $L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$.
- $BD$ (functions of bounded deformation): vector fields $b$ such that the symmetric distributional derivative $Eb := \tfrac{1}{2}(Db + (Db)^{T})$ is representable by a finite Radon measure with values in the symmetric $d\times d$ matrices.

For a Borel vector field $b$ with bounded divergence, a regular Lagrangian flow is a Borel map $X:[0,T]\times \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^d$ such that, for $\mathcal{L}^d$-a.e. $x$, $t\mapsto X(t,x)$ is an absolutely continuous integral solution of $\dot{X}(t,x) = b(t,X(t,x))$ with $X(0,x)=x$, and such that $X(t,\cdot)_{\#}\mathcal{L}^d \le C\,\mathcal{L}^d$ uniformly in $t\in[0,T]$. The associated continuity equation is
$$\partial_t \rho + \mathrm{div}(b\,\rho) = 0, \qquad \rho(0,\cdot)=\rho_0.$$

The DiPerna–Lions–Ambrosio theory establishes existence and uniqueness of the regular Lagrangian flow and well-posedness of the continuity equation in the class of bounded densities under $BV$ regularity of $b$ (with bounded divergence), as well as under $LD$-type assumptions.

Question: Does this existence-and-uniqueness theory for the continuity equation and for the associated regular Lagrangian flow extend to vector fields $b$ in $BD$ with bounded divergence? That is, for every $b \in L^{1}((0,T); BD(\Omega))$ with $\mathrm{div}\, b \in L^{\infty}$ and suitable growth/boundedness assumptions, do there exist a unique regular Lagrangian flow associated with $b$ and a unique bounded weak solution of the continuity equation with prescribed bounded initial datum?

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, and let $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ denote the polynomial algebra in $n$ variables over $k$. A $k$-linear derivation $D$ of $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is called locally nilpotent if for every $f \in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ there exists a positive integer $m$ (depending on $f$) such that $D^m(f) = 0$. For any locally nilpotent derivation $D$, the formal exponential
$$\exp(tD) = \sum_{m\ge 0} \frac{t^m D^m}{m!}$$
defines, for each $t \in k$, an automorphism of $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, and $\{\exp(tD) \mid t \in k\}$ is a one-parameter subgroup of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}_k(k[x_1,\dots,x_n])$, which carries its natural ind-group structure (so that "closed subgroup" and "finite-dimensional subgroup" are well-defined notions).

Let $P$ and $Q$ be two locally nilpotent derivations of $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, and let $G(P,Q)$ denote the minimal closed subgroup of $\mathrm{Aut}_k(k[x_1,\dots,x_n])$ containing the two one-parameter subgroups $\{\exp(tP) \mid t \in k\}$ and $\{\exp(tQ) \mid t \in k\}$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(P,Q)$ under which $G(P,Q)$ is finite-dimensional.

For a finite set B of permutation patterns, let Av(B) denote the class of permutations that avoid every pattern in B (i.e., contain no subsequence order-isomorphic to any element of B), and let s_n(B) denote the number of permutations of {1,2,...,n} in Av(B). A sequence (a_n)_{n≥0} of integers is called P-recursive (polynomially recursive) if there exist a positive integer k and polynomials p_0(x), p_1(x), ..., p_k(x), with p_k not identically zero, such that
    p_k(n) a_{n+k} + p_{k-1}(n) a_{n+k-1} + ... + p_0(n) a_n = 0
for all sufficiently large n. The Noonan–Zeilberger conjecture asserts that for every finite set B of permutation patterns, the sequence s_n(B) is P-recursive.

Prove or disprove: the sequence s_n(1324), counting permutations of length n that avoid the pattern 1324, is not P-recursive (and hence the Noonan–Zeilberger conjecture is false in this specific case).

For a finite set B of permutation patterns, let Av(B) denote the class of permutations that avoid every pattern in B (i.e., contain no subsequence order-isomorphic to any element of B), and let s_n(B) denote the number of permutations of {1,2,...,n} in Av(B). A sequence (a_n)_{n≥0} of integers is called P-recursive (polynomially recursive) if there exist a positive integer k and polynomials p_0(x), p_1(x), ..., p_k(x), with p_k not identically zero, such that
    p_k(n) a_{n+k} + p_{k-1}(n) a_{n+k-1} + ... + p_0(n) a_n = 0
for all sufficiently large n. The Noonan–Zeilberger conjecture asserts that for every finite set B of permutation patterns, the sequence s_n(B) is P-recursive.

Prove or disprove: the sequence s_n(1324), counting permutations of length n that avoid the pattern 1324, is not P-recursive (and hence the Noonan–Zeilberger conjecture is false in this specific case).

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The status of s_n(1324) itself remains open: it is still unknown whether the sequence counting 1324-avoiding permutations is P-recursive. However, the broader Noonan–Zeilberger conjecture has been disproved by Garrabrant and Pak ("Pattern Avoidance is Not P-Recursive"), who exhibited a finite set of patterns whose avoidance counting sequence is not P-recursive. The specific case of 1324 conjectured by Zeilberger is therefore partially resolved (the overarching conjecture is false, but the 1324 question itself is unresolved).

Let $d \ge 1$ and let $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ denote the space of Borel probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$, equipped with its natural Polish topology. Let $\mathcal{M}_+(\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ denote the set of nonnegative finite Borel measures on $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. For $\nu \in \mathcal{M}_+(\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d))$, define its expectation $\mathbb{E}\nu \in \mathcal{M}_+(\mathbb{R}^d)$ by
$$\mathbb{E}\nu(A) := \int_{\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)} \mu(A)\, d\nu(\mu), \qquad A \subset \mathbb{R}^d \text{ Borel}.$$
Call $\nu$ regular if $\mathbb{E}\nu \le C \mathcal{L}^d$ for some constant $C \ge 0$, where $\mathcal{L}^d$ denotes Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$.

Fix a Borel time-dependent vector field $b:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$. An $\mathcal{L}^d$-regular Lagrangian flow (RLF) for $b$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a Borel map $X:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ such that:
(i) for $\mathcal{L}^d$-a.e. $x$, $t\mapsto X(t,x)$ is an absolutely continuous integral solution of $\dot\gamma(t)=b(t,\gamma(t))$ with $\gamma(0)=x$; and
(ii) there is $L\ge 0$ with $X(t,\cdot)_\#\mathcal{L}^d \le L\,\mathcal{L}^d$ for every $t\in[0,T]$.

Lift $b$ to a vector field $B$ on $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ (in the sense used in continuity-equation theory on Wasserstein space). A $\nu$-regular Lagrangian flow for $B$ in $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ is a Borel map $\boldsymbol{\mu}:[0,T]\times\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)\to\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ such that:
(i') for $\nu$-a.e. $\mu$, $t\mapsto\boldsymbol{\mu}(t,\mu)$ is an integral curve of $B$ starting at $\mu$; and
(ii') $\boldsymbol{\mu}(t,\cdot)_\#\nu$ is regular with a uniform bound in $t$.

Given an $\mathcal{L}^d$-RLF $X$, one induces a flow on $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ by
$$\boldsymbol{\mu}(t,\mu) := \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\delta_{X(t,x)}\,d\mu(x). \qquad (*)$$

Question: Does there exist a regular $\nu$ and a $\nu$-regular Lagrangian flow $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ in $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ that is not of the form $(*)$ for any $\mathcal{L}^d$-regular Lagrangian flow $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$?

Inverse cohomological realization problem. Fix a base field k (for definiteness, take k to be a number field or its algebraic closure) and a Weil cohomology theory H^*(-) for smooth projective varieties over k (e.g., ℓ-adic étale cohomology, Betti cohomology if k ⊂ ℂ, or de Rham cohomology), so that for every smooth projective variety Y/k and every integer i ≥ 0 the group H^i(Y) is endowed with its natural additional structure (Galois action, Hodge structure, Frobenius action, etc.).

Suppose one is given an abstract object V of the appropriate target category (a Galois representation, a polarizable pure Hodge structure, an isocrystal, or more generally a candidate "pure motive" with prescribed weights, Hodge numbers, L-function, and symmetry group). Determine necessary and sufficient conditions under which there exists a smooth projective variety Y/k and an integer i such that V occurs as a direct summand (cut out by an idempotent algebraic correspondence) of H^i(Y) compatibly with all the natural structures.

Equivalently: characterize which objects of the target category lie in the essential image of the realization functor from the category of Chow (or numerical) motives over k, and, given such an object V, exhibit an explicit Y realizing it.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The inverse realization problem for motives — characterizing which Galois representations, Hodge structures, or motivic data come from the cohomology of an algebraic variety — is a central, broadly open problem in algebraic geometry related to the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture, the Hodge conjecture, and the Langlands program. Many special cases are known (e.g., constructions of motives attached to certain automorphic forms), but the general inverse problem remains unresolved.

Let $F$ be a global field (a number field or the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over a finite field), and let $G$ be a connected reductive algebraic group over $F$. Consider the space $\mathcal{A}$ of (cuspidal) automorphic forms on $G(\mathbb{A}_F)\backslash G(F)$, which is expected, according to the Langlands conjectures, to decompose into spectral components ("Langlands packets" or, more refined, components indexed by Langlands parameters, i.e., by suitable homomorphisms from a Langlands-type group of $F$ into the Langlands dual group $\hat G$).

Conjecture (motivic interpretation of automorphic forms): For each spectral component $\mathcal{A}_\sigma \subset \mathcal{A}$ associated with a Langlands parameter $\sigma$ (in the case of number fields, possibly subject to an algebraicity/regularity condition on $\sigma$), there exists a smooth projective algebraic variety $Y_\sigma$ defined over $F$, an integer $i$, and an idempotent algebraic correspondence on $Y_\sigma$ cutting out a direct summand (motive) $M_\sigma$ of $H^i(Y_\sigma)$, such that $\mathcal{A}_\sigma$ is canonically realized inside the cohomology of $Y_\sigma$ via $M_\sigma$; that is, $\mathcal{A}_\sigma$ admits an "arithmetico-geometric interpretation" as a motive over $F$ in the sense of Grothendieck.

Prove this conjecture in general. Equivalently:
(a) For number fields, remove the restrictive conditions under which Shimura varieties currently realize automorphic forms motivically, and produce such a motivic realization for all (algebraic) automorphic spectral components and all reductive groups $G$, including those not of Shimura type.
(b) For function fields, upgrade the known realization of automorphic forms inside the $\ell$-adic cohomology of moduli stacks of Drinfeld shtukas to a genuinely motivic construction: produce algebraic varieties (or motives) over $F$ whose Chow/Grothendieck motives realize each spectral component $\mathcal{A}_\sigma$, independently of the prime $\ell$.

The motivic interpretation of automorphic spectral components is a widely acknowledged open problem in the Langlands program. For number fields it is known only in restricted cases via Shimura varieties (e.g., work of Langlands, Kottwitz, Harris–Taylor, Scholze, and others handles specific PEL or Hodge-type cases), and for function fields the cohomological realization via shtukas (V. Lafforgue and others) is not yet motivic. No general solution is known.

A composition of a positive integer $n$ is a finite sequence $a=(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_k)$ of positive integers with $a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_k=n$ (order matters and parts may repeat). Given a permutation $\beta=\beta_1\beta_2\cdots\beta_m$ of $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$, we say that the composition $a$ contains the pattern $\beta$ if there exist indices $i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_m$ such that the subsequence $(a_{i_1},a_{i_2},\ldots,a_{i_m})$ is order-isomorphic to $\beta$ (i.e., $a_{i_p}<a_{i_q}$ if and only if $\beta_p<\beta_q$, for all $p,q$). Otherwise, $a$ avoids $\beta$.

A sequence $(c_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of complex numbers is called P-recursive (polynomially recursive) if there exist a positive integer $d$ and polynomials $p_0(n),p_1(n),\ldots,p_d(n)\in\mathbb{C}[n]$, with $p_d$ not identically zero, such that
$$p_d(n)\,c_{n+d}+p_{d-1}(n)\,c_{n+d-1}+\cdots+p_0(n)\,c_n=0$$
for all sufficiently large $n$.

Let $c_n$ denote the number of compositions of $n$ into positive parts that avoid the pattern $123$. Prove or disprove: the sequence $(c_n)_{n\ge 1}$ is not P-recursive.
