Let $F$ be a global field (a number field or the function field of a smooth projective curve over a finite field), let $\mathbb{A}_F$ denote its ring of adeles, and let $G$ be a connected reductive group over $F$. The space of automorphic forms on $G(F)\backslash G(\mathbb{A}_F)$ (with appropriate central character) carries an action of the relevant Hecke algebra and decomposes, conjecturally according to the Langlands program, into spectral pieces indexed by Langlands (or Arthur) parameters $\psi: L_F \times \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C}) \to {}^L G$, where $L_F$ denotes the conjectural Langlands group of $F$. For each such parameter $\psi$, the corresponding spectral component appears with a certain multiplicity $m(\psi,\pi)$ for each irreducible automorphic representation $\pi$ in the associated $A$-packet $\Pi_\psi$.

The problem is to give a precise general conjectural description, and ultimately a proof, of these multiplicities. Concretely:

(a) Formulate, for an arbitrary connected reductive group $G$ over $F$, an explicit multiplicity formula expressing $m(\psi,\pi)$ as a sum over the component group $S_\psi = \pi_0(\mathrm{Cent}({}^L G, \mathrm{Im}\,\psi)/Z({}^L G)^{\Gamma})$ of characters built from local data (local Langlands characters $\langle \cdot, \pi_v\rangle$ on $S_\psi$) and from a global sign character $\epsilon_\psi: S_\psi \to \{\pm 1\}$.

(b) Establish this formula, including in the function-field case (where $F$ is the function field of a smooth projective curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$), for both the discrete and continuous parts of $L^2(G(F)\backslash G(\mathbb{A}_F))$.

(c) Provide a geometric or categorical interpretation of these multiplicities (for instance, in terms of sheaves on the stack of $L$-parameters or on moduli of shtukas/$G$-bundles) that makes them computable.

Let $F$ be a global field (a number field or the function field of a smooth projective curve over a finite field), with ring of adèles $\mathbb{A}_F$. Let $G$ and $H$ be connected reductive algebraic groups over $F$, and let ${}^LG$ and ${}^LH$ denote their Langlands dual $L$-groups. Suppose $\rho : {}^LH \to {}^LG$ is a homomorphism of $L$-groups (i.e., an $L$-homomorphism compatible with the projections to the Galois/Weil group of $F$).

Langlands' functoriality conjecture predicts that to every automorphic representation $\pi_H$ of $H(\mathbb{A}_F)$ there is associated a transfer, i.e., an automorphic representation $\pi_G$ of $G(\mathbb{A}_F)$ (a "functorial lift"), such that for every place $v$ of $F$ where $\pi_{H,v}$ is unramified, the Satake/Langlands parameter of $\pi_{G,v}$ is the image under $\rho$ of the Satake parameter of $\pi_{H,v}$; more generally the local $L$-parameters should be compatible with $\rho$ at all places.

The problem is twofold:

(a) Prove this functoriality conjecture in full generality: for every choice of $F$, $G$, $H$, and $\rho$ as above, establish the existence of the predicted automorphic transfers from $H$ to $G$ along $\rho$, with the required local compatibilities at every place.

(b) Provide a conceptual explanation of this transfer as a "quantization" procedure: namely, construct a uniform mechanism that, given the datum $\rho : {}^LH \to {}^LG$, produces the transfer $\pi_H \rightsquigarrow \pi_G$, by analogy with the passage from classical to quantum mechanics, in such a way that the existence and properties of the transfer become structurally transparent rather than established only case-by-case.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The Langlands functoriality conjecture remains one of the central open problems in number theory and representation theory. Many important special cases have been established (e.g., cyclic base change by Arthur–Clozel, endoscopic transfer and the fundamental lemma by Ngô, symmetric power lifts for GL(2) by Kim–Shahidi and recent work by Newton–Thorne for all symmetric powers over totally real fields, and broad results in the function-field case via V. Lafforgue and others), but the general conjecture, and especially a conceptual "quantization-style" mechanism explaining functoriality, is not known.

Let S_n denote the set of permutations of {1,2,…,n}. A permutation σ ∈ S_n is said to contain a permutation τ ∈ S_k as a pattern if there exist indices 1 ≤ i_1 < i_2 < … < i_k ≤ n such that the values σ(i_1), σ(i_2), …, σ(i_k) appear in the same relative order as τ(1), τ(2), …, τ(k); otherwise σ avoids τ. For a permutation τ, write s_n(τ) for the number of permutations in S_n that avoid τ.

Given a permutation π of length k and permutations σ_1, σ_2, …, σ_k of arbitrary lengths m_1, m_2, …, m_k, the inflation π[σ_1, σ_2, …, σ_k] is the permutation of length m_1 + m_2 + … + m_k obtained as follows: partition the positions {1,2,…, m_1 + … + m_k} into k consecutive blocks B_1, B_2, …, B_k of sizes m_1, m_2, …, m_k respectively; fill block B_i with values forming a sub-permutation order-isomorphic to σ_i; and choose the value ranges of the blocks so that the relative order of the blocks (as wholes) is order-isomorphic to π.

For t ≥ 2 let 12…t denote the increasing permutation (1,2,…,t) and t…21 the decreasing permutation (t, t-1, …, 1).

Prove or disprove the following statements:

(1) For all permutations σ_1, σ_2, σ_3 and every positive integer n,
   s_n(132[σ_1, σ_2, σ_3]) < s_n(123[σ_1, σ_2, σ_3]).

(2) For all permutations σ_1, σ_2, σ_3 and every positive integer n,
   s_n(312[σ_1, σ_2, σ_3]) < s_n(123[σ_1, σ_2, σ_3]).

(3) For all permutations σ_1, σ_3, every integer t ≥ 2, and every positive integer n,
   s_n(123[σ_1, 12…t, σ_3]) < s_n(123[σ_1, t…21, σ_3]).

Let $\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{-s}$ for $\Re(s) > 1$, extended by analytic continuation to a meromorphic function on $\mathbb{C}$ with a simple pole at $s=1$.

(a) (Riemann Hypothesis) Prove that every non-trivial zero of $\zeta(s)$ (i.e., every zero with $0 < \Re(s) < 1$) satisfies $\Re(s) = 1/2$.

(b) (Generalized/Automorphic Riemann Hypothesis) Let $F$ be a number field with ring of adeles $\mathbb{A}_F$, and let $\pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_F)$ with unitary central character. Let $L(s,\pi)$ denote the completed principal $L$-function attached to $\pi$, which admits meromorphic continuation to $\mathbb{C}$ and a functional equation relating $s$ to $1-s$. Prove that every zero of $L(s,\pi)$ in the critical strip $0 < \Re(s) < 1$ satisfies $\Re(s) = 1/2$.

(The function-field analogues of these statements, for $L$-functions of varieties over finite fields, were established by Deligne; the problem asks for the number-field versions.)

For a positive integer n, let S_n denote the set of permutations of [n] = {1, 2, …, n}. Given a permutation π in S_n (written in one-line notation), define a poset P_π on the ground set {1, 2, …, n} by declaring i ≼ j (for i, j ∈ [n]) if and only if i ≤ j as integers and i appears weakly before j in the one-line notation of π. For any finite ranked poset (P, ≼) with rank function r, let conv(P) denote the poset on the same ground set as P defined by i ≼_conv j iff r(i) ≤ r(j) in P. A permutation σ ∈ S_n is called layered if it can be written as a concatenation of decreasing contiguous blocks whose entry values form consecutive increasing intervals (equivalently, σ avoids both 231 and 312). For every permutation π there is a unique layered permutation, denoted conv(π), such that P_{conv(π)} is isomorphic to conv(P_π).

For a permutation τ and integer n ≥ 1, let s_n(τ) denote the number of permutations in S_n that avoid τ as a (classical) pattern, i.e., that contain no subsequence whose relative order matches τ.

Prove or disprove: for every permutation π and every positive integer n,
   s_n(π) ≤ s_n(conv(π)).

Let H be a separable complex Hilbert space and let A: D(A) ⊂ H → H be a self-adjoint infinitesimal generator of a strongly continuous semigroup {S(t)}_{t≥0} on H. Fix μ ∈ ℝ such that μI − A is positive and self-adjoint, and for α ≥ 0 define the scale of Hilbert spaces H_α = D((μI − A)^α) endowed with the graph norm ‖x‖_α = ‖(μI − A)^α x‖. Set H_{−α} to be the completion of H with respect to ‖x‖_{−α} = ‖(μI − A)^{−α} x‖, so that (H_α)* ≅ H_{−α}.

Consider the linear control system
   y'(t) = A y(t) + B u(t),  t ∈ [0, T],   y(0) = y_0,
with admissible controls u ∈ L^∞(0, T; U) (U a Hilbert space) and a bounded control operator B: U → H. For a fixed target ȳ ∈ H, an admissible control u is called norm/time optimal if it achieves ȳ at time T while minimizing the corresponding cost. To any optimal control u there is associated, via the Pontryagin maximum principle, a "multiplier" (costate) z, characterised through the dual semigroup; this z lies a priori in a space of distributions on [0,T] taking values in an extrapolation space.

Let Z(T) denote the space of admissible multipliers (those z for which the maximum principle pairing ⟨B^* S(T−t)^* z, u(t)⟩ is well defined for all admissible u), and let E* ⊂ Z(T) denote the subspace of "strongly regular" multipliers (those z for which the costate trajectory t ↦ S(T−t)^* z takes values in the dual H_{−1}^* ≅ H_1, equivalently z is associated to an element in the natural energy space).

Call an optimal control regular if its multiplier z belongs to Z(T), and strongly regular if z ∈ E*.

Question. Suppose A is self-adjoint as above. If an optimal control reaches a target ȳ with ȳ ∈ D(A), must its associated multiplier z satisfy z ∈ E*? Equivalently, in the borderline case α = 1 of the smoothness correspondence between target and costate, does regularity imply strong regularity?

Let $S_n$ denote the set of permutations of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. For permutations $\sigma\in S_n$ and $\pi\in S_k$ with $k\le n$, say that $\sigma$ contains $\pi$ as a pattern if there exist indices $1\le i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_k\le n$ such that the sequence $\sigma(i_1),\sigma(i_2),\dots,\sigma(i_k)$ has the same relative order as $\pi(1),\pi(2),\dots,\pi(k)$; otherwise $\sigma$ avoids $\pi$. For a set $B$ of permutations, let
$$\mathrm{Av}(B)=\{\sigma : \sigma\text{ avoids every pattern in }B\},$$
and write $\mathrm{Av}(B)\cap S_n$ for the permutations in $\mathrm{Av}(B)$ of length $n$. The (upper) growth rate of $\mathrm{Av}(B)$ is
$$\overline{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Av}(B))=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\bigl|\mathrm{Av}(B)\cap S_n\bigr|^{1/n}.$$
By the Marcus–Tardos theorem, this $\limsup$ is finite whenever $B\neq\emptyset$.

Question: Prove or disprove that for every finite set $B$ of permutations the limit
$$\mathrm{gr}(\mathrm{Av}(B))=\lim_{n\to\infty}\bigl|\mathrm{Av}(B)\cap S_n\bigr|^{1/n}$$
exists (as a real number).

Let $S_n$ denote the set of permutations of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. For permutations $\sigma\in S_n$ and $\pi\in S_k$ with $k\le n$, say that $\sigma$ contains $\pi$ as a pattern if there exist indices $1\le i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_k\le n$ such that the sequence $\sigma(i_1),\sigma(i_2),\dots,\sigma(i_k)$ has the same relative order as $\pi(1),\pi(2),\dots,\pi(k)$; otherwise $\sigma$ avoids $\pi$. For a set $B$ of permutations, let
$$\mathrm{Av}(B)=\{\sigma : \sigma\text{ avoids every pattern in }B\},$$
and write $\mathrm{Av}(B)\cap S_n$ for the permutations in $\mathrm{Av}(B)$ of length $n$. The (upper) growth rate of $\mathrm{Av}(B)$ is
$$\overline{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Av}(B))=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\bigl|\mathrm{Av}(B)\cap S_n\bigr|^{1/n}.$$
By the Marcus–Tardos theorem, this $\limsup$ is finite whenever $B\neq\emptyset$.

Question: Prove or disprove that for every finite set $B$ of permutations the limit
$$\mathrm{gr}(\mathrm{Av}(B))=\lim_{n\to\infty}\bigl|\mathrm{Av}(B)\cap S_n\bigr|^{1/n}$$
exists (as a real number).

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Recent literature on permutation classes (including surveys and the 2019 work of Bevan and others on growth rates up to the uncountability threshold) continues to refer to the existence of the growth rate (Stanley–Wilf limit) for general, and even finitely based, permutation classes as an open conjecture. The Marcus–Tardos theorem establishes finiteness of the upper limit, but existence of the limit itself has not been established in general.

Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. Define the greedy (West) stack-sorting operator $s : S_n \to S_n$ as follows. Given a permutation $\pi = \pi_1\pi_2\cdots\pi_n$, process its entries from left to right using a single stack. At each step, if the stack is empty or the next input entry is smaller than the current top of the stack, push the next input entry onto the stack; otherwise, pop the top of the stack and append it to the output. When the input is exhausted, pop the remaining stack entries onto the output in order. The resulting output sequence is $s(\pi)$.

For a positive integer $t$, call a permutation $\pi \in S_n$ West $t$-stack sortable if $s^t(\pi) = \mathrm{id}$, where $s^t$ denotes the $t$-fold iteration of $s$ and $\mathrm{id}$ is the identity permutation. Let $W_t(n)$ denote the number of West $t$-stack sortable permutations of length $n$.

Determine all pairs of positive integers $(t,n)$ for which $W_t(n)$ is odd.

The problem is a question of Bóna asking to characterize the parities of the counts $W_t(n)$. Recent work has examined the parity of $W_3(n)$ and used it as evidence against a related conjecture of Bóna, but no general characterization of which $(t,n)$ give odd $W_t(n)$ appears to have been established. Consider t stacks arranged in series, where t ≥ 2 is a fixed integer. The sorting machine receives an input permutation π of {1, 2, …, n} on its left, has access to t stacks S_1, S_2, …, S_t arranged left to right, and produces an output sequence on its right. At each step, exactly one of the following "legal moves" may be performed:
(i) pop the next element of the input and push it onto S_1;
(ii) for some 1 ≤ i ≤ t − 1, pop the top of S_i and push it onto S_{i+1};
(iii) pop the top of S_t and append it to the output.
The permutation π is said to be sortable by the general t-stack sorting machine if there exists some sequence of legal moves (chosen with full knowledge of π, not restricted to any greedy or deterministic policy) that processes every element of π and produces the identity 1, 2, …, n as output.

Decision problem: Given a permutation π of {1, 2, …, n} as input, decide whether π is sortable by the general t-stack sorting machine.

Determine the computational complexity of this decision problem. Specifically, is there an algorithm that solves it in time polynomial in n, or is the problem NP-complete?

The case t = 2 was resolved by Pierrot and Rossin (2014, published 2018), who showed that deciding sortability with two stacks in series can be done in polynomial time. Let $d\ge 1$ and let $\dot B_1,\dots,\dot B_d$ be independent two-dimensional white noises on $\mathbb R_+^2$; write $\widehat{\mathbf B}=(\dot B_1,\dots,\dot B_d)$. Let $b:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Borel-measurable function, and let $\sigma:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be bounded, $C^\infty$, and strongly elliptic (i.e. $\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^d}\min_i|\sigma_i(x)|>0$). Consider the system of nonlinear hyperbolic stochastic PDEs on $[0,T]^2$ with appropriate (e.g. vanishing on the axes) boundary conditions,
$$\frac{\partial^2 u_i(t,x)}{\partial t\,\partial x}=b_i(u(t,x))+\sigma_i(u(t,x))\,\dot B_i(t,x),\qquad i=1,\dots,d,$$
whose mild/Walsh solution $u:[0,T]^2\to\mathbb R^d$ is known to exist and be unique.

For a level $z\in\mathbb R^d$ define the level set $L(z)=\{(t,x)\in(0,T)^2:u(t,x)=z\}$, and for fixed $t_0$ define the slice $L_{t_0}(z)=\{x:(t_0,x)\in L(z)\}$.

Establish, for the random field $u$, the natural analogues of the following properties known for the $d$-parameter Brownian sheet $\mathbf W:\mathbb R_+^2\to\mathbb R^d$:

(a) For $d<4$, almost surely $L(z)\ne\emptyset$ for $z$ in a set of positive Lebesgue measure, while for $d\ge 4$ the level sets are a.s. empty for Lebesgue-a.e. $z$; and the Hausdorff dimension of $L(z)$, when nonempty, equals $2-d/2$.

(b) For fixed $t_0\in(0,T)$, the slice $L_{t_0}(z)$ has Hausdorff dimension $1-d/2$ when $d<2$, and is finite or empty when $d\ge 2$, with analogous capacity/hitting-probability criteria for $L_{t_0}(z)$ to be nonempty.

(c) The corresponding hitting-probability bounds (in terms of Bessel–Riesz capacities and Hausdorff measures) characterizing $P\{u(E)\cap F\ne\emptyset\}$ for compact $E\subset(0,T)^2$ and $F\subset\mathbb R^d$.

Determine whether properties (a)–(c) hold for the solution $u$.

Let $B$ be an arbitrary nontrivial real Banach space with continuous dual $B^*$, and let $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\colon B\times B^*\to\mathbb{R}$ denote the canonical duality pairing. Fix a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)$. For any two sub-$\sigma$-fields $\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{F}$, define
$$R^{B}_{\infty,\infty}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}) \;:=\; \sup\frac{\bigl|E\langle X,Y\rangle - \langle EX,EY\rangle\bigr|}{\bigl\|\,\|X\|_B\,\bigr\|_\infty\;\bigl\|\,\|Y\|_{B^*}\,\bigr\|_\infty},$$
where the supremum is taken over all simple $B$-valued random variables $X$ that are $\mathcal{A}$-measurable and all simple $B^*$-valued random variables $Y$ that are $\mathcal{B}$-measurable (with the convention $0/0=0$).

Recall the classical real-valued dependence coefficients
$$\alpha(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}) := \sup_{A\in\mathcal{A},\,B\in\mathcal{B}}|P(A\cap B)-P(A)P(B)|,$$
$$\beta(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}) := \tfrac{1}{2}\sup\sum_{i,j}|P(A_i\cap B_j)-P(A_i)P(B_j)|,$$
where the second supremum is over all finite measurable partitions $\{A_i\}\subset\mathcal{A}$ and $\{B_j\}\subset\mathcal{B}$.

Say that two families of dependence measures $D_1,D_2$ are equivalent if, uniformly over choices of probability space and pair of $\sigma$-fields, $D_1(\mathcal{A}_n,\mathcal{B}_n)\to 0$ if and only if $D_2(\mathcal{A}_n,\mathcal{B}_n)\to 0$.

Question: Is it true that for every nontrivial real Banach space $B$, the dependence measure $R^{B}_{\infty,\infty}(\cdot,\cdot)$ is equivalent (in the sense above) to either $\alpha(\cdot,\cdot)$ or $\beta(\cdot,\cdot)$?

Let $X = (X_k)_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be a strictly stationary sequence of real-valued random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, P)$ with $E[X_k^2] < \infty$. For $-\infty \le J \le L \le \infty$, let $\mathcal{F}_J^L := \sigma(X_k : J \le k \le L)$. Define the $\varphi$-mixing coefficient
$$\varphi(n) := \sup\{|P(B \mid A) - P(B)| : A \in \mathcal{F}_{-\infty}^0,\ B \in \mathcal{F}_n^\infty,\ P(A) > 0\},$$
and assume that $\varphi(n) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ (i.e., $X$ is $\varphi$-mixing). Set $S_n := X_1 + X_2 + \cdots + X_n$ and assume that $\operatorname{Var}(S_n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$.

Question: Under these hypotheses alone, must $X$ satisfy a central limit theorem? That is, must there exist constants $a_n > 0$ and $b_n \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $(S_n - b_n)/a_n$ converges in distribution to a standard normal random variable as $n \to \infty$?

This is Ibragimov's conjecture (from the 1960s) on the CLT for $\varphi$-mixing strictly stationary sequences. It remains unsolved in general. Partial results are known: Peligrad established the CLT under the additional assumption $\liminf_{n\to\infty} n^{-1}\operatorname{Var}(S_n) > 0$, and various authors have proved related theorems under additional moment or rate conditions, but the conjecture in full generality is still open.

Let X = (X_k, k ∈ Z) be a strictly stationary sequence of random variables defined on a probability space (Ω, F, P), taking values in a finite set S with |S| ≥ 2 (nondegeneracy: X_0 is not almost surely constant). For integers −∞ ≤ J ≤ L ≤ ∞, let F_J^L denote the σ-field generated by {X_k : J ≤ k ≤ L}. Define the maximal correlation coefficient

  ρ(n) := sup { |Corr(f, g)| : f ∈ L^2(F_{-∞}^0), g ∈ L^2(F_n^∞) },

and say that X is ρ-mixing if ρ(n) → 0 as n → ∞.

Define the double-tail σ-field
  T_double := ⋂_{n ≥ 1} σ( F_{-∞}^{-n} ∪ F_n^∞ ).

Say that X is bilaterally deterministic if, modulo null sets, T_double = F_{-∞}^{∞} (equivalently, the entire sequence is measurable with respect to T_double up to null sets).

Question: Does there exist a nondegenerate, strictly stationary, finite-state sequence X = (X_k, k ∈ Z) that is simultaneously ρ-mixing and bilaterally deterministic?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Known related results: Burton–Denker–Smorodinsky constructed a strictly stationary, finite-state, strongly mixing (α-mixing), bilaterally deterministic sequence, and a real-valued (non-discrete) example exists that is both ρ-mixing and bilaterally deterministic. However, no construction or impossibility proof is known for the finite-state ρ-mixing bilaterally deterministic case, and no source found indicates the question has been resolved since it was posed.

Let $(X_k)_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be a strictly stationary Markov chain on a probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, P)$. For a sub-$\sigma$-field $\mathcal{A} \subseteq \mathcal{F}$ and a sub-$\sigma$-field $\mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{F}$, define the dependence coefficients

$$\varphi(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}) = \sup\{ |P(B \mid A) - P(B)| : A \in \mathcal{A},\ B \in \mathcal{B},\ P(A) > 0\},$$

$$\rho(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}) = \sup\{ |\mathrm{Corr}(f, g)| : f \in L^2(\mathcal{A}),\ g \in L^2(\mathcal{B})\}.$$

For each $n \geq 1$, set
$$\varphi(n) = \sup_{j \in \mathbb{Z}} \varphi\big(\sigma(X_k : k \leq j),\ \sigma(X_k : k \geq j+n)\big),$$
and let the interlaced maximal-correlation coefficient be
$$\rho^*(n) = \sup\{ \rho(\sigma(X_k : k \in S),\ \sigma(X_k : k \in T)) \},$$
where the supremum is over all pairs of nonempty disjoint subsets $S, T \subset \mathbb{Z}$ satisfying $\mathrm{dist}(S, T) := \min\{|s - t| : s \in S,\ t \in T\} \geq n$.

The chain is said to be $\varphi$-mixing if $\varphi(n) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, and $\rho^*$-mixing if $\rho^*(n) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.

Question: Must every strictly stationary $\varphi$-mixing Markov chain be $\rho^*$-mixing?

Let $X = (X_k)_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be a stationary, mean-zero, real-valued Gaussian sequence with covariance function $\gamma(k) = \mathbb{E}[X_0 X_k]$, and assume that $X$ admits a spectral density $f \in L^1([-\pi,\pi])$, so that $\gamma(k) = \int_{-\pi}^{\pi} e^{ik\lambda} f(\lambda)\,d\lambda$ for all $k \in \mathbb{Z}$.

For two sub-$\sigma$-fields $\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}$ of the underlying probability space, define the maximal correlation coefficient
$$\rho(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}) := \sup\{ |\mathrm{Corr}(U,V)| : U \in L^2(\mathcal{A}),\ V \in L^2(\mathcal{B})\}.$$

For each $n \geq 1$ define
$$\rho^*(n) := \sup \rho\!\left( \sigma(X_k : k \in S),\ \sigma(X_k : k \in T) \right),$$
where the supremum is taken over all pairs of nonempty finite subsets $S, T \subset \mathbb{Z}$ such that $\min_{s\in S,\, t\in T} |s-t| \geq n$.

The sequence $X$ is said to be $\rho^*$-mixing if $\rho^*(n) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.

Find a necessary and sufficient condition, expressed directly in terms of the spectral density $f$, for the stationary Gaussian sequence $X$ to be $\rho^*$-mixing.

Let Γ be a group. Define the true prosoluble completion PS(Γ) of Γ as the inverse limit of the inverse system of all soluble quotients of Γ (equivalently, the inverse limit of Γ/N as N ranges over the normal subgroups of Γ with Γ/N soluble). A group Γ is called residually soluble if the natural map Γ → PS(Γ) is injective, equivalently if the intersection of all normal subgroups N ⊴ Γ with Γ/N soluble is trivial.

Any homomorphism ψ: Γ → Δ between groups induces a continuous homomorphism PS(ψ): PS(Γ) → PS(Δ) of topological groups.

Problem. Suppose Γ and Δ are residually soluble groups and ψ: Γ → Δ is a homomorphism such that PS(ψ): PS(Γ) → PS(Δ) is an isomorphism of topological groups.

(a) Must ψ itself be an isomorphism? If not, exhibit pairs (Γ, Δ, ψ) for which PS(ψ) is an isomorphism but ψ is not, and quantify how far ψ can be from an isomorphism.

(b) Under what additional hypotheses on Γ and Δ — for instance, finite generation, finite presentation, or further finiteness/structural properties — does the assumption that PS(ψ) is an isomorphism force ψ to be an isomorphism?

Let Γ denote the first Grigorchuk group, that is, the group generated by the four automorphisms a, b, c, d of the infinite rooted binary tree defined by Grigorchuk; Γ is infinite, residually a finite 2-group, and every proper quotient of Γ is a finite 2-group. Let PF(Γ) denote the profinite completion of Γ, so that Γ embeds densely in PF(Γ). A subgroup H of PF(Γ) is said to have the congruence subgroup property if every finite-index subgroup of H contains the closure (in PF(Γ)) of some level stabilizer St_Γ(n), where St_Γ(n) is the subgroup of Γ fixing the n-th level of the binary tree pointwise.

Question: Does there exist an element g ∈ PF(Γ) ∖ Γ such that the (abstract) subgroup Δ := ⟨Γ, g⟩ ≤ PF(Γ) generated by Γ together with g has the congruence subgroup property?

(Equivalently, exhibit such a g, thereby producing an inclusion ψ : Γ ↪ Δ which is not an isomorphism but for which the induced homomorphism PF(ψ) : PF(Γ) → PF(Δ) of profinite completions is an isomorphism.)

Specify which conventions (e.g., constructions from arithmetic, set theory, logic, two-dimensional pictorial rasters, periodic-table references, or progressively built-up formal languages such as Lincos) are to be used, and prove or argue that under reasonable assumptions about the recipient's mathematical and physical knowledge the message is uniquely interpretable.

Provide a complete description of such a system, together with criteria by which its detectability and decodability can be evaluated.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The general problem of designing a self-explanatory interstellar message remains an active, unresolved area of research. Concrete proposals (Freudenthal's Lincos, the Arecibo message, Dutil–Dumas Cosmic Call messages, Ouspensky-style "Lingua Cosmica" updates, and various algorithmic-information approaches) all exist, but none is recognized as a definitive solution; debates continue in the SETI/METI literature about how to guarantee detectability and unambiguous decodability without shared context.

Let Γ be a discrete (abstract) group. Define the following three completions of Γ:

(i) The profinite completion PF(Γ) is the inverse limit of the finite quotients Γ/N, where N runs over the normal subgroups of finite index in Γ.

(ii) The prosoluble completion PS(Γ) is the inverse limit of the soluble quotients Γ/N, where N runs over the normal subgroups of Γ for which Γ/N is soluble.

(iii) The profinite soluble (finite-soluble) completion PFS(Γ) is the inverse limit of the finite soluble quotients Γ/N, where N runs over the normal subgroups of finite index in Γ such that Γ/N is soluble.

There are canonical homomorphisms Γ → PF(Γ), Γ → PS(Γ), and Γ → PFS(Γ). The map Γ → PF(Γ) is injective iff Γ is residually finite; the map Γ → PS(Γ) is injective iff Γ is residually soluble.

Question: Does there exist a discrete group Γ that is simultaneously residually finite and residually soluble (so both Γ → PF(Γ) and Γ → PS(Γ) are injective), yet such that the canonical homomorphism Γ → PFS(Γ) fails to be injective?

Let $\Lambda=(\lambda_n)_{n=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers with $0=\lambda_0<\lambda_n<\lambda_{n+1}\to\infty$. For a real number $a$, let $\Pi_a=\{z=\sigma+it\in\mathbb{C}:\sigma<a\}$ and let $S_a(\Lambda)$ denote the class of Dirichlet series
$$F(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n e^{z\lambda_n}$$
which converge absolutely in $\Pi_a$. For such $F$, define the maximum modulus and the maximal term
$$M(x,F)=\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|F(x+it)|, \qquad \mu(x,F)=\max_{n\ge 0}|a_n|e^{x\lambda_n}.$$
Let $L$ denote the class of positive continuous functions $\psi$ on $[0,\infty)$ which are nondecreasing to $+\infty$, and let $L_0\subset L$ consist of those $\psi$ for which $\psi(x)/x\to 0$. For $\psi\in L$, set
$$S_\psi(\Lambda)=\{F\in S_0(\Lambda):\ \ln\mu(x,F)\le \psi(x)\ \text{for all sufficiently large } x<0\ \text{(in the appropriate variable)}\}$$
and consider $S^0(\Lambda)$, the class of Dirichlet series of the above form that converge absolutely in the half-plane $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} z<0\}$.

Two known results for the classes $S_\psi(\Lambda)$ assert:

(A) Under appropriate growth conditions on $\psi\in L$ and $h\in L_0$ relating $\Lambda$ and $\psi$, one has the equivalence: for every $F\in S_\psi(\Lambda)$ there exists $x_0$ such that for all $x\ge x_0$,
$$M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\,h(\ln\mu(x,F)).$$

(B) Under analogous conditions, one has the stronger statement: for every $d\in L_0$ and every $F\in S_\psi(\Lambda)$ there exists $x_0$ such that for all $x\ge x_0$,
$$M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\,h(x\,d(x)).$$

The problem is: formulate and prove an analogue of (A) or (B) for the class $S^0(\Lambda)$. Specifically, identify hypotheses on $\Lambda$ and on auxiliary functions $h$ (and possibly $d$) under which, for every $F\in S^0(\Lambda)$, a no-exceptional-set upper bound of the form
$$M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\,h(\ln\mu(x,F)) \quad\text{or}\quad M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\,h(x\,d(x))$$
holds for all $x$ sufficiently close to $0$ from the left (i.e. as $x\to 0^-$).

Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma>-1$ and consider the weight $w(x)=|x|^{\gamma}(1-x)^{\alpha}(1+x)^{\beta}$ on $[-1,1]$. For each positive integer $n$, let $p_{2n}$ denote the monic polynomial of degree $2n$ characterized by the multiple orthogonality conditions
$$\int_{-1}^{0} p_{2n}(x)\,x^{k}\,w(x)\,dx = 0, \qquad \int_{0}^{1} p_{2n}(x)\,x^{k}\,w(x)\,dx = 0, \qquad k=0,1,\dots,n-1.$$
Assume the real case in which $p_{2n}$ has exactly $n$ simple zeros in $(-1,0)$ and exactly $n$ simple zeros in $(0,1)$; denote these zero sets by $X^{-}=\{x_1^{-},\dots,x_n^{-}\}\subset(-1,0)$ and $X^{+}=\{x_1^{+},\dots,x_n^{+}\}\subset(0,1)$.

Consider the following electrostatic model. Place fixed external charges $\alpha/2$ at $1$, $\beta/2$ at $-1$, and $\gamma/2$ at $0$, and assume all free charges interact via the planar logarithmic potential ($U(z,w)=-\log|z-w|$). Place $n$ free positive unit charges $y_1,\dots,y_n\in(0,1)$ and $n$ free positive unit charges $z_1,\dots,z_n\in(-1,0)$. Additionally, regard each unit charge in one subinterval as exerting an attenuated influence on the other subinterval: from the perspective of the charges in $(0,1)$, each of the $n$ charges in $(-1,0)$ contributes with weight $1/2$, and symmetrically for the charges in $(-1,0)$.

Determine whether there exists a precise formulation of this two-component electrostatic problem under which the equilibrium configuration of the two systems of $n$ unit charges (minimizing the corresponding total energy on $(-1,0)$ and $(0,1)$) coincides with the zero sets $X^{-}$ and $X^{+}$ of $p_{2n}$ for every $n$.

Consider the Freud weight $w(x)=e^{-x^4}$ on $\mathbb{R}$, perturbed by a point mass $\lambda>0$ at the origin; that is, work with the measure $d\mu(x)=e^{-x^4}\,dx+\lambda\,\delta_0$. Let $\{p_n\}$ be the sequence of monic polynomials orthogonal with respect to $\mu$, and for fixed $n$ let $X^*=(x_1^*,\dots,x_n^*)$ denote the zeros of $p_n$ (assumed real and simple).

For a configuration $X=(x_1,\dots,x_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ of $n$ unit charges, define the total energy
$$E(X)\;=\;-\sum_{1\le j<k\le n}\log|x_j-x_k|\;+\;\sum_{k=1}^{n}\Big(\tfrac{1}{2}x_k^4-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\log\frac{x_k^2}{x_k^2+c}\Big)\quad\text{(or the analogous external field arising from }w\text{ and the point mass at }0\text{),}$$
so that $E$ is the standard logarithmic energy of $n$ unit charges in the external field generated by the perturbed weight. It is known that $X^*$ is a critical point of $E$, i.e.\ $\nabla E(X^*)=0$.

Determine whether $X^*$ satisfies any of the following stronger equilibrium properties:

(a) (Local minimum) There exists a neighborhood $U\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ of $X^*$ such that $E(X)\ge E(X^*)$ for all $X\in U$.

(b) (Coordinatewise / Nash-type equilibrium) For every $k\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, the one-variable function
$$x_k\mapsto E(x_1^*,\dots,x_{k-1}^*,x_k,x_{k+1}^*,\dots,x_n^*)$$
attains its minimum at $x_k=x_k^*$.

Either prove that (a) or (b) holds for the zeros $X^*$ of the Freud-type polynomials $p_n$ (for all $n$, or for $n$ sufficiently large), or exhibit a counterexample.

Let G be a finite simple graph with at least four edges, and let E(G) = {e_1, ..., e_m} denote its edge set. Define the edge-deck of G to be the multiset

  D_e(G) = { G - e_i : i = 1, ..., m },

where each G - e_i is the subgraph obtained from G by deleting the edge e_i (keeping all vertices), and graphs in the multiset are considered up to isomorphism.

Say that G is edge-reconstructible if every finite simple graph H satisfying D_e(H) = D_e(G) (as multisets of isomorphism classes) is isomorphic to G.

Question: Is every finite simple graph G with at least four edges edge-reconstructible?

A graph G is called hypohamiltonian if G itself has no Hamiltonian cycle, but for every vertex v of G, the graph G − v obtained by deleting v (and all incident edges) does have a Hamiltonian cycle. A graph is planar if it can be drawn in the plane with no two edges crossing.

(a) Determine the minimum number N of vertices of a planar hypohamiltonian graph; that is, find the smallest integer N such that there exists a planar hypohamiltonian graph on N vertices.

A graph G is called hypohamiltonian if G itself has no Hamiltonian cycle, but for every vertex v of G, the graph G − v obtained by deleting v (and all incident edges) does have a Hamiltonian cycle. A graph is planar if it can be drawn in the plane with no two edges crossing.

(a) Determine the minimum number N of vertices of a planar hypohamiltonian graph; that is, find the smallest integer N such that there exists a planar hypohamiltonian graph on N vertices.

(b) Let N be the value from part (a). Decide whether, for every integer n ≥ N, there exists a planar hypohamiltonian graph on exactly n vertices, or whether there are "gaps" — values n ≥ N for which no planar hypohamiltonian graph on n vertices exists.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The exact minimum order of a planar hypohamiltonian graph is still unknown. The smallest known planar hypohamiltonian graphs have 34 vertices (Tsai, 2024/2025), improving the prior bound of 40 (Jooyandeh, McKay, Östergård, Pettersson, Zamfirescu, 2017). The best known lower bound is around 23 vertices. Existence on orders 35, 36, 39 remains open, while planar hypohamiltonian graphs are known on 34, 37, 38, 40, and all sufficiently large orders. Hence the question of the minimum and the gap structure is only partially resolved.

Setup. For a finite set of distinct points $A=\{a_0,a_1,\dots,a_p\}\subset\mathbb{C}$ (with prescribed positive masses $\alpha_0,\dots,\alpha_p>0$ for the "external field" / weights) and an integer $n\ge 1$, consider configurations $X=\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}$ of $n$ points in $\mathbb{C}\setminus A$. Define the total logarithmic energy
$$E(X)=\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}\log\frac{1}{|x_i-x_j|}+\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{k=0}^{p}\alpha_k\log\frac{1}{|x_i-a_k|}.$$
A configuration $X$ is called a discrete critical configuration if $\nabla E(X)=0$; equivalently, $X$ is the zero set of a Heine–Stieltjes polynomial associated with $A$ and the weights $\alpha_k$. The normalized counting measure of $X$ is the corresponding discrete critical measure.

A finite positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}$ with compact support is called a continuous critical measure (for the data $(A,\alpha_0,\dots,\alpha_p)$) if it is a saddle point of the weighted logarithmic energy functional in the appropriate sense — concretely, if there exists a rational function $R$ with poles only in $A$ such that, with $C^{\mu}(z)=\int\frac{d\mu(t)}{z-t}$ the Cauchy transform of $\mu$, one has $(C^{\mu}(z)-\sum_k \alpha_k/(z-a_k))^2 = R(z)$ for $z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus(\mathrm{supp}\,\mu\cup A)$ (so the support of $\mu$ lies on critical trajectories of a quadratic differential $-R(z)\,dz^2$).

Problem. Give a feasible (explicit and effectively parameterized) description of the entire multi-parameter family of continuous critical measures in this class. That is, identify the natural parameters (e.g. the free coefficients of the rational function $R$, the homology/combinatorial data of the critical graph of the quadratic differential, periods of $\sqrt{R}\,dz$, etc.) and characterize, in terms of these parameters, which choices arise as continuous critical measures, together with a constructive procedure to recover $\mu$ from the parameters.

representations.normalized:
Consider the following scheduling problem. There are $n$ jobs, all available at time $0$, to be processed nonpreemptively on a single machine. Every job has unit processing time, and each job $j \in \{1,\dots,n\}$ has an associated integer due date $d_j$. Precedence constraints are given by a directed graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ in which every vertex has indegree at most $1$ and outdegree at most $1$ (so $G$ is a disjoint union of directed chains). A feasible schedule is a permutation $\sigma : \{1,\dots,n\} \to \{1,\dots,n\}$ such that $\sigma(j) < \sigma(k)$ whenever $(j,k)$ is an arc of $G$; here $\sigma(j)$ denotes the position (equivalently, the completion time) of job $j$. The tardiness of job $j$ in schedule $\sigma$ is $\max\{0,\sigma(j) - d_j\}$, and the total tardiness is $\sum_{j=1}^{n} \max\{0, \sigma(j) - d_j\}$.

Determine the computational complexity of finding a feasible permutation $\sigma$ that minimizes the total tardiness. In particular, decide whether this problem is solvable in polynomial time or is NP-hard.

Let $(M,F)$ be a compact foliated manifold with holonomy groupoid $G$, and let $G_F^N$ denote the associated transverse groupoid (the holonomy groupoid restricted to a complete transversal, or equivalently the normal/transverse groupoid). Let $E\to M$ be a smooth Hermitian vector bundle, and let $\pi:T^*G_F^N\to G_F^N$ (or the appropriate projection to the transverse cotangent bundle) be the canonical projection. Consider the algebra $\overline{\Psi}^{0,-\infty}(M,F,E)$ obtained as the closure of the algebra of order-zero transverse pseudodifferential operators with smoothing tangential part acting on sections of $E$, in the operator norm. Let
$$\overline{\sigma}:\overline{\Psi}^{0,-\infty}(M,F,E)\;\longrightarrow\;\overline{S}^{\,0}\!\left(G_F^N,\;\mathcal{L}(\pi^*E)\otimes |TG_N|^{1/2}\right)$$
be the continuous extension of the transverse principal symbol map to these completions, where $\overline{S}^{\,0}$ denotes the corresponding closure of the symbol algebra and $|TG_N|^{1/2}$ is the half-density bundle along the units of the transverse groupoid. It is known that $\overline{\sigma}$ is always surjective, and that it is injective whenever the groupoid $G$ is amenable (so in particular non-amenability of $G$ is an obstruction to injectivity).

Determine geometric or analytic conditions on $(M,F)$, on the groupoid $G$, and/or on the bundle $E$, that are sufficient (and ideally also necessary) to guarantee that the completed transverse principal symbol map $\overline{\sigma}$ is injective.

Consider the following scheduling problem. The input is a directed acyclic graph G = (V, E) with V = {1, 2, …, n}, representing precedence constraints among n unit-time jobs. A feasible schedule is a function σ : V → ℤ_{≥1} such that:
(i) σ(j) < σ(k) whenever (j, k) ∈ E (precedence is respected), and
(ii) for every integer t ≥ 1, |{ j ∈ V : σ(j) = t }| ≤ 3 (at most three jobs share a time slot, corresponding to three identical parallel machines).
The makespan of σ is C(σ) = max_{j ∈ V} σ(j). The goal is to compute min C(σ) over all feasible schedules.

Determine the computational complexity of this optimization problem: is it solvable in polynomial time in n, or is it NP-hard?

Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a (not necessarily Riemannian) smooth foliation on $M$ of codimension $q$. Let $T\mathcal{F}\subset TM$ denote the tangent bundle to the leaves and let $H\subset TM$ be a smooth subbundle complementary to $T\mathcal{F}$, so that $TM=T\mathcal{F}\oplus H$. The Riemannian metric on $M$ induces a leafwise (tangential) Laplacian $\Delta_{\mathcal{F}}$ acting along leaves and, via the splitting, a transverse Laplacian $\Delta_H$.

Let $N^*\mathcal{F}\subset T^*M$ denote the conormal bundle to $\mathcal{F}$. The foliation $\mathcal{F}$ lifts to the linearized foliation $\mathcal{F}_N$ on $N^*\mathcal{F}$, whose leaves are given by the differential of the holonomy along the conormal directions. Let $\Delta_{\mathcal{F}_N}$ be the tangential Laplacian for $\mathcal{F}_N$ with respect to the natural metric induced on $N^*\mathcal{F}$, and let $g_N\colon N^*\mathcal{F}\to\mathbb{R}$ denote the induced fiberwise quadratic function (the squared norm in the transverse metric). Let $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal{F}_N}$ denote the noncommutative trace associated with the holonomy groupoid of $\mathcal{F}_N$ on $N^*\mathcal{F}$, applied to leafwise smoothing operators of trace-class type.

For a parameter $h>0$, consider the adiabatic-type operator $\Delta_{\mathcal{F}}+h^2\Delta_H$ acting on $L^2(M)$.

Question: Is it true that for every $f\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})$ one has the asymptotic formula
$$\operatorname{tr} f(\Delta_{\mathcal{F}}+h^2\Delta_H)=(2\pi)^{-q}h^{-q}\,\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal{F}_N} f(\Delta_{\mathcal{F}_N}+g_N)+o(h^{-q})$$
as $h\to 0^+$?

Consider the quadratic polynomial family
$$P_\alpha(z) = e^{2\pi i \alpha} z + z^2, \qquad z \in \mathbb{C},$$
where $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$. Recall that an irrational number $\alpha$ with continued fraction convergents $p_n/q_n$ is called a Brjuno (Bruno) number if
$$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{\log q_{n+1}}{q_n} < \infty.$$
By a theorem of Brjuno–Yoccoz, for every Brjuno number $\alpha$ the polynomial $P_\alpha$ is locally linearizable at the fixed point $0$; that is, there is a maximal open neighborhood $S_\alpha$ of $0$ (the Siegel disk of $P_\alpha$) on which $P_\alpha$ is conformally conjugate to the rigid rotation $z \mapsto e^{2\pi i \alpha} z$.

Question: Does there exist a Brjuno number $\alpha$ such that the boundary $\partial S_\alpha$ of the Siegel disk of $P_\alpha$ is not a Jordan curve (i.e., is not homeomorphic to a circle)?

The general question of whether Siegel disk boundaries of quadratic polynomials with Brjuno rotation number are Jordan curves remains an open problem in complex dynamics. Significant partial results exist: for quadratic polynomials with rotation number of sufficiently high type the Siegel disk is known to be a Jordan domain (Yang, 2016), and for almost all (in a measure-theoretic sense) rotation numbers the boundary is a Jordan curve equal to the closure of the critical orbit. However, no Brjuno parameter has been exhibited for which $\partial S_\alpha$ fails to be a Jordan curve, nor is such non-existence proved in general.

Let $(M, \mathcal{F})$ be a compact foliated manifold equipped with a holonomy invariant transverse Riemannian structure, and let $E \to M$ be a Hermitian vector bundle. Let $D$ be a first-order transversally elliptic, formally self-adjoint pseudodifferential operator acting on sections of $E$, and consider its associated noncommutative bicharacteristic flow $F_t$ on the cotangent bundle to the holonomy groupoid restricted to the conormal directions $G_{FN}$. The (first) noncommutative Egorov theorem asserts that, for a transverse pseudodifferential operator $K$ of order $m$ with principal symbol $k$, the operator $K(t)=e^{itD}Ke^{-itD}$ is again a transverse pseudodifferential operator of order $m$, and its principal symbol $k(t)$ depends on $k$ and $D$ in a prescribed (in general nontrivial) way. In the special case that $E$ is the trivial line bundle and that the subprincipal symbol of $D^2$ vanishes, the principal symbol evolves purely classically: $k(t) = F_t^*(k)$, where $k \in S^m(G_{FN}, |T G_N|^{1/2})$.

Problem. Extend this last identity to the case in which $E$ is an arbitrary Hermitian vector bundle. Concretely, formulate and prove the appropriate generalization of $k(t) = F_t^*(k)$ for transversally elliptic operators $D$ acting on sections of an arbitrary vector bundle $E \to M$, identifying the correct notion of subprincipal symbol vanishing, the appropriate replacement of the pullback $F_t^*$ by a parallel-transport operator along the orbits of $F_t$ associated with a connection on $E$, and the class of operators $D$ for which the resulting formula holds.

Let $n\ge 1$ and let $\mathbb{T}^n=\mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$. A vector $\alpha\in\mathbb{T}^n$ is called Diophantine if there exist constants $\gamma>0$ and $\tau>0$ such that
$$|k\cdot\alpha-m|\ge \gamma|k|^{-\tau}\qquad\text{for all }k\in\mathbb{Z}^n\setminus\{0\},\;m\in\mathbb{Z}.$$
Let $\mathrm{DC}\subset\mathbb{T}^n$ denote the set of Diophantine vectors.

For a smooth function $\varphi:\mathbb{T}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ with zero mean (i.e.\ $\int_{\mathbb{T}^n}\varphi=0$), define the exact symplectic map
$$F_\varphi:\mathbb{T}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{T}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n,\qquad F_\varphi(\theta,r)=\bigl(\theta+r,\;r+\partial_\theta\varphi(\theta+r)\bigr).$$

For $\alpha\in\mathrm{DC}$, let $U_\alpha$ be the set of smooth zero-mean $\varphi$ for which $F_\varphi$ admits a smooth invariant torus on which the restricted dynamics is smoothly conjugate to the translation $\theta\mapsto\theta+\alpha$. Set $U=\bigcup_{\alpha\in\mathrm{DC}}U_\alpha$.

Determine the smallest real number $k>0$ such that $U$ is a neighborhood of $0$ in the $C^k$ topology on smooth zero-mean functions on $\mathbb{T}^n$.

Let $(M,\mathcal{F})$ be a compact smooth manifold equipped with a Riemannian foliation $\mathcal{F}$, endowed with a bundle-like metric. Let $F_t^*$ denote the transverse geodesic flow associated with $(M,\mathcal{F})$, viewed as a flow on the (leaf space of the) conormal bundle to the foliation, and let $\Phi_t$ denote the corresponding noncommutative geodesic flow, i.e., the one-parameter group of automorphisms of (a suitable completion of) the operator algebra associated with the foliation that arises through an Egorov-type theorem for transversally elliptic operators (so that conjugation by $e^{itP}$, with $P$ a transverse Laplace-type operator of order one, induces $\Phi_t$ at the level of principal transverse symbols, which in turn corresponds to $F_t^*$ classically).

Problem. Define
(i) a classical topological entropy $h(F^*)$ for the transverse geodesic flow $F_t^*$, taking into account its non-Hausdorff/foliated nature, and
(ii) a quantum (noncommutative) topological entropy $h(\Phi)$ for the noncommutative geodesic flow $\Phi_t$ acting on the relevant operator algebra,
in such a way that one can establish meaningful relations between $h(F^*)$ and $h(\Phi)$ (for instance, an inequality, equality, or variational principle relating the two, in analogy with the classical case of geodesic flows on compact Riemannian manifolds).

Let $(M,\mathcal{F})$ be a smooth Riemannian foliation on a compact manifold $M$. Let $G_{\mathcal{F}}$ denote its holonomy groupoid and let $G_{\mathcal{F}}^N \to N$ denote the transverse (normal) groupoid associated with a complete transversal $N$, with associated tangent groupoid $TG_N$. Consider the convolution algebra $C^{\infty}_{\mathrm{prop}}(G_{\mathcal{F}}^N, |TG_N|^{1/2})$ of properly supported smooth half-densities on $G_{\mathcal{F}}^N$, which serves as a noncommutative model for the algebra of smooth functions on the cotangent bundle of the leaf space $M/\mathcal{F}$, carrying a natural Poisson structure.

Problem: Construct a strict deformation quantization of $C^{\infty}_{\mathrm{prop}}(G_{\mathcal{F}}^N, |TG_N|^{1/2})$ in the sense of Rieffel; that is, construct a continuous field $\{A_\hbar\}_{\hbar\in[0,1]}$ of $C^*$-algebras together with a dense $*$-subalgebra of sections containing the given algebra at $\hbar=0$, such that for any two elements $f,g$, the section $\hbar \mapsto f\star_\hbar g$ is continuous and satisfies
$$\Big\| \frac{f\star_\hbar g - g\star_\hbar f}{i\hbar} - \{f,g\} \Big\|_\hbar \longrightarrow 0 \quad \text{as } \hbar\to 0,$$
where $\{\cdot,\cdot\}$ is the natural Poisson bracket on the noncommutative cotangent algebra of the leaf space.

A Lagrangian torus in R^{2n} is an embedded n-dimensional submanifold on which the standard symplectic form vanishes identically.

Let f : (R^{2n}, 0) → (R^{2n}, 0) be a germ of a real-analytic symplectic diffeomorphism fixing the origin, and assume that its linear part df(0) ∈ Sp(2n,R) is symplectically conjugate to r_α for some Diophantine vector α ∈ R^n.

Question: Does it follow that, for every sufficiently small neighborhood U of 0, the union of the f-invariant Lagrangian tori contained in U has positive Lebesgue measure?

This is a version of Herman's conjecture on accumulation of an elliptic Diophantine fixed point by Lagrangian invariant tori of positive measure. Eliasson, Fayad and Krikorian (2014) proved the conjecture under the additional assumption that the Birkhoff normal form at 0 satisfies a Rüssmann transversality condition, and showed unconditional accumulation by complex-analytic KAM tori; the fully degenerate (general) case in the form stated remains not definitively settled in the literature. Garay (2012) announced a positive resolution via KAM versal deformation theory, but this is not universally regarded as a complete proof of the original conjecture.

Let $(M,\mathcal{F})$ be a smooth compact foliated manifold of codimension $q$, and let $E\to M$ be a smooth complex vector bundle. Consider the bifiltered algebra $\Psi^{*,*}(M,\mathcal{F},E)$ of (transversal) pseudodifferential operators adapted to the foliation, where the first index records the transverse order and the second index the longitudinal order. Denote by $\Psi^{-q,-\infty}(M,\mathcal{F},E)$ the class of operators of transverse order $-q$ and longitudinal order $-\infty$. On the Hilbert space $L^2(M,E)$, denote by $\mathcal{L}^{1,\infty}$ the Dixmier (weak trace) ideal, consisting of compact operators $T$ whose singular values $\mu_n(T)$ satisfy $\sum_{n\le N}\mu_n(T) = O(\log N)$, and for $T\in\mathcal{L}^{1,\infty}_+$ let $\mathrm{Tr}_\omega(T)$ denote the Dixmier trace associated with an invariant mean $\omega$ on $\ell^\infty(\mathbb{N})$. Let $\tau$ denote the residue (noncommutative residue) trace defined on $\Psi^{-q,-\infty}(M,\mathcal{F},E)$.

Prove or disprove: every $P\in\Psi^{-q,-\infty}(M,\mathcal{F},E)$ belongs to $\mathcal{L}^{1,\infty}(L^2(M,E))$, the value $\mathrm{Tr}_\omega(P)$ is independent of the choice of invariant mean $\omega$, and
$$\mathrm{Tr}_\omega(P) \;=\; \tau(P).$$

Berger and Turaev (2017, published 2019) proved Herman's positive entropy conjecture: the identity of the disk can be $C^\infty$-perturbed to an area-preserving diffeomorphism with positive metric entropy, and more generally area-preserving diffeomorphisms with positive metric entropy form a $C^\infty$-dense set near any elliptic fixed point. This rules out alternative (a) (the zero-entropy set $G$ is not dense in $\mathrm{Diff}^\infty_\mu(D^2)$). However, this does not establish alternative (b), since a nonempty $C^\infty$-open set on which entropy is uniformly bounded below by some $\delta>0$ has not been exhibited. The full dichotomy thus appears not fully resolved.

Let $D \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a bounded, simply connected planar domain with smooth boundary, and fix two distinguished boundary points that split $\partial D$ into two complementary boundary arcs $\partial^+$ and $\partial^-$. Let $h$ denote the (zero-boundary) Gaussian free field on $D$, i.e. the centered Gaussian random distribution with covariance given by the Dirichlet Green's function of $D$. Let $\{\varphi_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ be an $L^2(D)$-orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $D$ with eigenvalues $0 < \mu_1 \leq \mu_2 \leq \cdots$, so that formally $h = \sum_n \alpha_n \mu_n^{-1/2} \varphi_n$ with $\alpha_n$ i.i.d.\ standard Gaussian. For $r > 0$, define the spectral truncation
$$h_r := \sum_{n:\, \mu_n \leq r} \alpha_n \mu_n^{-1/2} \varphi_n,$$
which is a smooth random function on $D$. Let $u_\lambda$ be the bounded harmonic function on $D$ with boundary values $+\lambda$ on $\partial^+$ and $-\lambda$ on $\partial^-$, and set
$$H_r := h_r + u_\lambda.$$
The known critical constant is $\lambda = \sqrt{\pi/8}$ (with the normalization in which the GFF has covariance kernel equal to $(2\pi)^{-1}$ times the Dirichlet Green's function, or equivalently the convention for which level lines of the continuum GFF are SLE$_4$ curves).

Question: For this choice of $\lambda$, does the zero level interface of $H_r$ connecting the two distinguished boundary points converge in distribution, as $r \to \infty$, to chordal SLE$_4$ in $D$ between these points (with respect to a suitable curve topology, e.g.\ the Hausdorff distance or the metric on the space of unparametrized curves)?

The Schramm–Sheffield construction establishes convergence of zero contour lines for projections of the GFF onto piecewise-linear approximation spaces, and later work (e.g. Miller–Sheffield's imaginary geometry, and continuum level-line uniqueness results) gives many related couplings between GFF and SLE$_4$. However, the specific question about the spectral truncation (projection onto Dirichlet-Laplacian eigenfunctions with eigenvalues at most $r$) and convergence of its zero level interface to SLE$_4$ as $r \to \infty$ does not appear to be addressed in the readily available literature, and no resolution could be confirmed.

Let $M^n$ be a compact connected smooth manifold of dimension $n$, and let $f: M^n \to M^n$ be a $C^\infty$-diffeomorphism. Recall that $f$ is called:
- minimal if every orbit $\{f^k(x) : k \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ is dense in $M^n$;
- uniquely ergodic if there exists exactly one $f$-invariant Borel probability measure on $M^n$;
- strictly ergodic if it is both minimal and uniquely ergodic.

The topological entropy $h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$ is defined as
$$h_{\mathrm{top}}(f) = \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log s(n, \varepsilon),$$
where $s(n, \varepsilon)$ denotes the maximal cardinality of an $(n, \varepsilon)$-separated subset of $M^n$ with respect to any fixed Riemannian metric.

Prove or disprove: every strictly ergodic $C^\infty$-diffeomorphism $f$ of a compact connected manifold $M^n$ satisfies $h_{\mathrm{top}}(f) = 0$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The conjecture that every strictly ergodic smooth diffeomorphism of a compact manifold has zero topological entropy appears to still be open. Known related results include: uniquely ergodic homeomorphisms can have positive topological entropy (Hahn–Katznelson, Rees, Béguin–Crovisier–Le Roux); Herman constructed minimal $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms with positive entropy, but those examples are not uniquely ergodic. A separate conjecture of Herman regarding perturbations of the identity to a positive-entropy area-preserving diffeomorphism was proved by Berger and Turaev (2017–2019), but that is a different statement and does not address the strict ergodicity vs. zero entropy question.

Let $q\in(0,4)$ and consider the Fortuin–Kasteleyn random-cluster measure on a finite subgraph of the square lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$ at its self-dual point $p=\sqrt{q}/(1+\sqrt{q})$. Recall that the random-cluster measure on configurations $\omega\in\{0,1\}^{E}$ is given by
$$\mu_{p,q}(\omega)\;\propto\;\prod_{e\in E} p^{\omega(e)}(1-p)^{1-\omega(e)}\;q^{k(\omega)},$$
where $k(\omega)$ is the number of connected components of the spanning subgraph determined by the open edges $\{e:\omega(e)=1\}$.

Fix a simply connected planar domain $D$ with two distinguished prime ends $a,b$ on its boundary, and approximate $D$ by subgraphs $D_\delta$ of $\delta\mathbb{Z}^2$ with two boundary arcs separated by $a_\delta,b_\delta$. Impose Dobrushin-type boundary conditions (one arc wired, the other free), so that there is a well-defined interface $\gamma_\delta$ on the medial lattice running from $a_\delta$ to $b_\delta$ between the two boundary arcs.

Prove that, as $\delta\to 0$, the law of $\gamma_\delta$ converges weakly (with respect to a suitable curve topology) to chordal Schramm–Loewner Evolution $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ in $D$ from $a$ to $b$, with
$$\kappa \;=\; \frac{4\pi}{\arccos(-\sqrt{q}/2)}.$$

The case $q=2$ (FK-Ising), giving $\kappa=16/3$, was established by Smirnov and collaborators using discrete complex analysis (parafermionic observables). For general $q\in(0,4)\setminus\{2\}$ the convergence to SLE$_\kappa$ remains open; rigorous techniques used at $q=2$ are not known to extend, although conformal invariance and rotational invariance of certain critical observables have been proven in the random-cluster model for all $q\in[1,4)$ in recent work by Duminil-Copin and collaborators.

Let G = Z^2 be the planar square lattice, viewed as a graph with edges between nearest-neighbor vertices. A lattice tree in G is a finite connected subgraph of G that contains no cycles (equivalently, a finite subtree of G). Fix an integer n ≥ 1 and let T_n be a uniformly random lattice tree in G that contains the origin and has exactly n vertices.

(a) Determine the growth rate, as n → ∞, of the expected diameter E[diam(T_n)], where diam(T_n) is the maximum graph distance (within T_n) between two vertices of T_n.

(b) Rescale T_n by dividing all graph distances by a factor a_n chosen so that the expected (or median) diameter of the rescaled tree equals 1. Viewed as a random compact metric space (for instance with the Gromov–Hausdorff topology, or as a random embedded subset of the plane after rescaling Z^2 by a_n), does the law of the rescaled T_n converge to a limit as n → ∞?

(c) If such a scaling limit exists, describe its geometric and topological properties (e.g. Hausdorff dimension, whether it is a topological tree, its degree structure, conformal/rotational symmetries, and whether it can be identified explicitly).

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

In sufficiently high dimensions (d large, or spread-out models above the upper critical dimension 8), the scaling limit of uniform lattice trees is known to be Aldous's integrated super-Brownian excursion (ISE), confirming Aldous's conjecture. In two dimensions, however, the growth rate of the diameter of a uniformly random n-vertex lattice tree and the existence/identification of a scaling limit remain open; no proof of convergence (only conjectures of conformal invariance for related planar tree models) appears in the literature.

representations.normalized:
Consider site percolation on the triangular lattice with mesh ε > 0, restricted to the upper half-plane. Each hexagonal site is independently colored white with probability p and black with probability 1 − p. Fix a 1 × 1 square Q in the upper half-plane and let f(p, ε) denote the probability of a left-to-right white crossing of Q. Fix a value q ∈ (0, 1) with q ≠ 1/2, and for each ε > 0 choose p(ε) so that f(p(ε), ε) = q. With suitable boundary conditions placing white sites on the positive real axis and black sites on the negative real axis, there is an unbounded interface (a simple lattice path) starting at the origin and separating the two colors.

Determine the scaling limit, as ε ↓ 0, of this interface viewed as a random curve in the upper half-plane, under the near-critical tuning p = p(ε) corresponding to fixed crossing probability q ≠ 1/2. In particular, describe whether the limit exists, identify it explicitly (for example as a "massive" or otherwise perturbed variant of SLE₆), and characterize its law.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The near-critical scaling limit of 2D percolation on the triangular lattice has been substantially developed: Camia–Newman–Fontes described a conjectural framework, and Garban–Pete–Schramm (arXiv:1305.5526) constructed the scaling limit of near-critical percolation in the quad-crossing topology and showed it is invariant under translations but not under rotations/scalings, giving a "massive" deformation of the critical limit. Tuning p(ε) so that a fixed 1×1 crossing probability equals q ≠ 1/2 corresponds to a specific near-critical scale, and the corresponding interface is expected to converge to a "massive SLE₆"-type curve. While the existence and many properties of this near-critical limit are now established, an explicit, fully characterized description of the interface law as a continuum curve (analogous to SLE₆ at criticality) does not appear to have been completely achieved, so the precise problem is best classified as partially solved.

Let $M^n$ be a smooth compact oriented manifold of dimension $n$ with Euler characteristic $\chi(M^n)=0$, and let $\Omega$ be a smooth volume form on $M^n$. A smooth vector field $X$ on $M^n$ is called $\Omega$-divergence-free if the Lie derivative $\mathcal{L}_X\Omega = 0$, equivalently, the flow $f_X^t$ generated by $X$ preserves the measure induced by $\Omega$. The flow is said to be $\Omega$-ergodic if every $f_X^t$-invariant Borel set has either zero or full $\Omega$-measure.

Question: Does there exist a smooth, nowhere-vanishing, $\Omega$-divergence-free vector field $X$ on $M^n$ whose flow $f_X^t$ is $\Omega$-ergodic?

representations.normalized:
Let $\eta$ be a homogeneous Poisson point process of intensity $1$ in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, and let $\mathcal{V}(\eta) = \{V_x : x \in \eta\}$ be the associated Voronoi tessellation, where $V_x = \{y \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |y-x| \le |y-x'| \text{ for all } x' \in \eta\}$. Independently of $\eta$, color each Voronoi cell $V_x$ black with probability $1/2$ and white with probability $1/2$. This is critical planar Voronoi percolation.

For a Jordan domain $D \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with four marked boundary prime ends $a,b,c,d$ in counterclockwise order, and for $\delta > 0$, let $f_\delta(D;a,b,c,d)$ denote the probability that, in the rescaled model on $\delta\mathbb{R}^2$ (equivalently, intensity $\delta^{-2}$), there exists a black crossing in $D$ from the boundary arc $ab$ to the boundary arc $cd$.

Prove the following analogue of Smirnov's theorem (originally established for critical site percolation on the triangular lattice):

(i) (Conformal invariance / Cardy's formula.) For every such configuration $(D;a,b,c,d)$, the limit
$$f(D;a,b,c,d) = \lim_{\delta \downarrow 0} f_\delta(D;a,b,c,d)$$
exists, is conformally invariant (i.e. $f(D;a,b,c,d) = f(\varphi(D);\varphi(a),\varphi(b),\varphi(c),\varphi(d))$ for every conformal map $\varphi$ defined on a neighborhood of $\overline{D}$), and is given by Cardy's formula: writing $(D;a,b,c,d)$ as the equilateral triangle with vertices $a,b,c$ and a marked point $d$ on the side $ca$ at signed distance $u \in [0,1]$ from $c$, one has $f = u$.

(ii) (Scaling limit / SLE$_6$.) The interface of the critical Voronoi percolation model in a Jordan domain with Dobrushin boundary conditions converges in distribution, as $\delta \downarrow 0$, to chordal Schramm–Loewner Evolution with parameter $\kappa = 6$.

The problem appears to remain open. Smirnov's theorem (conformal invariance, Cardy's formula and convergence of interfaces to SLE_6) has been proved only for critical site percolation on the triangular lattice. For Voronoi percolation, Benjamini and Schramm established invariance of crossing probabilities under conformal changes of metric, and Bollobás–Riordan determined the critical probability to be 1/2, but no full Smirnov-type theorem (Cardy's formula and SLE_6 scaling limit) has been established for Voronoi percolation in the literature found.

Let $n \geq 3$ and consider the cotangent bundle $T^*\mathbb{T}^n \cong \mathbb{T}^n \times \mathbb{R}^n$ with canonical coordinates $(\theta, r)$ and the standard symplectic form $\sum_i d\theta_i \wedge dr_i$. Define the integrable Hamiltonian
$$H_0(\theta, r) = \tfrac{1}{2}\|r\|^2.$$
Fix an integer $k \geq 2$. Question: does there exist a smooth ($C^\infty$) Hamiltonian $H$ on $T^*\mathbb{T}^n$ lying in an arbitrarily small $C^k$-neighborhood of $H_0$ such that the Hamiltonian flow of $H$, restricted to the energy hypersurface $H^{-1}(1)$, possesses at least one dense orbit?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question (often attributed to Herman, 1998 ICM) appears to remain open. Partial progress was obtained by Kaloshin and Saprykina (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012), who constructed a nearly integrable Hamiltonian with an orbit dense in a set of maximal Hausdorff dimension on the unit energy surface, but not dense in the full energy surface. The full quasi-ergodic-type question with a single orbit dense in $H^{-1}(1)$ has not, to current knowledge, been resolved.

Consider critical Bernoulli site percolation on the triangular lattice in the plane (equivalently, any model in the same conformally invariant universality class). For R ≥ 1, let θ(R) denote the probability that the percolation cluster of the origin has Euclidean diameter at least R, and let π(R) denote the probability that a fixed site is pivotal for the crossing event of a box of side length R (i.e., that there exist four alternating-color arms from the site to distance R). It is known that

  θ(R) = R^{-5/48 + o(1)}  and  π(R) = R^{-5/4 + o(1)}  as R → ∞,

and analogous polynomial-with-o(1) estimates hold for other arm events (half-plane j-arm events and polychromatic j-arm events in the whole plane).

Problem: Sharpen these asymptotics. In particular, prove that θ(R) and π(R), as well as the half-plane and polychromatic j-arm probabilities, are each comparable to an explicit power of R up to multiplicative constants bounded above and below (i.e., remove the o(1) in the exponent and replace it by a quantitative power-law error or, ideally, by a true multiplicative-constant equivalence). More generally, obtain precise asymptotic formulas, including (where possible) the leading multiplicative constants.

Significant recent progress has been made. Du, Gao, Li, and collaborators (Comm. Math. Phys. 405:182, 2024; arXiv:2205.15901) establish sharp estimates (matching upper and lower bounds up to multiplicative constants, with power-law error bounds in most cases) for half-plane j-arm events for j ≥ 1 and polychromatic whole-plane j-arm events for j > 1 in critical planar percolation, explicitly answering a large part of the problem. The one-arm whole-plane case (the R^{-5/48} estimate for cluster diameter) is not fully covered by these results, so the problem is partially solved rather than fully resolved, and obtaining the exact multiplicative constants remains open.

Let $M$ be a closed (compact, boundaryless) smooth manifold and let $H \in C^\infty(T^*M, \mathbb{R})$ be a Tonelli Hamiltonian (i.e., $H$ is fiberwise strictly convex and superlinear in the momentum). Fix the energy level $\Sigma = H^{-1}(1)$ and assume it is regular and compact, and let $\varphi^t_H$ denote the Hamiltonian flow of $H$ restricted to $\Sigma$.

Recall the Mañé/Mather setting: an invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ for $\varphi^t_H$ supported in $\Sigma$ is called a minimizing measure (at energy $1$) if it minimizes the action $\int L\, d\mu'$ over all $\varphi^t_H$-invariant probability measures whose Lagrangian projection has the corresponding rotation/cohomology class, where $L$ is the Lagrangian dual to $H$. Let $\mathcal{M}_{\min}^{\mathrm{erg}}(H)$ denote the set of ergodic minimizing measures, viewed in the weak-$*$ topology on probability measures on $\Sigma$. Let $\mathcal{P}(H) \subset \mathcal{M}_{\min}^{\mathrm{erg}}(H)$ denote the subset consisting of those ergodic minimizing measures that are supported on a single periodic orbit of $\varphi^t_H$.

Question: Is it true that for a $C^\infty$-generic (i.e., residual in $C^\infty(T^*M,\mathbb{R})$) Tonelli Hamiltonian $H$, the set $\mathcal{P}(H)$ is dense in $\mathcal{M}_{\min}^{\mathrm{erg}}(H)$ with respect to the weak-$*$ topology?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question, in the spirit of Mañé's genericity program, remains open in general. Partial progress exists: Bernard showed that Mañé-generic Tonelli Hamiltonians have only non-degenerate periodic orbits on a fixed energy level, and Rifford–Ruggiero and others have proved generic properties of closed orbits from Mañé's viewpoint. Density of periodic-orbit measures in the set of ergodic minimizing measures for $C^\infty$-generic Hamiltonians has not been established; related results are known only in restricted (e.g., expanding/symbolic, hyperbolic) settings.

Consider Bernoulli bond percolation on the square lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$ at the critical parameter $p_c = 1/2$ (or, equivalently, critical site percolation on the triangular lattice). For $R > 0$, restrict attention to the box $[0,R]^2$ and consider the event $\mathcal{C}_R$ that there exists an open left-right crossing of this box (a path of open edges/sites joining the left side to the right side staying inside the box). On the event $\mathcal{C}_R$, let $L_R$ denote the (graph) length of the shortest open left-right crossing of $[0,R]^2$ — the so-called chemical distance across the box.

Determine the real number $\alpha$ such that
$$\mathbb{E}\!\left[L_R \,\big|\, \mathcal{C}_R\right] = R^{\alpha + o(1)} \qquad \text{as } R \to \infty,$$
or prove that no such exponent exists.

representations.normalized:
Consider the Newtonian spatial $n$-body problem with $n \geq 3$: point masses $m_1, \dots, m_n > 0$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with positions $q_i$ interacting via the Newtonian potential $U(q) = \sum_{i<j} m_i m_j / |q_i - q_j|$, with Hamiltonian $H(q,p) = \sum_i |p_i|^2/(2m_i) - U(q)$. Fix the center of mass at the origin and pass to the standard reduced phase space. After a smooth time reparametrization that slows time near collisions so as to extend the flow to a complete smooth flow on each energy hypersurface (replacing $H$ by an equivalent Hamiltonian $H_e$ on the level $H_e^{-1}(0)$ corresponding to the original energy $e$), one obtains a complete Hamiltonian flow on $H_e^{-1}(0)$.

Recall that a point $x$ is nonwandering for a flow $\phi^t$ if for every neighborhood $U$ of $x$ and every $T>0$ there exists $t > T$ with $\phi^t(U) \cap U \neq \emptyset$. Let $\Omega(e) \subset H_e^{-1}(0)$ denote the nonwandering set of the reparametrized flow.

Question: For every real value of the energy $e$, is $\Omega(e)$ nowhere dense in $H_e^{-1}(0)$?

The question, attributed by Herman to Birkhoff and Kolmogorov and described as one of the oldest problems on the Newtonian n-body problem, remains open. Recent surveys and works on the Painlevé conjecture and on compactification of energy surfaces of n-body problems still cite the conjecture (nonwandering set nowhere dense in every energy level) as unresolved.

representations.normalized:
Consider critical site percolation on the triangular lattice, in which each site is independently coloured black or white with probability 1/2. For a positive integer ℓ, let D_ℓ denote an approximately ℓ×ℓ square region of the triangular lattice with two designated opposite sides, and let f_ℓ : {-1,+1}^{D_ℓ} → {-1,+1} be the Boolean crossing function whose value is +1 if and only if there is a black path in D_ℓ connecting the two designated sides. Expand f_ℓ in the Fourier–Walsh basis,
   f_ℓ = Σ_{S ⊂ D_ℓ} f̂_ℓ(S) χ_S,
where χ_S(ω) = Π_{x∈S} ω(x). Define the spectral probability measure on subsets S ⊂ D_ℓ by P̂_ℓ(S) = f̂_ℓ(S)^2 (which sums to 1 because f_ℓ takes values ±1), and let μ̃_{f_ℓ} be the law of the (random) cardinality |S| under P̂_ℓ; thus μ̃_{f_ℓ} is a probability measure on {0,1,…,|D_ℓ|}.

(a) Prove or disprove: for every 0 ≤ α_1 < 3/4 < α_2,
        μ̃_{f_ℓ}([ℓ^{α_1}, ℓ^{α_2}]) → 1   as ℓ → ∞.

(b) More generally, determine the asymptotic behaviour of μ̃_{f_ℓ}([ℓ^{α_1}, ℓ^{α_2}]) as ℓ → ∞ for arbitrary 0 ≤ α_1 < α_2 ≤ 2.

The concentration question in part (a) was resolved affirmatively by Garban, Pete and Schramm in "The Fourier spectrum of critical percolation" (Acta Mathematica 205 (2010), 19–104), who proved that the spectral mass of f_ℓ concentrates on cardinalities of order ℓ^{3/4} (the conjectured pivotal/spectral exponent), giving sharp lower-tail estimates. A complete description of the asymptotic behaviour of μ̃_{f_ℓ}([ℓ^{α_1}, ℓ^{α_2}]) for all 0 ≤ α_1 < α_2 ≤ 2 (in particular near the endpoints and at finer scales than power-law concentration) does not appear to be fully established; the existence of a scaling limit of the spectral sample as a random Cantor-like set of Hausdorff dimension 3/4 has subsequently been obtained, but precise fluctuation asymptotics for the windowed mass remain partial.

Let $m\ge 1$ be an integer and let $F_m$ denote the free group on $m$ generators $x_1,\dots,x_m$. A word $w\in F_m$ is called primitive if it belongs to some free generating set of $F_m$. Let $G\le \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ be an $m$-generated linear group over a field $K$, with a fixed generating $m$-tuple $(g_1,\dots,g_m)\in G^m$. For each primitive word $w\in F_m$, let $w(g_1,\dots,g_m)\in G\subseteq \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ denote its evaluation.

Suppose there exists a nonzero polynomial $p(t)\in K[t]$ such that $p(w(g_1,\dots,g_m))=0$ in the matrix algebra $M_n(K)$ for every primitive word $w\in F_m$. Must $G$ be soluble-by-finite (i.e., contain a soluble subgroup of finite index)?

Consider dynamical critical site percolation on the triangular lattice with mesh ε > 0: each site is independently open or closed with probability 1/2, and each site independently resamples (flips with the appropriate probability to maintain the stationary Bernoulli(1/2) law) at rate λ = λ(ε), chosen so that, for a fixed square Q in the plane, the correlation between the indicator of the event {there is an open left–right crossing of Q at time 0} and the indicator of the same event at time 1 equals 1/2.

(a) Prove that as ε → 0, the scaling limit of this time-dependent random percolation configuration process exists (in an appropriate topological space of percolation configurations on the plane, e.g. the quad-crossing space).

(b) Prove that for any two times t₁ < t₂, the correlation between left–right crossing events of a fixed quad at times t₁ and t₂ tends to 0 as t₂ − t₁ → ∞.

(c) Prove that the probability that the left–right crossing indicator of a fixed quad changes between times t₁ and t₂ tends to 0 as t₂ − t₁ → 0.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

Nikolov and Segal (Annals of Mathematics, 2007, "On finitely generated profinite groups, I: strong completeness and uniform bounds") proved that in every topologically finitely generated profinite group, every subgroup of finite index is open; as a consequence the abstract subgroup G^n generated by n-th powers is closed, and the corresponding uniform bound N(m,n) on the number of n-th powers needed to express elements of K^n in finite m-generated groups K exists. This affirmatively resolves the question.

Let $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}^2/\Lambda$ be a flat torus, where $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is a rank-two lattice, and for each small $\delta > 0$ let $G_\delta$ be a fine square-grid graph that approximates $\mathbb{T}$ (the vertex set is a $\delta$-mesh on $\mathbb{T}$, and the edges connect nearest neighbors, with the grid wrapping around in accordance with $\Lambda$). Let $T_\delta$ be a uniformly chosen spanning tree of $G_\delta$. Form the dual graph $D_\delta$ on the faces of $G_\delta$ consisting of exactly those dual edges that are perpendicular to primal edges not belonging to $T_\delta$.

It is a fact that $D_\delta$ contains precisely three edge-simple closed paths $\gamma_1^\delta, \gamma_2^\delta, \gamma_3^\delta$ (paths with no repeated edges), and that each of these paths is non-null-homotopic in $\mathbb{T}$. Each $\gamma_i^\delta$ therefore represents a nonzero element $[\gamma_i^\delta] \in \pi_1(\mathbb{T}) \cong \mathbb{Z}^2$ (up to inversion and choice of basepoint), and we set this triple of free-homotopy classes as $\bigl([\gamma_1^\delta],[\gamma_2^\delta],[\gamma_3^\delta]\bigr)$, viewed as an unordered triple of primitive elements of $H_1(\mathbb{T};\mathbb{Z})/\{\pm 1\}$.

Determine, as $\delta \to 0$, the joint distribution of the (unordered) triple of homotopy classes $\bigl([\gamma_1^\delta],[\gamma_2^\delta],[\gamma_3^\delta]\bigr)$, expressed explicitly as a function of the conformal/geometric shape of the torus $\mathbb{T}$ (i.e., its modular parameter).

Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold (without boundary), and let $\Delta_g$ denote the (non-negative) Laplace–Beltrami operator acting on smooth functions on $M$. It is classical that the spectrum of $\Delta_g$ consists of a discrete sequence
$$0 = \lambda_0 < \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \lambda_3 \le \cdots \to \infty$$
of eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity), each of finite multiplicity.

Problem. Find necessary and sufficient conditions on a discrete subset (or sequence) $S \subset \mathbb{R}^+$ that characterize when $S$ arises as the Laplace spectrum of some smooth compact Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$. In other words, give an intrinsic characterization (in terms of the sequence $S$ alone, without reference to a manifold) of those discrete sets of positive real numbers that occur as $\{\lambda_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ for some compact Riemannian manifold equipped with its Laplace–Beltrami operator.

Problem. Find necessary and sufficient conditions on a discrete subset (or sequence) $S \subset \mathbb{R}^+$ that characterize when $S$ arises as the Laplace spectrum of some smooth compact Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$. In other words, give an intrinsic characterization (in terms of the sequence $S$ alone, without reference to a manifold) of those discrete sets of positive real numbers that occur as $\{\lambda_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ for some compact Riemannian manifold equipped with its Laplace–Beltrami operator.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

A general intrinsic characterization of which discrete subsets of $\mathbb{R}^+$ arise as Laplace spectra of compact Riemannian manifolds is not known. Only partial results exist: Weyl's law gives an asymptotic necessary condition, heat-kernel and wave-trace invariants supply further constraints, and isospectral but non-isometric examples (Milnor 1964; Sunada; Gordon–Webb–Wolpert) show the spectrum-to-geometry map is highly non-injective. No survey identifies a solution to the inverse-existence problem, which remains an open question in spectral geometry.
