representations.normalized:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ ($N \geq 1$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary. Fix real exponents $0 < k < 1$ and $0 < \alpha < 1$ and a real spectral parameter $\lambda > 0$. Consider the singular semilinear elliptic boundary-value problem
$$
\begin{cases}
-\Delta u + u^{-\alpha}\,\chi_{\{u>0\}} = \lambda\, u^{k} & \text{in } \Omega,\\
u \geq 0 & \text{in } \Omega,\\
u = 0 & \text{on } \partial\Omega,
\end{cases}
\tag{III}
$$
where the absorption term $u^{-\alpha}\chi_{\{u>0\}}$ is interpreted in the maximal monotone graph sense (so that $u^{-\alpha}\chi_{\{u>0\}} = 0$ wherever $u = 0$). A weak solution $u \in H_0^1(\Omega) \cap L^\infty(\Omega)$ is called a *compact-support solution* if its positivity set $\{x \in \Omega : u(x) > 0\}$ has its closure strictly contained in $\Omega$ (so that the free boundary $\partial\{u>0\} \cap \Omega$ is non-empty).

Assume one is in the parameter regime $k - \alpha < 1$ in which non-trivial non-negative solutions to (III) are known to exist for sufficiently large $\lambda$. Describe completely the structure of the set
$$
\mathcal{C}(\lambda) = \{u : u \text{ is a compact-support solution of (III) for the given } \lambda\}.
$$
In particular, determine: (i) for which values of $\lambda$ the set $\mathcal{C}(\lambda)$ is non-empty; (ii) whether $\mathcal{C}(\lambda)$ may contain more than one element (multiplicity); (iii) whether $\mathcal{C}(\lambda)$ admits a continuous parametrization (e.g., a continuum or branch in $\lambda$ bifurcating from the trivial solution or from infinity); and (iv) the geometric structure of the corresponding free boundaries.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is posed as an open problem in a 2014 survey on singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption. Subsequent works by Díaz, Hernández and collaborators (e.g., on indefinite sublinear elliptic problems and on spectral problems with strong absorption, 2015–2025) have addressed related existence and multiplicity issues, but no source found gives a complete description of the structure of the set of compact-support solutions in the regime $k-\alpha<1$. The problem appears to remain open.

representations.normalized:
Consider a spherically symmetric stellar model of the Sun in which, in addition to (or in place of) the standard proton–proton fusion chain, the dominant energy-generating mechanism is taken to be neutron capture on ambient nuclei followed by beta decay of neutron-rich isotopes. Assume the Sun has a central source emitting a steady neutron flux Φ(r) (neutrons per unit area per unit time as a function of radius r), and that throughout the solar interior these neutrons are either (i) captured by a nucleus of charge Z and mass number A, producing an isotope (Z, A+1) which may subsequently beta-decay to (Z+1, A+1) and release energy, or (ii) decay freely to a proton, electron, and antineutrino, contributing to the ionized hydrogen population.

Develop a quantitative model with the following components and address the questions below:

1. Let n_{Z,A}(r,t) denote the number density of nuclide (Z,A) and let σ_{Z,A} denote its thermal neutron-capture cross section and λ_{Z,A} its beta-decay rate. Write down the coupled transport/burn-up equations governing {n_{Z,A}}, the neutron flux Φ, the local temperature T(r), and the luminosity L(r), incorporating hydrostatic equilibrium, radiative/convective energy transport, and the energy released per capture and per beta decay.

2. Determine whether there exists a choice of central neutron source strength and initial composition such that the steady-state solution reproduces simultaneously:
   (a) the observed total solar luminosity L_⊙ ≈ 3.828 × 10^{26} W,
   (b) the observed surface and bulk isotopic abundances of the Sun across the periodic table,
   (c) the measured solar neutrino fluxes (including the electron-antineutrino flux that such a scenario would predict from beta decays, in contrast with the electron-neutrino flux of pp fusion).

3. Quantify the neutron flux Φ(r) required, the resulting net upward drift in average Z (nuclear transmutation pattern through the periodic table), and the predicted antineutrino spectrum, and decide whether any such model is consistent with current observational constraints.

State precisely under which assumptions on Φ, σ_{Z,A}, λ_{Z,A}, and initial composition such a non-fusion-based solar energy model is mathematically and physically viable, or prove that no such consistent model exists.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The standard solar model based on proton–proton fusion is overwhelmingly supported by helioseismology and by SNO/Super-Kamiokande/Borexino neutrino measurements, which directly detect pp, ⁷Be, ⁸B, and CNO neutrinos consistent with fusion. No accepted alternative model based on a central neutron source driving the Sun's luminosity via neutron capture and beta decay has been developed or verified; the speculative question of constructing such a model has not been formally settled in the mathematical-physics literature and remains an unaddressed (effectively open, though widely regarded as inconsistent with data) modeling problem.

representations.normalized:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ ($N\ge 2$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, let $0<\gamma<1$, and let $\lambda>0$. Consider singular semilinear elliptic problems of absorption type whose prototype is
$$-\Delta u + \chi_{\{u>0\}}\,u^{-\gamma} = f \quad\text{in } \Omega,\qquad u\ge 0 \text{ in } \Omega,\qquad u=0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
together with related formulations in which the singular zero-order term may appear with a non-constant coefficient, i.e.
$$-\Delta u + a(x)\,\chi_{\{u>0\}}\,u^{-\gamma} = f \quad\text{in } \Omega,$$
with $a\ge 0$. For such problems, the set $\{u=0\}$ is referred to as the free boundary.

Develop a theory of the above problems when the data are Radon measures rather than functions. Specifically:

(a) (Measure source.) Let $\mu$ be a nonnegative bounded Radon measure on $\Omega$ and replace $f$ by $\mu$. Determine in what sense (e.g., renormalized, entropy, or distributional solutions) and under what assumptions on $\mu$ (absolute continuity with respect to a suitable capacity, concentration on lower-dimensional sets, etc.) the problem admits a nonnegative solution; analyze uniqueness versus multiplicity of solutions; and describe the structure, regularity, non-degeneracy, and Hausdorff dimension estimates of the free boundary $\partial\{u>0\}$ in terms of $\mu$.

(b) (Measure coefficient of the zero-order term.) Allow the coefficient $a$ to be a nonnegative Radon measure $\nu$ on $\Omega$, so that the singular absorption term takes the formal expression $\nu\,\chi_{\{u>0\}}u^{-\gamma}$. Give a rigorous meaning to this term, establish existence (and, where possible, uniqueness or multiplicity) of nonnegative solutions, and study how the support and singular part of $\nu$ influence the location, regularity, and geometric-measure properties of the free boundary.

The problem is to extend the existence, multiplicity, and free-boundary results known in the function-data setting to these two measure-data settings, identifying the optimal classes of measures for which each phenomenon persists.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Substantial progress has been made on singular nonlinear elliptic equations with measure data: existence/uniqueness theories (renormalized and entropy solutions) for $-\Delta_p u + H(u)=\mu$ with singular $H$ have been developed (e.g., Oliva–Petitta and subsequent works), and quasilinear equations with measure-valued absorption terms and measure data have been treated. Free-boundary aspects (regularity, non-degeneracy, Hausdorff estimates) are well-studied for function data and have been partially extended, but a complete theory addressing multiplicity and free-boundary structure when measures appear simultaneously as sources and as coefficients of the singular zero-order term remains incomplete.

Let $G$ denote Newton's gravitational constant appearing in the gravitational force law $F = G\,m_1 m_2 / r^2$, and more generally let $\{c_i\}$ denote the dimensionful fundamental constants of nature (such as $G$, the speed of light $c$, Planck's constant $\hbar$, and the fine-structure constant $\alpha$). Determine whether any of these constants—and in particular $G$—are truly invariant, or whether they depend on cosmic time $t$ and/or on the local physical environment (matter density, gravitational potential, scale, etc.). Specifically:

(a) Decide whether $\dot G/G \neq 0$, and if so, give a quantitative law $G = G(t,\mathbf{x};\text{environment})$ governing the variation.

(b) Determine whether the same law (or any consistent law) reconciles the value of $G$ inferred from celestial-mechanical observations (planetary ephemerides, binary pulsar timing, lunar laser ranging, gravitational-wave inspirals of compact binaries, cosmological probes such as the CMB, BAO, and BBN) with the value measured in terrestrial laboratory (Cavendish-type) experiments.

(c) If a variation exists, derive the functional form of $G(t)$ from first principles within a self-consistent theory of gravity and verify its compatibility with the current observational bounds.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Current observational and laboratory studies through 2025 continue only to place tighter upper bounds on $\dot G/G$ (e.g., $\dot G/G = (0.016 \pm 0.098)\times 10^{-15}\,\text{yr}^{-1}$ from white-dwarf H$_2$ spectra in 2025; cosmological CMB+BAO+BBN measurements in 2025 consistent with the laboratory value within $1\sigma$; gravitational-wave bounds from GW170817 of order $10^{-8}\,\text{yr}^{-1}$). No definitive detection of temporal variation has been established, and no universally accepted law for the variation exists. The problem is therefore open.

Consider a 3D bipedal robot modeled as a hybrid dynamical system consisting of:

(i) Continuous single-support (and possibly double-support) phases governed by Lagrangian dynamics
   D(q) q̈ + C(q, q̇) q̇ + G(q) = B u + J(q)^T λ,
where q ∈ Q ⊂ R^n is the configuration, u ∈ R^m is the control input, λ are ground-reaction forces enforcing unilateral contact constraints (foot non-penetration, friction-cone, and zero-moment conditions);

(ii) Discrete impact maps modeling foot touchdown,
   (q^+, q̇^+) = Δ(q^-, q̇^-),
which reset velocities under a rigid plastic-impact assumption.

Let the terrain be described by an unknown function h : R^2 → R giving the ground height, with bounded slope and curvature but otherwise not known a priori to the controller. The robot has no advance map of h; at each step the location and orientation of the support surface beneath the swing foot is revealed only at (or shortly before) impact.

Problem. Construct a feedback control law u = κ(q, q̇, y), where y is online sensory information available to the robot (e.g., joint encoders, IMU, contact sensing, possibly proprioceptive estimation of local terrain), together with a choice of reference / virtual-constraint or gait-library structure, such that the closed-loop hybrid system admits a forward-invariant set of states from which the robot executes an infinite sequence of steps without falling, for every admissible terrain function h in a prescribed class H of uneven grounds (characterized by uniform bounds on slope, step height, and friction). Equivalently, exhibit a provably stable walking strategy on unknown uneven terrain in the above class, or establish fundamental obstructions to its existence.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Stable 3D bipedal walking over unknown uneven terrain remains an active and largely open research problem. Substantial partial progress exists (e.g., gait libraries, hybrid zero dynamics extensions, rough-terrain MPC, and learning-based controllers demonstrated on robots like Cassie and ATLAS), but no general control framework with rigorous stability guarantees over arbitrary unknown uneven terrain has been established.

Consider a planar or three-dimensional bipedal robot modeled as a rigid open kinematic chain with stiff (non-compliant) feet and limbs. Walking is described as a hybrid dynamical system that alternates between continuous-time phases (single support, double support) and discrete impact events corresponding to the swing leg striking the ground.

The standard rigid-body impact model treats the foot-ground collision as an instantaneous, perfectly inelastic impulsive event: the impact map is derived from conservation of generalized momentum subject to the algebraic constraint that the impacting foot has zero velocity immediately after impact (and, in many formulations, that the previous stance foot lifts off). Under this standard model, it can be shown that any nontrivial double-support phase, in which both feet remain in stationary ground contact for a positive time interval while the configuration evolves, is essentially precluded for a robot with stiff feet and limbs.

Problem: Construct an impact model — exact or approximate — for the inelastic collision of the swing leg with the ground in a rigid bipedal robot with stiff feet and limbs, such that the resulting hybrid model admits periodic walking gaits with a nontrivial (positive-duration) double-support phase occupying a substantial fraction of the gait cycle, in qualitative agreement with human walking. Specify the post-impact velocity reset map, the contact constraints active during double support, the conditions for transition into and out of double support, and verify that the resulting hybrid model is physically consistent (energy-non-increasing, satisfies unilateral contact constraints with non-negative normal forces and friction-cone conditions) and admits at least one stable periodic gait with a nontrivial double-support sub-phase.

Consider a hybrid dynamical model of a 3D bipedal walker, consisting of (i) continuous-time Lagrangian dynamics during single-support phases of the form $D(q)\ddot q + C(q,\dot q)\dot q + G(q) = B(q)u$, where $q\in Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ are generalized coordinates and $u\in\mathbb{R}^m$ is the control input, together with (ii) a discrete impact map $(q^+,\dot q^+) = \Delta(q^-,\dot q^-)$ that resets the state when a swing-foot guard surface $S=\{(q,\dot q): h(q)=0,\, L_{\dot q}h(q)<0\}$ is reached. A solution $(q(\cdot),\dot q(\cdot),u(\cdot))$ is called a hybrid periodic orbit of period $T>0$ if it satisfies the continuous dynamics on $[0,T)$, hits $S$ at $t=T^-$, and $(q(0),\dot q(0)) = \Delta(q(T^-),\dot q(T^-))$.

A virtual-constraint controller is specified by a smooth output $y = h_c(q) - h_d(\theta(q))$, where $\theta:Q\to\mathbb{R}$ is a monotonic phasing variable and $h_d$ is a parametrized desired profile (e.g., Bézier polynomials with parameter $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^N$). The zero dynamics manifold $Z_\alpha = \{(q,\dot q): y=0,\,\dot y=0\}$ is required to be invariant under both the continuous dynamics (under the feedback that zeros $y$) and the impact map.

Problem. Develop a numerical method that, given the hybrid model and a class of virtual constraints parametrized by $\alpha$, computes an open-loop periodic state-input trajectory $(q^*(\cdot),\dot q^*(\cdot),u^*(\cdot))$ together with parameters $\alpha^*$ such that:
(a) the trajectory is a hybrid periodic orbit of the closed-loop system with $y\equiv 0$ on the orbit (i.e., the orbit lies in $Z_{\alpha^*}$ and is invariant under $\Delta$),
(b) the cost functional $J(\alpha) = \frac{1}{T}\int_0^T \|u^*(t)\|^2\,dt$ (or another energy-efficiency criterion such as cost of transport) is minimized, subject to inequality constraints encoding ground-reaction feasibility, friction-cone, joint-limit, and unilateral-contact conditions,
(c) the method overcomes the proliferation of spurious local minima that plague direct nonlinear-programming formulations of this combined periodicity-plus-efficiency problem, and
(d) the resulting periodic solution and parameters $\alpha^*$ are directly usable for designing exponentially stabilizing feedback laws via hybrid zero dynamics.

Provide such an algorithm (or prove an obstruction) that reliably produces certified periodic, energy-efficient solutions for 3D biped models with $n\geq 7$ degrees of freedom.

Let X be a separable metric space, viewed as a subspace of the real line R. For a collection A of open covers of X, let O denote all open covers, Ω the open ω-covers (those open covers U such that every finite subset of X is contained in some single member of U), and Γ the open γ-covers (infinite open covers U such that every point of X lies in all but finitely many members of U).

For two such collections A and B, the selection principle Ufin(A, B) asserts that whenever (U_n : n ∈ N) is a sequence of members of A such that no U_n contains a finite subcover of X, there exist finite subfamilies F_n ⊆ U_n with the property that the cover { ⋃ F_n : n ∈ N } belongs to B.

A subset F of R is σ-compact if it is a countable union of compact sets. A subset B of R is Fσδ if it is a countable intersection of Fσ sets.

Question. Suppose X ⊆ B ⊆ R, where B is a Borel set and X has the property Ufin(O, Γ) (i.e. X is a Hurewicz space). Must there exist a σ-compact set F with X ⊆ F ⊆ B? Does the answer remain affirmative under the stronger hypothesis that B is an Fσδ set?

Banakh and Zdomskyy (Topology Appl. 156 (2008), 10–15) showed that the Gδ-separation property is equivalent to the Hurewicz property, but consistently (e.g. under the set-theoretic hypothesis b = d) there is a Hurewicz subspace of a Borel/Fσδ ambient space that is not contained in any σ-compact subset of that ambient space. Hence the answer to both questions is consistently "no", giving a negative consistency answer; a definitive ZFC resolution is not visible in the search results, so the problem appears to be at least partially resolved (negatively, modulo consistency assumptions).

Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the real line with its standard topology, and let $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}$. An open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is called an $\omega$-cover of $X$ if $X \notin \mathcal{U}$ and for every finite subset $F \subseteq X$ there exists $U \in \mathcal{U}$ with $F \subseteq U$. Let $\Omega(X)$ denote the family of all open $\omega$-covers of $X$.

The selection principle $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Omega,\Omega)$ holds for $X$ if for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\omega}$ with $\mathcal{U}_n \in \Omega(X)$, there exist finite subsets $\mathcal{F}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_{n\in\omega} \mathcal{F}_n \in \Omega(X)$.

Let $\mathfrak{d}$ denote the dominating number, namely the least cardinality of a family $D \subseteq \omega^\omega$ such that for every $f \in \omega^\omega$ there exists $g \in D$ with $f(n) \le g(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$.

Question: Does ZFC prove the existence of a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ satisfying $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Omega,\Omega)$ with $|X| = \mathfrak{d}$?

For a set of reals $X$, let $\mathcal{B}(X)$ denote the family of countable covers of $X$ by Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}$. The selection principle $\mathsf{S}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{B})$ asserts that for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with each $\mathcal{U}_n\in\mathcal{B}(X)$, there exist finite subfamilies $\mathcal{F}_n\subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\mathcal{F}_n$ is a cover of $X$ (this is the Menger-type selection principle restricted to countable Borel covers).

For a class $\mathcal{J}$ of sets of reals, "Borel's Conjecture for $\mathcal{J}$" is the statement that every member of $\mathcal{J}$ is countable.

Question: Is it consistent with ZFC that every set of reals $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ satisfying $\mathsf{S}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{B})$ is countable?

For a set of reals $X$, a countable family $\mathcal{U}$ of Borel subsets of $X$ is called a Borel $\omega$-cover of $X$ if $X \notin \mathcal{U}$ and for every finite set $F \subseteq X$ there exists $U \in \mathcal{U}$ with $F \subseteq U$. Let $\mathcal{B}_\Omega$ denote the family of all countable Borel $\omega$-covers of $X$.

A set of reals $X$ satisfies the selection principle $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{B}_\Omega, \mathcal{B}_\Omega)$ if for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of elements of $\mathcal{B}_\Omega$ there exist finite subfamilies $\mathcal{F}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \mathcal{F}_n \in \mathcal{B}_\Omega$.

Question: Is it consistent with ZFC that every set of reals $X$ satisfying $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{B}_\Omega, \mathcal{B}_\Omega)$ is countable?

For graphs $G$, $H$, and $F$, write $F \to (G,H)$ if for every coloring of the edges of $F$ with the two colors red and blue there is either a red subgraph isomorphic to $G$ or a blue subgraph isomorphic to $H$. A graph $F$ is called Ramsey $(G,H)$-minimal if $F \to (G,H)$ but for every edge $e \in E(F)$ one has $F-e \not\to (G,H)$. Let $kK_2$ denote the matching consisting of $k$ pairwise disjoint edges.

For each integer $t \ge 6$, give an explicit characterization of all $2$-connected graphs $F$ that are Ramsey $(2K_2,\, tK_2)$-minimal.

Let $X$ be a set of real numbers (equivalently, a separable metrizable zero-dimensional space). A countable family $\mathcal{U}$ of Borel subsets of $X$ is called a Borel $\omega$-cover of $X$ if $X \notin \mathcal{U}$ and for every finite set $F \subseteq X$ there exists $U \in \mathcal{U}$ with $F \subseteq U$. Let $\mathcal{B}_\Omega$ denote the collection of all countable Borel $\omega$-covers of $X$.

For collections $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ of families of subsets of $X$:
- $X$ satisfies $S_1(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B})$ if, for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with each $\mathcal{U}_n \in \mathcal{A}$, there exist $U_n \in \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{U_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \in \mathcal{B}$.
- $X$ satisfies $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B})$ if, for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with each $\mathcal{U}_n \in \mathcal{A}$, there exist finite sets $\mathcal{F}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}} \mathcal{F}_n \in \mathcal{B}$.

Question: If a set of reals $X$ satisfies $S_1(\mathcal{B}_\Omega, \mathcal{B}_\Omega)$, must $X^k$ satisfy $S_1(\mathcal{B}_\Omega, \mathcal{B}_\Omega)$ for every positive integer $k$? Analogously, if $X$ satisfies $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{B}_\Omega, \mathcal{B}_\Omega)$, must every finite power $X^k$ satisfy $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{B}_\Omega, \mathcal{B}_\Omega)$?

Let X and Y be sets of real numbers (regarded as topological subspaces of R). For a topological space Z, let:
• O(Z) denote the family of all open covers of Z;
• Ω(Z) denote the family of open ω-covers of Z, i.e. open covers U of Z such that Z ∉ U and every finite subset of Z is contained in some member of U;
• Γ(Z) denote the family of open γ-covers of Z, i.e. infinite open covers U of Z such that every point of Z belongs to all but finitely many members of U.

For classes A, B of covers, define the following selection principles:
• S1(A, B): for every sequence (Un : n ∈ N) with each Un ∈ A, there exist Un ∈ Un such that {Un : n ∈ N} ∈ B.
• Sfin(A, B): for every sequence (Un : n ∈ N) with each Un ∈ A, there exist finite Fn ⊆ Un such that ∪n Fn ∈ B.
• Ufin(A, B): for every sequence (Un : n ∈ N) of elements of A with no finite subcover, there exist finite Fn ⊆ Un such that {∪Fn : n ∈ N} ∈ B.

The property S1(O, O) is the Rothberger property and Ufin(O, Γ) is the Hurewicz property.

Suppose that X and Y both satisfy S1(O, O), and that X additionally satisfies Ufin(O, Γ). Does it necessarily follow that the product space X × Y satisfies S1(O, O)?

Research on productive Rothberger/Hurewicz properties (Miller–Tsaban–Zdomskyy, "Selective covering properties of product spaces", and subsequent work) gives consistency results and partial answers: under hypotheses like Semifilter Trichotomy or in the Miller model, every scale/concentrated set is productively Rothberger and Hurewicz, and in the Miller model every Rothberger set of reals is Hurewicz. Work in the oriented 3-sphere S^3. A generalized knot in S^3 is an oriented immersed circle whose only self-intersections are transverse double points (so at each double point the two tangent vectors are linearly independent). For each integer m ≥ 0, let K_m denote the set of generalized knots with exactly m double points, considered up to ambient isotopy.

Given a generalized knot K ∈ K_m and a double point p of K, choose a small disk neighborhood of p in which the two branches of K appear as an "X" with both strands oriented upward. Define K^+_p ∈ K_{m-1} to be the generalized knot obtained by replacing this crossing by the resolution in which the strand from lower-left to upper-right passes over the strand from lower-right to upper-left, and define K^-_p ∈ K_{m-1} to be the resolution with the opposite over/under choice.

Let n ≥ 1 be a fixed integer. An ambient-isotopy invariant I defined on generalized knots with at least n double points is said to integrate to an invariant of generalized knots with n−1 double points if there exists an invariant I′ on K_{n-1} such that, for every K ∈ K_n with set of double points D,
   I(K) = Σ_{p ∈ D} ( I′(K^+_p) − I′(K^-_p) ).
By iterating, one says that I integrates all the way to an invariant of honest knots (elements of K_0) if there is a chain of invariants on K_{n-1}, K_{n-2}, …, K_0 each integrating the previous one.

Question: Suppose I is an invariant of generalized knots with at least n double points which integrates to some invariant of K_{n-1}. Must I then necessarily integrate all the way down to an invariant of honest knots in K_0?

Background and definitions. Let X be a topological space (typically a Lindelöf space, e.g. a set of reals). For a family U of subsets of X, U is called a (open) cover of X if X = ⋃ U and X ∉ U. Let O(X) denote the collection of all open covers of X.

Given collections A and B of covers of X, define the following selection principles:
- S_fin(A, B): For every sequence (U_n : n ∈ ω) with each U_n ∈ A, there exist finite F_n ⊆ U_n such that ⋃_{n∈ω} F_n ∈ B.
- U_fin(A, B): For every sequence (U_n : n ∈ ω) with each U_n ∈ A and no U_n containing a finite subcover of X, there exist finite F_n ⊆ U_n such that { ⋃ F_n : n ∈ ω } ∈ B.

Let Ω denote the collection of ω-covers of X (open covers U such that every finite subset of X is contained in some member of U), and let Γ denote the collection of γ-covers of X (infinite open covers U such that every x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of U).

The Scheepers diagram consists of the (provably distinct, in ZFC, classes of) covering properties obtained by choosing A, B ∈ {O, Ω, Γ}, including in particular the Menger property S_fin(O, O), the property S_fin(Γ, Ω), the Hurewicz property U_fin(O, Γ), the Scheepers property U_fin(O, Ω), and U_fin(O, O) (= S_fin(O, O) for Lindelöf spaces).

A property P of topological spaces is said to be preserved under finite products if whenever X and Y satisfy P, the product X × Y satisfies P.

Question. Is there a model of ZFC in which at least one of the S_fin-type or U_fin-type covering properties appearing in the Scheepers diagram is preserved under finite products (for, say, sets of real numbers)?

Let Ω denote the collection of ω-covers of X (open covers U such that every finite subset of X is contained in some member of U), and let Γ denote the collection of γ-covers of X (infinite open covers U such that every x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of U).

The Scheepers diagram consists of the (provably distinct, in ZFC, classes of) covering properties obtained by choosing A, B ∈ {O, Ω, Γ}, including in particular the Menger property S_fin(O, O), the property S_fin(Γ, Ω), the Hurewicz property U_fin(O, Γ), the Scheepers property U_fin(O, Ω), and U_fin(O, O) (= S_fin(O, O) for Lindelöf spaces).

A property P of topological spaces is said to be preserved under finite products if whenever X and Y satisfy P, the product X × Y satisfies P.

Question. Is there a model of ZFC in which at least one of the S_fin-type or U_fin-type covering properties appearing in the Scheepers diagram is preserved under finite products (for, say, sets of real numbers)?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Recent work (2024–2025) on the Scheepers diagram continues to investigate productive behavior of these properties, mostly establishing partial productivity results for individual spaces (e.g., b-scale sets being productively Hurewicz/Menger) and exhibiting counterexamples to product preservation in ZFC. No model has been published in which an S_fin- or U_fin-type Scheepers-diagram property is preserved under finite products in general, and recent papers still list related productivity questions as open.

Let X be a separable metrizable (zero-dimensional) topological space, and let B(X) denote the collection of countable covers of X by Borel sets. A Borel cover U of X is called a Borel ω-cover if X itself is not in U and for every finite subset F ⊆ X there exists U ∈ U with F ⊆ U; let BΩ(X) be the family of all Borel ω-covers of X.

For families A and B of covers of X, the selection principle Sfin(A, B) asserts: for every sequence (Un : n ∈ ω) of elements of A there exist finite subsets Fn ⊆ Un such that ⋃_{n∈ω} Fn ∈ B. A topological property P (regarded as a class of sets of reals) is called additive if whenever X and Y are sets of reals satisfying P, the union X ∪ Y also satisfies P.

Question: Is there a model of ZFC in which the property Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) is additive — that is, in which for all sets of reals X, Y satisfying Sfin(BΩ(X), BΩ(X)) and Sfin(BΩ(Y), BΩ(Y)) respectively, the union X ∪ Y satisfies Sfin(BΩ(X∪Y), BΩ(X∪Y))?

Consider the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations for a polytropic ideal gas, written for the conserved variables (density ρ>0, momentum ρu, total energy E) on ℝ×(0,∞):

  ∂_t ρ + ∂_x(ρu) = 0,
  ∂_t(ρu) + ∂_x(ρu² + p) = 0,
  ∂_t E + ∂_x((E+p)u) = 0,

with E = ρe + ½ρu², pressure law p = (γ−1)ρe for some adiabatic constant γ>1, and specific internal energy e>0. An entropy weak solution is a bounded measurable solution of the system in the distributional sense that, in addition, satisfies the entropy inequality

  ∂_t(ρS(η)) + ∂_x(ρuS(η)) ≤ 0

for every convex entropy pair associated with the system (equivalently, the Lax/physical entropy admissibility condition at shocks).

Let BV(ℝ) denote the space of functions of bounded total variation on the real line. Given Cauchy data (ρ_0, u_0, e_0) ∈ BV(ℝ) with ρ_0, e_0 bounded away from 0 but with no smallness restriction on the total variation (large-BV data), determine whether the Cauchy problem admits, for all times t∈[0,∞), a globally defined entropy weak solution, and whether such a solution is unique within a natural class of admissible BV solutions. In other words: establish (or disprove) global existence, uniqueness, and entropy admissibility of entropy weak solutions in BV for arbitrarily large BV initial data.

Global well-posedness of entropy weak solutions to the 1D compressible Euler equations for a polytropic gas with large BV initial data is widely cited as an outstanding open problem. Glimm's theorem and subsequent work (Bressan, Liu, Yang, etc.) establish global existence and uniqueness only for small-BV data. Let X be a topological space (typically a separable metrizable space, e.g., a set of real numbers). An open cover U of X is called an ω-cover if X is not a member of U and every finite subset of X is contained in some member of U. An open ω-cover U of X is called a τ-cover if for every two distinct points x,y of X, either {U ∈ U : x ∈ U, y ∉ U} is finite or {U ∈ U : y ∈ U, x ∉ U} is finite. Let Ω denote the collection of all open ω-covers of X and T the collection of all open τ-covers of X.

Consider the following two properties of X.

(a) The property ((Ω, T)): every open ω-cover of X contains a subfamily which is an open τ-cover of X.

(b) The selection principle S_fin(Ω, T): for every sequence (U_n : n ∈ ℕ) of open ω-covers of X, there exist finite sets F_n ⊆ U_n such that the union ⋃_{n ∈ ℕ} F_n is an open τ-cover of X.

Question: Are the properties ((Ω, T)) and S_fin(Ω, T) equivalent for all such spaces X?

Consider the compressible Euler equations in $d\ge 2$ space dimensions for an ideal fluid:
$$\partial_t \rho + \nabla\cdot(\rho u)=0,\qquad \partial_t(\rho u)+\nabla\cdot(\rho u\otimes u)+\nabla p=0,\qquad \partial_t E+\nabla\cdot((E+p)u)=0,$$
where $\rho>0$ denotes density, $u\in\mathbb{R}^d$ velocity, $p$ pressure, and $E=\tfrac12\rho|u|^2+\rho e$ total energy, closed by an equation of state (e.g.\ ideal-gas $p=(\gamma-1)\rho e$, $\gamma>1$). It is known that for generic smooth (e.g.\ $C^\infty$, compactly supported perturbations of a constant state) initial data, the local-in-time smooth solution must lose regularity in finite time.

Provide a characterization, in terms of the initial data, of the structure of the singularities that first form from such smooth solutions. In particular:

(a) Classify the possible types of first singularities (e.g.\ genuine shocks formed by gradient catastrophe of an outgoing simple wave, versus "shell singularities" associated with focusing/collapse of characteristic surfaces of the acoustic metric, and any other admissible types).

(b) Give explicit, verifiable conditions on the initial data $(\rho_0,u_0,e_0)$ that determine which type of singularity occurs first, and in particular identify the open set (or generic class) of smooth initial data for which a genuine shock (a pre-shock with the canonical $C^{1/3}$ cusp followed by a discontinuity) forms strictly before any shell singularity develops.

Consider the compressible Navier–Stokes equations governing a viscous polytropic gas in d=2 or 3 spatial dimensions, written for the density ρ(t,x) ≥ 0, the velocity u(t,x) ∈ R^d, and the absolute temperature θ(t,x) ≥ 0:

∂_t ρ + div(ρ u) = 0,
∂_t(ρ u) + div(ρ u ⊗ u) + ∇p = μ Δu + (μ+λ) ∇ div u,
∂_t(ρ E) + div((ρ E + p) u) = div(κ ∇θ) + div(S · u),

where E = e + |u|^2/2 with internal energy e = c_v θ, the pressure is given by the polytropic law p = R ρ θ (R, c_v > 0), the viscous stress is S = μ(∇u + ∇u^T) + λ div u · I with shear viscosity μ > 0 fixed and bulk viscosity satisfying 2μ + dλ ≥ 0, and the heat conductivity satisfies κ ≥ 0. No exterior force or heat source is applied. Equip the system with either (a) Cauchy data on R^d, or (b) physically admissible boundary conditions on a bounded domain Ω ⊂ R^d.

Address the following questions for arbitrarily large initial data:

1. Is the Cauchy problem (and the initial–boundary-value problem) globally well posed in time for large initial data (without smallness assumptions)?

2. If singularities can form, can they form in finite or infinite time for solutions issuing from large but smooth, vacuum-free initial data (i.e., with inf ρ_0 > 0)? In particular, can the vacuum state {ρ = 0} appear in finite time from initial data that are bounded away from vacuum?

3. Identify the admissible function spaces in which weak solutions can be defined and studied after singularity formation, and characterize the structure of such singularities.

4. Determine the large-time asymptotic behavior of these weak solutions.

Provide proofs or counterexamples for each of (1)–(4).

Global well-posedness of the full compressible Navier–Stokes system in 2D/3D for large initial data, the possibility of finite-time vacuum formation from non-vacuum smooth data, the proper functional framework for weak solutions past singularities, and their long-time asymptotics remain widely recognized as major open problems. Let X be an infinite topological space. A cover U of X by proper open subsets is called:
- an ω-cover (notation Ω) if every finite subset of X is contained in some member of U;
- a γ-cover (notation Γ) if U is infinite and every x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of U;
- a τ-cover (notation T) if U is a large cover (each x ∈ X is in infinitely many members of U) and for any two points x, y ∈ X, either {U ∈ U : x ∈ U, y ∉ U} or {U ∈ U : y ∈ U, x ∉ U} is finite.

For classes A, B of covers of X, define the selection principles:
- S1(A, B): for every sequence (Un)n∈N of covers from A there exist Un ∈ Un such that {Un : n ∈ N} ∈ B.
- Sfin(A, B): for every sequence (Un)n∈N of covers from A there exist finite Fn ⊆ Un such that ⋃n Fn ∈ B.

A property P of topological spaces is said to be preserved under finite powers if whenever X satisfies P, then Xk satisfies P for every positive integer k.

Question: Determine, for each of the selection properties
   S1(Ω, T), Sfin(Ω, T), S1(T, Γ), S1(T, T), S1(T, Ω), Sfin(T, T), Sfin(T, Ω),
whether it is preserved under finite powers.

Consider the compressible Navier–Stokes equations for a heat-conducting fluid in $d$ space dimensions,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\partial_t \rho + \nabla\!\cdot(\rho u) &= 0,\\
\partial_t(\rho u) + \nabla\!\cdot(\rho u\otimes u) + \nabla p &= \varepsilon\,\nabla\!\cdot\bigl(\mu(\nabla u + \nabla u^\top) + \lambda(\nabla\!\cdot u)\,\mathbb{I}\bigr),\\
\partial_t(\rho E) + \nabla\!\cdot\bigl((\rho E + p)u\bigr) &= \varepsilon\,\nabla\!\cdot\bigl(\kappa\nabla\theta\bigr) + \varepsilon\,\nabla\!\cdot\!\bigl((\mu(\nabla u+\nabla u^\top)+\lambda(\nabla\!\cdot u)\mathbb{I})\,u\bigr),
\end{aligned}
$$
where $\rho>0$ is the density, $u$ the velocity, $\theta$ the absolute temperature, $p=p(\rho,\theta)$ the pressure, $E=\tfrac{1}{2}|u|^2+e(\rho,\theta)$ the total energy, $\mu,\lambda,\kappa>0$ are normalized transport coefficients, and $\varepsilon>0$ is a small parameter scaling viscosity and heat conduction. Let $u^\varepsilon=(\rho^\varepsilon,u^\varepsilon,\theta^\varepsilon)$ denote a sequence of solutions, and let $\bar u=(\bar\rho,\bar u,\bar\theta)$ be a corresponding solution of the compressible Euler system obtained by setting $\varepsilon=0$.

Establish the following three statements concerning the zero-dissipation limit $\varepsilon\to 0^+$.

(a) Suppose $\bar u$ is piecewise smooth on a finite time interval $[0,T]$ with finitely many entropy-satisfying shock discontinuity surfaces. Show that, for suitably prepared initial data, $u^\varepsilon\to\bar u$ uniformly on every compact subset of the complement of an arbitrarily thin tubular neighborhood of the shock surfaces, and quantify the convergence rate.

(b) Suppose $\bar u$ is piecewise smooth and contains contact discontinuity surfaces (which are linearly degenerate and subject to vortex-sheet instability). Determine whether, and in what sense, $u^\varepsilon$ converges to $\bar u$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^+$, in particular in space dimension $d\ge 2$ where shear may trigger Kelvin–Helmholtz-type instabilities.

(c) In a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ with solid boundary $\partial\Omega$, where $u^\varepsilon$ satisfies the no-slip condition $u^\varepsilon|_{\partial\Omega}=0$ while $\bar u$ satisfies only the no-penetration condition $\bar u\cdot \nu|_{\partial\Omega}=0$, rigorously justify Prandtl's laminar boundary layer ansatz: prove that $u^\varepsilon=\bar u+U^P(t,x_\parallel,x_\perp/\sqrt{\varepsilon})+o(1)$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^+$, where $U^P$ solves the Prandtl boundary layer equations, for physically relevant flows.

Setup. Let $X$ be an infinite topological space. By a "cover" of $X$ we always mean a collection of open subsets of $X$ none of which equals $X$ itself, whose union is $X$.

- A cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is an $\omega$-cover ($\mathcal{U}\in\Omega$) if every finite subset of $X$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{U}$.
- A cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is a $\tau$-cover ($\mathcal{U}\in T$) if it is a large cover (every $x\in X$ belongs to infinitely many $U\in\mathcal{U}$) and for any two points $x,y\in X$, either $\{U\in\mathcal{U}: x\in U,\ y\notin U\}$ is finite, or $\{U\in\mathcal{U}: y\in U,\ x\notin U\}$ is finite.
- A cover $\mathcal{U}$ is multifinite if it can be partitioned into infinitely many finite blocks.
- Let $\gimel(T)$ denote the family of $T$-glueable covers, i.e. open covers $\mathcal{U}$ such that either $\mathcal{U}$ is multifinite, or $\mathcal{U}$ admits a partition into finite blocks $\mathcal{U}=\bigsqcup_{n} F_n$ with $F_n$ finite, such that the collection $\{\bigcup F_n : n\in\mathbb{N}\}$ is an open $\tau$-cover of $X$.

For families $\mathscr{A},\mathscr{B}$ of covers, the selection principles are defined as follows.

- $\mathsf{S}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathscr{A},\mathscr{B})$: For every sequence $\langle \mathcal{U}_n : n\in\mathbb{N}\rangle$ of members of $\mathscr{A}$, there exist finite sets $F_n\subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_{n}F_n\in\mathscr{B}$.
- $\mathsf{U}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathscr{A},\mathscr{B})$: For every sequence $\langle \mathcal{U}_n : n\in\mathbb{N}\rangle$ of members of $\mathscr{A}$ (with no $\mathcal{U}_n$ containing a finite subcover), there exist finite sets $F_n\subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{\bigcup F_n : n\in\mathbb{N}\}\in\mathscr{B}$.

Let $O$ denote the family of all open covers of $X$.

Question. Is it true that, for every (suitable) topological space $X$, the property $\mathsf{U}_{\mathrm{fin}}(O,T)$ is equivalent to $\mathsf{S}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Omega,\gimel(T))$?

Let $X$ be an infinite topological space (typically a set of real numbers with the subspace topology). An open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is called:

- a *large cover* if $X \notin \mathcal{U}$ and every $x \in X$ belongs to infinitely many members of $\mathcal{U}$; the family of large open covers of $X$ is denoted $\Lambda$.
- an $\Omega$-*cover* if $X \notin \mathcal{U}$ and for every finite set $F \subseteq X$ there exists $U \in \mathcal{U}$ with $F \subseteq U$; the family of $\Omega$-covers is denoted $\Omega$.

For a cover $\mathcal{U}$, call $\mathcal{U}$ an $\Omega$-*glueable cover* if it is a large open cover and there exists a partition $\mathcal{U} = \bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}} \mathcal{F}_n$ of $\mathcal{U}$ into finite sets $\mathcal{F}_n$ such that $\{\bigcup \mathcal{F}_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is an $\Omega$-cover of $X$. Let $\gimel(\Omega)$ denote the family of $\Omega$-glueable covers.

For families $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ of covers, the selection principle $\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$ holds for $X$ if for every sequence $\mathcal{U}_1, \mathcal{U}_2, \dots \in \mathcal{A}$ (none containing a finite subcover of $X$) there exist finite sets $\mathcal{F}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{\bigcup \mathcal{F}_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \in \mathcal{B}$.

Let $(\Lambda\ \gimel(\Omega))$ denote the property that every large open cover of $X$ contains an $\Omega$-glueable subcover.

Question: Is the property $\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O}, \Omega)$ (where $\mathcal{O}$ is the family of all open covers) equivalent to the property $(\Lambda\ \gimel(\Omega))$?

Consider the nonlinear Boltzmann equation
\[ \partial_t F + v\cdot\nabla_x F = \tfrac{1}{\varepsilon} Q(F,F), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d,\ v\in\mathbb{R}^3, \]
where $F=F^\varepsilon(t,x,v)\ge 0$ is the one-particle distribution function, $\varepsilon>0$ is the Knudsen number, and $Q$ is the standard binary collision operator (e.g. for the hard-sphere model)
\[ Q(F,F)(v) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\!\int_{S^2}\big(F(v')F(v'_*)-F(v)F(v_*)\big)\,B(v-v_*,\omega)\,d\omega\,dv_*, \]
with $v',v'_*$ the post-collisional velocities. The macroscopic (fluid) variables of $F$ are
\[ \rho=\!\int F\,dv,\quad \rho u=\!\int vF\,dv,\quad \rho\big(\tfrac{|u|^2}{2}+e\big)=\!\int \tfrac{|v|^2}{2}F\,dv. \]
Formally, as $\varepsilon\to 0$, $(\rho,u,e)$ should solve the compressible Euler system, and at the next order the compressible Navier–Stokes system.

Question. Provide a rigorous mathematical justification of the hydrodynamic limit $\varepsilon\to 0$ from the Boltzmann equation to the compressible Euler (and to the compressible Navier–Stokes) equations in each of the following situations, going beyond smooth flows in the whole space and beyond simplified discrete-velocity models such as the Broadwell model:
(a) when the limiting fluid solution contains shock waves;
(b) when the limiting fluid solution contains contact discontinuities;
(c) when the spatial domain $\Omega$ has a physical boundary, with appropriate kinetic boundary conditions (e.g. diffuse reflection, specular reflection, or Maxwell-type) and the corresponding fluid boundary conditions.

In particular, establish convergence of $F^\varepsilon$ to a local Maxwellian determined by the fluid solution, in a function-space topology strong enough to capture the discontinuities and/or boundary layers, for the full nonlinear Boltzmann equation with a physical collision kernel.

Significant partial progress exists: rigorous derivations of the compressible Euler limit from the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation have been obtained for individual shock waves, contact discontinuities, rarefaction waves, and even Riemann-type superpositions, via Hilbert expansion with shock-layer corrections and macro–micro decomposition (Yu, Huang–Wang–Wang–Yang and collaborators). Boundary-layer/half-space results with diffuse-reflection conditions have also appeared. However, a fully general justification covering arbitrary BV/entropy solutions with multiple interacting shocks, general contact discontinuities, and general physical boundaries for the full nonlinear Boltzmann equation remains open.

For families $\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{V}$ of open covers, the property $\mathrm{Split}(\mathcal{U},\mathcal{V})$ asserts: for every cover $\mathcal{U} \in \mathcal{U}$, there exist disjoint subfamilies $\mathcal{V}_1, \mathcal{V}_2 \subseteq \mathcal{U}$ with $\mathcal{V}_1 \cup \mathcal{V}_2 = \mathcal{U}$ (up to refinement) such that both $\mathcal{V}_1, \mathcal{V}_2 \in \mathcal{V}$.

In particular, $\mathrm{Split}(\Lambda,\Lambda)$ means that every large open cover of the space can be partitioned into two disjoint large subcovers.

Question: Assume that $X$ is a compact topological space and $Y$ is a topological space satisfying $\mathrm{Split}(\Lambda,\Lambda)$. Must the product space $X \times Y$ satisfy $\mathrm{Split}(\Lambda,\Lambda)$?

Substantial progress has been made on global well-posedness for the Boltzmann equation with large-amplitude initial data: Duan–Huang–Wang–Yang (2017) and subsequent works established global existence and uniqueness of mild solutions in the whole space, torus, and bounded domains under bounded velocity-weighted L∞ norms with smallness only of certain L¹_x L∞_v norms and defect mass/energy/entropy, allowing large-amplitude oscillations. Let G be a finite graph with vertex set {1, 2, ..., n} and edge set E(G). For an integer d ≥ 1, the configuration space of G in R^d is B_d(G) := (R^d)^n, whose points are realizations P = (p_1, ..., p_n) with p_i ∈ R^d.

For a realization P ∈ B_d(G), a self-stress on (G, P) is an assignment w : E(G) → R of weights w_{ij} to the edges {i,j} ∈ E(G) satisfying the equilibrium condition at every vertex i:
   sum over j with {i,j} ∈ E(G) of w_{ij} (p_j − p_i) = 0.
The set W(G, P) of all self-stresses is a real vector space, called the self-stress space at P.

Define an equivalence relation on B_d(G) as follows. Two realizations P and P' are equivalent if there is a sign-preserving homeomorphism between W(G, P) and W(G, P'); that is, a homeomorphism ϕ : W(G, P) → W(G, P') such that for every edge e ∈ E(G) and every w ∈ W(G, P), the sign of ϕ(w)(e) equals the sign of w(e) (with sign 0 preserved as 0). The equivalence classes form a stratification of B_d(G), and one records both the strata (organized by dimension) and the adjacency relations between strata (which strata lie in the closure of which).

Problem. Describe explicitly the combinatorial structure of these stratifications in the following three cases:
(a) G = K_6 and d = 2 (the complete graph on 6 vertices in the plane);
(b) G = K_4 and d = 3 (the complete graph on 4 vertices in 3-space);
(c) G = K_5 and d = 3 (the complete graph on 5 vertices in 3-space).
For each case, list all strata of every dimension and determine the adjacency relations among them.

Consider configurations of $n$ labeled points $p_1, \ldots, p_n$ in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. A (planar) tensegrity on such a configuration is an assignment of real weights ("stresses") $w_{ij} = w_{ji}$ to (a subset of) the pairs $\{i,j\}$ such that the equilibrium condition
$$\sum_{j \neq i} w_{ij}(p_j - p_i) = 0$$
holds at every point $p_i$. For a fixed graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, the set of nonzero self-stresses supported on $G$ for a given configuration forms a real vector space whose dimension depends on the configuration. The configuration space $(\mathbb{R}^2)^n$ is thereby decomposed (stratified) according to the dimensions of these self-stress spaces (equivalently, the rank pattern of the rigidity/stress matrix); each piece of this decomposition is called a stratum, and two strata have the same "type" if they correspond to the same combinatorial/algebraic data of admissible self-stresses.

Problem: For every positive integer $n$, determine the number of distinct types of strata that arise in this stratification of the configuration space of $n$ labeled points in the plane.

For a Tychonoff space $X$, let $C_p(X)$ denote the space of continuous real-valued functions on $X$ equipped with the topology of pointwise convergence (i.e., as a subspace of $\mathbb{R}^X$). Write $\mathbf{0} \in C_p(X)$ for the constant zero function, and let $\Gamma_{\mathbf{0}}$ denote the collection of all countably infinite subsets $A \subseteq C_p(X)$ such that every neighborhood of $\mathbf{0}$ contains all but finitely many elements of $A$ (equivalently, $A$, enumerated as a sequence, converges to $\mathbf{0}$).

A topological space $Y$ (with a distinguished point, here $\mathbf{0}$) is said to satisfy the selection principle $\mathsf{S}_1(\Gamma_{\mathbf{0}}, \Gamma_{\mathbf{0}})$ if for every sequence $(A_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with each $A_n \in \Gamma_{\mathbf{0}}$, one can pick a point $a_n \in A_n$ for each $n$ such that $\{a_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \in \Gamma_{\mathbf{0}}$.

Let $\mathfrak{b}$ denote the bounding number: the least cardinality of an unbounded family in $(\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}, \leq^*)$, where $f \leq^* g$ means $f(n) \leq g(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$.

Let $n \geq 2$ and consider $n$ labeled points $p_1,\dots,p_n$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (typically $d=2$). A tensegrity framework on these points with underlying graph $G$ is an assignment of a real "stress" coefficient $w_{ij}$ to each edge $\{i,j\}$ of $G$ such that the equilibrium condition
$$\sum_{j:\{i,j\}\in E(G)} w_{ij}(p_j-p_i)=0$$
holds at every vertex $i$. For a fixed graph $G$, the configuration space $\Omega_G$ is the set of point configurations $(p_1,\dots,p_n)$ that admit a nonzero self-stress, and it carries a natural stratification by the dimension of the space of self-stresses (equivalently, by the combinatorial type of the equilibrium condition). The codimension of a stratum is its codimension inside the ambient configuration space.

A stratum $S$ of codimension greater than $1$ is said to be "obtainable from codimension-$1$ strata" if there exist codimension-$1$ strata $S_1,\dots,S_k$ such that $S$ is contained in (a component of) the intersection of their closures $\overline{S_1}\cap\cdots\cap\overline{S_k}$, and equals such an intersection set-theoretically.

Problem: Identify and classify all strata of $\Omega_G$ (over all graphs $G$) of codimension strictly greater than $1$ that cannot be obtained as set-theoretic intersections of closures of codimension-$1$ strata.

Let X be a Tychonoff topological space, and let C_p(X) denote the space of all real-valued continuous functions on X equipped with the topology of pointwise convergence. Fix the constant function 0 ∈ C_p(X) as a basepoint.

Definitions of covering families on X:
- An open cover U of X is an ω-cover if X ∉ U and every finite subset of X is contained in some member of U. Let Ω denote the family of open ω-covers of X.
- An open cover U of X is a γ-cover if it is infinite and every x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of U. Let Γ denote the family of open γ-covers of X.

Definitions of families at 0 in C_p(X):
- A set A ⊆ C_p(X) \ {0} is an Ω₀-set if 0 belongs to the closure of A in C_p(X); equivalently, every basic neighborhood of 0 meets A. Let Ω₀ be the collection of all such sets.
- A sequence (f_n) in C_p(X) \ {0} is in Γ₀ if it converges pointwise to 0; equivalently, viewed as a set, every basic neighborhood of 0 contains all but finitely many of its elements. Let Γ₀ denote this family.

Selection principle S₁(A, B): A space (or pointed space) has property S₁(A, B) if for every sequence (A_n : n ∈ ω) with each A_n ∈ A, one can choose b_n ∈ A_n such that {b_n : n ∈ ω} ∈ B.

Question: For every Tychonoff space X, is the property S₁(Γ₀, Ω₀) of C_p(X) equivalent to the property S₁(Γ, Ω) of X?

Setup. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph with $n=|V|$ vertices. A planar configuration of $G$ is a map $p\colon V\to\mathbb{R}^2$ assigning to each vertex $v_i$ a point $p_i\in\mathbb{R}^2$. Identify the configuration space of $G$ in the plane with $B_2(G)=(\mathbb{R}^2)^V$ (or, equivalently, with the configuration space of the complete graph $B_2(K_n)$ when one ignores the edge structure of $G$).

A self-stress (or equilibrium stress) on $G$ at $p$ is an assignment of real weights $w_{ij}=w_{ji}$ to the edges $\{v_i,v_j\}\in E$ such that, for every vertex $v_i$,
$$\sum_{j:\,\{v_i,v_j\}\in E} w_{ij}\,(p_j-p_i)=0.$$
A tensegrity is a configuration $p$ together with a self-stress $w$ in which the signs of the weights are prescribed (cables, struts, bars). The tensegrity stratification of $B_2(G)$ is the partition of the configuration space according to the sign pattern (and the dimension of the space) of self-stresses supported on $G$ at $p$. Each stratum is a semi-algebraic subset of $B_2(G)$, and one defines the codimension-$1$ strata in the usual way (those of codimension exactly $1$ in $B_2(G)$).

The (planar) Cayley algebra is the algebraic system whose elements are points and lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$, equipped with two partial operations: the join $\vee$ which sends a pair of points to the line through them, and the meet $\wedge$ which sends a pair of lines to their intersection point. A Cayley algebra system is a finite system of equalities/incidence conditions built from variable points (the $p_i$) and from terms obtained by iterated application of $\vee$ and $\wedge$; its solution set is the locus in $B_2(G)$ of configurations $p$ satisfying all conditions of the system. A finite collection of Cayley algebra systems is said to describe a subset $S\subseteq B_2(G)$ if $S$ equals the union of the solution sets of these systems.

Setup. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph with $n=|V|$ vertices. A planar configuration of $G$ is a map $p\colon V\to\mathbb{R}^2$ assigning to each vertex $v_i$ a point $p_i\in\mathbb{R}^2$. Identify the configuration space of $G$ in the plane with $B_2(G)=(\mathbb{R}^2)^V$ (or, equivalently, with the configuration space of the complete graph $B_2(K_n)$ when one ignores the edge structure of $G$).

A self-stress (or equilibrium stress) on $G$ at $p$ is an assignment of real weights $w_{ij}=w_{ji}$ to the edges $\{v_i,v_j\}\in E$ such that, for every vertex $v_i$,
$$\sum_{j:\,\{v_i,v_j\}\in E} w_{ij}\,(p_j-p_i)=0.$$
A tensegrity is a configuration $p$ together with a self-stress $w$ in which the signs of the weights are prescribed (cables, struts, bars). The tensegrity stratification of $B_2(G)$ is the partition of the configuration space according to the sign pattern (and the dimension of the space) of self-stresses supported on $G$ at $p$. Each stratum is a semi-algebraic subset of $B_2(G)$, and one defines the codimension-$1$ strata in the usual way (those of codimension exactly $1$ in $B_2(G)$).

For each neighborhood $U$ of $e$, let $\mathcal{C}_U = \{gU : g \in G\}$ be the cover of $G$ by left translates of $U$, and let $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{nbd}}(G) = \{\mathcal{C}_U : U \text{ a neighborhood of } e\}$. Let $\mathcal{O}(G)$ denote the family of all open covers of $G$.

Recall Scheepers' selection principle $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with each $\mathcal{U}_n \in \mathcal{A}$, there exist finite subfamilies $\mathcal{F}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \mathcal{F}_n \in \mathcal{B}$.

A topological group $G$ is said to satisfy $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{nbd}}, \mathcal{O})$ if, for every sequence $(U_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of neighborhoods of $e$, there exist finite subsets $F_n \subseteq G$ such that $\{f U_n : n \in \mathbb{N},\ f \in F_n\}$ is an open cover of $G$.

Let $S$ be the closed unit square in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ with side length $\ell>0$, and let $K=\partial S$ denote its boundary (the union of its four sides). A subset $C\subseteq S$ is called an opaque barrier for $S$ if every straight line in $\mathbb{R}^2$ that intersects $K$ also intersects $C$. For a sufficiently regular set $C$ (for example, a finite union of rectifiable curves), let $\mathcal{L}(C)$ denote its one-dimensional Hausdorff measure (total length).

Determine
$$ m(\ell) \;=\; \inf\bigl\{\,\mathcal{L}(C)\;:\; C\subseteq S\text{ is an opaque barrier for }S\,\bigr\}, $$
and exhibit a curve (or finite system of curves) $C^\star\subseteq S$ that attains this infimum, or prove that no minimizer exists. In particular, decide whether the configuration consisting of the Steiner minimal tree of three vertices of the square together with the segment joining the fourth vertex to the center—of total length $\sqrt{2}+\tfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\,\ell$ when $\ell=1$—is optimal.

Let $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{nbd}}$ denote the family of covers of $G$ of the form $\{gU : g \in G\}$ where $U$ is a neighborhood of the identity, and let $\mathcal{O}$ denote the family of open covers of $G$. Let $\Omega_{\mathrm{nbd}}$ denote the family of $\omega$-covers consisting of left translates of identity neighborhoods (i.e., covers $\mathcal{U}\subseteq \mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{nbd}}$ such that every finite subset of $G$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{U}$), and let $\Gamma$ denote the family of $\gamma$-covers (infinite open covers in which every point of $G$ belongs to all but finitely many members).

Recall the selection principles:
\begin{itemize}
\item $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\omega}$ with $\mathcal{U}_n \in \mathcal{A}$, there exist finite subsets $\mathcal{F}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_n \mathcal{F}_n \in \mathcal{B}$.

\end{itemize}

Let $S$ be the closed unit square in the Euclidean plane, with side length $\ell>0$ (take $\ell=1$ for normalization). A subset $C\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is called an opaque barrier (or opaque set) for $S$ if $C$ is a finite union of rectifiable curves and every straight line in the plane that meets $S$ also meets $C$. The length $|C|$ is the sum of the one-dimensional Hausdorff measures of its components.

For an integer $n\ge 1$, let
$$L_n \;=\; \inf\bigl\{\,|C|\;:\; C \text{ is an opaque barrier for } S \text{ consisting of at most } n \text{ connected components}\bigr\}.$$
The shortest known opaque barrier (using two components: the Steiner tree of three vertices of $S$ together with a segment from the fourth vertex to the center) has length
$$\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}\,\ell \;=\;\bigl(\sqrt{2}+\tfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\bigr)\ell \;\approx\; 2.6389\,\ell.$$

Questions:
(a) Does there exist an integer $n\ge 3$ and an opaque barrier for $S$ with at most $n$ connected components whose total length is strictly less than $\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}\,\ell$?
(b) Is the sequence $(L_n)_{n\ge 1}$ strictly decreasing for all sufficiently large $n$, so that
$$L_\infty := \inf_{n\ge 1} L_n \;<\; L_n \quad\text{for every }n,$$
i.e., the infimum length over opaque barriers with finitely many components is not attained by any single barrier with a bounded number of components?

Let $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}$ denote the Baer–Specker group, equipped with its standard Polish group topology (the product topology with $\mathbb{Z}$ discrete). For an open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of a topological space $X$, recall the Scheepers selection principles:
- $\mathsf{S}_1(\mathcal{O},\mathcal{O})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of open covers of $X$ there exist $U_n\in\mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{U_n:n\in\mathbb{N}\}$ is an open cover of $X$ (Rothberger's property).
- $\mathsf{S}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O},\mathcal{O})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of open covers of $X$ there exist finite $\mathcal{F}_n\subseteq\mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_n \mathcal{F}_n$ is an open cover of $X$ (Menger's property).

A set $X$ in a Polish group $(G,\cdot)$ with a left-invariant metric has strong measure zero if for every sequence $(\varepsilon_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of positive reals there exist sets $A_n\subseteq G$ of diameter at most $\varepsilon_n$ with $X\subseteq\bigcup_n A_n$.

A subset $X\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}$ is unbounded if it is unbounded with respect to the eventual-domination order $\le^*$ on $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}$ (equivalently, on $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ after taking absolute values).

Question: Is it consistent with ZFC that there exists a subgroup $G\le\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}$ such that
1. $G$ has strong measure zero,
2. $G$ satisfies $\mathsf{S}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O},\mathcal{O})$,
3. $G$ is unbounded in $(\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}},\le^*)$, and
4. $G$ does not satisfy $\mathsf{S}_1(\mathcal{O},\mathcal{O})$?

Let $\Gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a connected one-dimensional rectifiable set (an "armature"; e.g., a finite connected union of rectifiable arcs) of prescribed total one-dimensional length $\mathcal{H}^1(\Gamma) = L > 0$. Let $\operatorname{conv}(\Gamma)$ denote its convex hull and $\operatorname{vol}_3$ the three-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Consider the optimization problem
$$ V(L) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{\,\operatorname{vol}_3(\operatorname{conv}(\Gamma)) : \Gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^3 \text{ connected, } \mathcal{H}^1(\Gamma)=L\,\bigr\}. $$
A candidate extremal armature is the helical arc $\Gamma^*$ (Nudel'man curve) given parametrically (up to scaling so that its length equals $L$) by
$$ x(t) = \cos t,\quad y(t)=\sin t,\quad z(t) = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,t, \qquad t \in [0, 2\pi]. $$
Prove or disprove: this helical arc $\Gamma^*$ attains the supremum $V(L)$, i.e., it is a global maximizer of the convex-hull volume among all connected one-dimensional armatures of total length $L$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

Let $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}$ denote the Baer–Specker group, i.e., the topological group of all integer sequences with pointwise addition, endowed with the product topology (each copy of $\mathbb{Z}$ being discrete). For a topological space $X$:

- An open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is an $\omega$-cover if $X \notin \mathcal{U}$ and every finite subset of $X$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{U}$.
- An open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is a $\gamma$-cover if it is infinite and every $x \in X$ belongs to all but finitely many members of $\mathcal{U}$.
- Let $\Omega$ (resp. $\Gamma$) denote the family of all open $\omega$-covers (resp. open $\gamma$-covers) of $X$.
- A countable Borel cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is a Borel $\omega$-cover if every finite subset of $X$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{U}$, and a Borel $\gamma$-cover if every $x \in X$ is in all but finitely many members. Let $\mathcal{B}_\Omega$ (resp. $\mathcal{B}_\Gamma$) denote the families of countable Borel $\omega$-covers (resp. $\gamma$-covers).
- For families $\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}$ of covers, $S_1(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B})$ is the selection principle: for every sequence $(U_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with $U_n \in \mathcal{A}$, one can choose $u_n \in U_n$ such that $\{u_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \in \mathcal{B}$.

Question: Assuming the Continuum Hypothesis, does there exist a subgroup $G \leq \mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}$ of cardinality $\mathfrak{c}$ (with the subspace topology) such that $G$ satisfies $S_1(\mathcal{B}_\Omega, \mathcal{B}_\Gamma)$? Failing that, must there at least exist such a subgroup satisfying $S_1(\Omega, \Gamma)$?

Let $S \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the unit sphere, viewed as an opaque body: a point $p \in S$ "sees" a point $q \in \mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \mathrm{int}(B)$ (where $B$ is the closed unit ball bounded by $S$) if the open line segment from $p$ to $q$ does not intersect the interior of $B$. Equivalently, $q$ is visible from $p$ if and only if $q$ lies in the closed half-space $H_p = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \langle x - p, p\rangle \ge 0\}$ tangent to $S$ at $p$.

A rectifiable curve $\gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \mathrm{int}(B)$ (not assumed closed and not assumed connected to anything) is said to be visible from every point of the sphere if for every $p \in S$ there exists a point $q \in \gamma$ with $q \in H_p$, i.e. $\gamma \cap H_p \neq \emptyset$.

Determine
$$
L^* \;=\; \inf \bigl\{\, \mathrm{length}(\gamma) \;:\; \gamma \text{ is a rectifiable curve in } \mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \mathrm{int}(B) \text{ visible from every point of } S \,\bigr\},
$$
and exhibit (or characterize) a curve attaining this infimum, if one exists.

Work in ZFC. Let ω denote the natural numbers, and for A,B ⊆ ω write A ⊆* B (A is almost contained in B) when A \ B is finite. A family F ⊆ [ω]^ω of infinite subsets of ω is called centered if every finite subfamily has infinite intersection. A pseudo-intersection of F is an infinite set A ⊆ ω with A ⊆* B for every B ∈ F. A family L ⊆ [ω]^ω is said to linearly refine F (modulo finite) if L is linearly ordered by ⊆*, and for every B ∈ F there exists A ∈ L with A ⊆* B.

Define:
 • p = the minimal cardinality of a centered family F ⊆ [ω]^ω which has no pseudo-intersection (the pseudo-intersection number);
 • p* = the minimal cardinality of a centered family F ⊆ [ω]^ω which is not linearly refinable modulo finite, i.e. admits no linearly (⊆*-) ordered refining family.

Decide whether p = p* is provable in ZFC.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The cardinal p* was renamed lr (the linear refinement number). Machura, Shelah and Tsaban (Fundamenta Mathematicae, "The linear refinement number and selection theory", 2014) proved that it is consistent that p < lr < c, and in particular that p < p*. Hence p = p* is not a theorem of ZFC; the question is resolved in the negative.

Let f: R^n -> R be twice continuously differentiable and bounded below, with gradient g = ∇f assumed to be Lipschitz continuous on the level set of the starting point. Consider the quasi-Newton iteration

  x_{k+1} = x_k + α_k d_k,   d_k = -B_k^{-1} g(x_k),

where {B_k} is updated by the Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno (BFGS) formula

  B_{k+1} = B_k - (B_k s_k s_k^T B_k)/(s_k^T B_k s_k) + (y_k y_k^T)/(y_k^T s_k),

with s_k = x_{k+1} - x_k and y_k = g(x_{k+1}) - g(x_k), and where the step size α_k > 0 is chosen by the weak Wolfe–Powell (WWP) line search: there exist constants 0 < δ < σ < 1 such that

  f(x_k + α_k d_k) ≤ f(x_k) + δ α_k g(x_k)^T d_k,
  g(x_k + α_k d_k)^T d_k ≥ σ g(x_k)^T d_k.

It is known that for general nonconvex f the standard BFGS method under the WWP line search may fail to converge (counterexamples are known).

Question: Does there exist a variant of the BFGS quasi-Newton method (for instance, using a projection-type modification of the iterates and/or a modification of the WWP line search and/or the update formula) that, under standard regularity assumptions on f (twice continuous differentiability, lower boundedness, Lipschitz continuous gradient) but without assuming convexity, satisfies the global convergence property

  liminf_{k → ∞} ‖g(x_k)‖ = 0   (or, stronger, lim_{k → ∞} ‖g(x_k)‖ = 0)?

Consider the following projection-based reformulation of an unconstrained optimization problem. Given a smooth objective function $f:\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ that is bounded below by some constant $m$ (so $f(x) \geq m$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$), associate to $f$ the "projection paraboloid"
$$P_f = \{(x,t) \in \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R} : t \geq \|x\|^2 + (f(x) - m)\},$$
or, more generally, a paraboloid-type surface
$$S_\phi = \{(x,t) : t = \phi(x) + f(x)\},$$
where $\phi:\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is a strictly convex quadratic ("paraboloid") auxiliary function. The minimization of $f$ is then reformulated as a projection problem onto $S_\phi$ (or onto $P_f$) from a suitably chosen point in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$.

Question: Within this projection framework, does there exist a choice of paraboloid $\phi$ (or, equivalently, of projection paraboloid $P_f$) that is provably better — in terms of convergence rate, conditioning, or computational efficiency of the resulting projection-based algorithm — than the canonical isotropic choice $\phi(x) = \|x\|^2$? If so, exhibit such a paraboloid and quantify the improvement; if not, prove optimality of the isotropic choice within a specified class of admissible paraboloids.

Let $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ denote the Baire space of functions from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{N}$, equipped with the product topology and the preorder $\le^*$ of eventual dominance: $f \le^* g$ iff $f(n) \le g(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$.

For a topological space $X$, an open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is called an $\omega$-cover if $X \notin \mathcal{U}$ and every finite subset of $X$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{U}$. Let $\mathcal{O}$ denote the collection of all open covers of $X$ and $\Omega$ the collection of all $\omega$-covers. The selection principle $\mathsf{U}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O},\Omega)$ asserts that for every sequence $\langle \mathcal{U}_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\rangle$ of open covers of $X$, none of which contains a finite subcover of $X$, there exist finite sets $\mathcal{F}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{\bigcup \mathcal{F}_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is an $\omega$-cover of $X$.

Suppose $X$ is a topological space that satisfies $\mathsf{U}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O},\Omega)$, and let $Y \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ be a continuous image of $X$. Define
$$G = \{\, g \in \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}} : \exists k\in\mathbb{N}\ \exists f_1,\dots,f_k \in Y,\ g \le^* \max\{f_1,\dots,f_k\}\,\}.$$

Must $G$ (with the subspace topology inherited from $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$) also satisfy $\mathsf{U}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O},\Omega)$?

Consider the full nonlinear microwave-heating model in a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ³ with smooth boundary, on a time interval (0,T). The unknowns are the electric field E(x,t), the magnetic field H(x,t), and the temperature θ(x,t), satisfying Maxwell's equations coupled with the heat equation:

  ε ∂E/∂t − ∇ × H + σ(θ) E = 0   in Ω × (0,T),
  μ ∂H/∂t + ∇ × E = 0           in Ω × (0,T),
  ρ c ∂θ/∂t − ∇·(k ∇θ) = q(θ) σ(θ) |E|²   in Ω × (0,T),

together with standard initial conditions E(·,0)=E₀, H(·,0)=H₀, θ(·,0)=θ₀, the perfect-conductor boundary condition E × n = 0 on ∂Ω × (0,T), and a boundary condition for θ (e.g. θ = θ_b or k ∂θ/∂n + h(θ−θ_b) = 0) on ∂Ω × (0,T). Here ε, μ, ρ, c, k > 0 are given constants (or smooth positive functions), and the electrical conductivity σ : ℝ → (0,∞) and the thermal absorptivity q : ℝ → (0,∞) are given continuous, bounded, positive functions of the temperature θ.

Existence of a weak solution (E, H, θ) to this coupled system can be obtained via a Galerkin approximation combined with the Schauder fixed point theorem. The question is:

Under these hypotheses on σ(θ) and q(θ) (both genuinely temperature-dependent, with no monotonicity or smallness assumption beyond continuity and positive bounds), is the weak solution (E, H, θ) of the coupled Maxwell–heat system unique?

Existence of weak/global solutions for Maxwell's equations coupled with the heat equation under temperature-dependent electrical conductivity (and related variants with temperature-dependent permittivity) has been established in several works (e.g., Yin's results on Maxwell's equations in an electromagnetic field with temperature effect, and the coupled heat–Maxwell system with temperature-dependent permittivity). Let $S$ be a semitopological semigroup (a semigroup endowed with a Hausdorff topology such that for each $s\in S$ the maps $t\mapsto st$ and $t\mapsto ts$ are continuous on $S$). Let $\mathrm{CB}(S)$ denote the space of bounded continuous real-valued functions on $S$ with the supremum norm, and for $s\in S$ and $f\in \mathrm{CB}(S)$ define $(\ell_s f)(t)=f(st)$. The space $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ of left uniformly continuous bounded functions on $S$ consists of all $f\in \mathrm{CB}(S)$ for which the map $s\mapsto \ell_s f$ from $S$ into $\mathrm{CB}(S)$ is norm continuous. A left invariant mean (LIM) on $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ is a continuous linear functional $m$ on $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ with $m(1)=\|m\|=1$ such that $m(\ell_s f)=m(f)$ for every $s\in S$ and every $f\in \mathrm{LUC}(S)$.

Say that $S$ has the fixed point property $(\mathrm{fpp}^*)$ if the following holds: whenever $E$ is a Banach space, $C$ is a nonempty weak$^*$-compact convex subset of the dual space $E^*$, and $\mathcal{S}=\{T_s:s\in S\}$ is a representation of $S$ as norm-nonexpansive self-mappings of $C$ (i.e., $T_{st}=T_s\circ T_t$ for all $s,t\in S$ and $\|T_s x-T_s y\|\le \|x-y\|$ for all $x,y\in C$, $s\in S$) such that the action map $(s,x)\mapsto T_s(x)$ from $S\times C$ to $C$ is jointly continuous when $C$ carries the weak$^*$ topology, then there exists $x_0\in C$ with $T_s x_0=x_0$ for every $s\in S$.

Question: Does every semitopological semigroup $S$ for which $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ admits a left invariant mean necessarily have property $(\mathrm{fpp}^*)$?

Work in the real line $\mathbb{R}$ with its usual topology and Lebesgue measure. A set $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ is called:

- meager-additive if for every meager set $M\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, the algebraic sum $X+M=\{x+m:x\in X,\,m\in M\}$ is again meager;
- null-additive if for every Lebesgue null set $N\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, the algebraic sum $X+N$ is again Lebesgue null.

A subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$ is called meager-additive (respectively null-additive) if the same definition holds with $\mathbb{R}$ replaced by $\mathbb{R}^2$, addition being coordinate-wise, and meagerness (respectively Lebesgue nullness) taken in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Question. Suppose $X,Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}$.

(a) If $X$ and $Y$ are both meager-additive, must the Cartesian product $X\times Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ be meager-additive?

(b) If $X$ and $Y$ are both null-additive, must $X\times Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ be null-additive?

Setup. Let $A$ be an F-algebra in the following sense: $A$ is a Banach algebra that is the unique predual of a $W^*$-algebra $M$, so that $M = A^*$, and the identity $1$ of $M$ is a multiplicative linear functional on $A$. Define
$$P(A) = \{\varphi \in A : \|\varphi\| = \langle 1, \varphi\rangle = 1\}.$$
For $\varphi \in A$ and $f \in M$, define $\varphi \cdot f \in M$ by $\langle \psi, \varphi \cdot f\rangle = \langle \psi\varphi, f\rangle$ for all $\psi \in A$.

A topological left invariant mean (TLIM) on $A$ is an element $m \in M^*$ with $\|m\| = 1$ such that
$$\langle m, \varphi \cdot f\rangle = \langle m, f\rangle \quad \text{for all } f \in M \text{ and all } \varphi \in P(A).$$
The algebra $A$ is called left amenable if there exists at least one TLIM on $A$. Let $\mathrm{TLIM}(A) \subseteq M^*$ denote the (convex) set of all TLIMs on $A$.

Problem. Suppose $A$ is a left amenable F-algebra. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $A$ under which the linear span of $\mathrm{TLIM}(A)$ in $M^*$ is finite dimensional.

Let $S_2$ be the partially bicyclic semigroup with identity $e$ generated by elements $a, b, c$ subject to the relations $ab = e$ and $ac = e$ (so $S_2 = \langle e, a, b, c \mid ab = e,\ ac = e\rangle$).

Let $E$ be a Banach space with dual $E^*$. A representation of $S_2$ on a subset $C \subseteq E^*$ is a family $\mathcal{S} = \{T_s : s \in S_2\}$ of mappings $T_s : C \to C$ such that $T_e = \mathrm{id}_C$ and $T_{st} = T_s \circ T_t$ for all $s, t \in S_2$. The representation is called norm nonexpansive if $\|T_s x - T_s y\| \leq \|x - y\|$ for every $s \in S_2$ and all $x, y \in C$.

A semigroup $S$ is said to have the fixed point property $(\mathrm{fpp}^*_s)$ if, for every Banach space $E$ and every nonempty, norm-separable, weak* compact convex subset $C$ of $E^*$, every norm nonexpansive representation $\mathcal{S} = \{T_s : s \in S\}$ of $S$ on $C$ such that the action map $(s, x) \mapsto T_s(x)$ from $S \times C \to C$ is jointly continuous when $C$ carries the weak* topology of $E^*$, has a common fixed point in $C$ (i.e., there exists $x_0 \in C$ with $T_s x_0 = x_0$ for all $s \in S$).

Question: Does the partially bicyclic semigroup $S_2$ have the fixed point property $(\mathrm{fpp}^*_s)$?

Let $G$ be a connected semisimple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional algebraic $G$-module such that the stabilizer in $G$ of a point in general position of $V$ is trivial. Given an automorphism $\sigma\colon G\to G$, define ${}^{\sigma}V$ to be the same underlying variety $V$ equipped with the new $G$-action $G\times V\to V$, $(g,v)\mapsto \sigma(g)\cdot v$. Two $G$-varieties $X$ and $Y$ are called birationally $G$-isomorphic if there exists a $G$-equivariant birational isomorphism between them.

Do there exist such a connected semisimple $G$, a finite-dimensional algebraic $G$-module $V$ with trivial generic stabilizer, and an automorphism $\sigma$ of $G$ for which $V$ and ${}^{\sigma}V$ are not birationally $G$-isomorphic?

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $G$ be a connected simple algebraic group over $k$ with Lie algebra $\mathrm{Lie}(G)$. Consider $G$ as a $G$-variety via the conjugation action, and consider $\mathrm{Lie}(G)$ as a $G$-variety via the adjoint representation. A dominant rational map $\varphi\colon G \dashrightarrow \mathrm{Lie}(G)$ is called $G$-equivariant if $\varphi(g x g^{-1}) = \mathrm{Ad}(g)\,\varphi(x)$ as rational maps. The degree of such a $\varphi$ is the degree of the induced extension of function fields $[k(G):\varphi^*k(\mathrm{Lie}(G))]$. Define the Cayley degree
$$\mathrm{Cay}(G) \;=\; \min\{\deg(\varphi) : \varphi\colon G \dashrightarrow \mathrm{Lie}(G)\text{ dominant rational }G\text{-equivariant}\}.$$
Determine $\mathrm{Cay}(G)$ for every connected simple algebraic group $G$.
