The question, posed by E. Lindenstrauss, asks for general conditions guaranteeing stiffness of H-actions preserving a geometric structure. While stiffness has been established in several important settings (e.g., Bourgain–Furman–Lindenstrauss–Mozes for non-abelian toral automorphisms, Benoist–Quint for actions on homogeneous spaces of semisimple groups, and recent work of Landesberg–Lee–Lindenstrauss–Oh on horospherical measures for Anosov subgroups), no general characterization is known, and the problem remains open in its full generality.

Let $G$ be a noncompact semisimple real Lie group of real rank one, let $\Gamma \subset G$ be a discrete subgroup (not assumed to be a lattice), and let $U \subset G$ be a horospherical subgroup (i.e., the unipotent radical of a minimal parabolic subgroup of $G$). Consider the right action of $U$ on the homogeneous space $G/\Gamma$, which preserves the class of locally finite Borel (Radon) measures. A $U$-invariant Radon measure $\mu$ on $G/\Gamma$ is called $U$-ergodic if every $U$-invariant Borel set has either zero or locally full $\mu$-measure. Two natural families of such measures are known:

(a) measures supported on a single closed $U$-orbit in $G/\Gamma$ (giving the Haar measure on that orbit), and

(b) measures produced by the harmonic-function construction: starting from a positive $\Gamma$-invariant eigenfunction (a harmonic function with respect to a suitable Laplacian, equivalently a $\Gamma$-conformal density on the boundary of the symmetric space of $G$), one builds an associated $U$-invariant Radon measure on $G/\Gamma$ via the Burger–Roblin / Babillot–Ledrappier construction.

Classify all $U$-ergodic Radon measures on $G/\Gamma$. In particular, determine whether every such measure is either supported on a closed $U$-orbit or arises from the harmonic-function construction described in (b).

The problem has substantial partial progress. In rank one, Sarig proved the classification for horocycle flows on $\mathbb Z^d$-covers of compact hyperbolic surfaces, and Ledrappier–Sarig extended it to regular covers of finite-volume surfaces. Landesberg–Lindenstrauss-type results and work by Landesberg on geometrically infinite quotients (IMRN 2022) further classify horospherical Radon measures under suitable hypotheses (e.g., when the Bowen–Margulis–Sullivan measure is conservative). However, a complete classification for arbitrary discrete subgroups $\Gamma$ of a general rank-one semisimple Lie group is not yet established in full generality, so the question remains partially solved.

representations.normalized:
Let $G=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ and let $\{u_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ denote the one-parameter subgroup
$$u_t=\begin{pmatrix}1 & t\\ 0 & 1\end{pmatrix},$$
acting on quotients $\Gamma\backslash G$ by right translation; this action is the horocycle flow.

Let $\Lambda<G$ be a uniform (cocompact) lattice. A subgroup $\Gamma\trianglelefteq\Lambda$ is called conilpotent if the quotient $\Lambda/\Gamma$ is a nilpotent group. Assume that $\Gamma$ is a normal conilpotent subgroup of $\Lambda$; then $\Gamma$ is a discrete subgroup of $G$ and the right $u_t$-action on $\Gamma\backslash G$ preserves the Haar measure $\mu$ (the $G$-invariant Radon measure inherited from Haar measure on $G$).

For a $u_t$-invariant Radon measure $\mu$ on a standard Borel space carrying the horocycle flow, the centralizer of $u_t$ is the group of invertible nonsingular (Borel) transformations that commute with $u_t$ modulo $\mu$-null sets. The measure $\mu$ is called squashable if its centralizer contains an invertible nonsingular transformation $T$ such that $T_*\mu$ is not a scalar multiple of $\mu$; otherwise $\mu$ is called nonsquashable.

Question: Is the Haar measure on $\Gamma\backslash G$ nonsquashable under the horocycle flow?

Searches surface the work of Babillot–Ledrappier and Sarig classifying ergodic invariant Radon measures for horocycle flows on regular covers of compact hyperbolic surfaces, where squashability is studied for abelian covers (yielding nonsquashability of one distinguished measure). Let $\Gamma$ be a group acting by measure-preserving transformations in one of the following two settings:

(1) $N$ is a connected, simply connected nilpotent Lie group, $\Lambda \subset N$ is a lattice (so that $N/\Lambda$ is a finite-volume nilmanifold), and $\Gamma$ is a "large" (for instance, Zariski dense in the real algebraic group $\mathrm{Aut}(N)$) subgroup of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(N/\Lambda)$ of the nilmanifold.

(2) $G$ is a Lie group, $\Lambda \subset G$ is a lattice, and $\Gamma$ is a "large" subgroup of $G$ (for instance, generating a Zariski dense subgroup with sufficient unipotent structure) acting on $G/\Lambda$ by left translations.

Prove or disprove: in either setting, every ergodic $\Gamma$-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ on the relevant homogeneous space is either
(a) supported on a finite $\Gamma$-orbit, or
(b) the normalized Haar (Lebesgue) measure on the whole space.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The conjecture (attributed to A. Furman) is a measure-rigidity statement that remains open in full generality. Significant partial results exist: for higher-rank abelian actions by toral/nilmanifold automorphisms there are classification theorems under additional hypotheses (positive entropy, TNS conditions, irreducibility) by Katok–Spatzier, Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss, and others; for translation actions, Ratner's theorems handle the case where Γ is generated by unipotents, and recent work of Eskin–Lindenstrauss and Benoist–Quint covers stationary measures under semisimplicity assumptions. Nevertheless, the general Zariski-dense automorphism case (without entropy assumptions) and many translation cases remain unresolved.

representations.normalized:
Let $\phi_t : M \to M$ be a smooth Anosov flow on a compact Riemannian manifold $M$, with hyperbolic splitting $TM = E^s \oplus E^0 \oplus E^u$, where $E^0$ is the one-dimensional bundle tangent to the flow and $E^s$, $E^u$ are the stable and unstable bundles. Suppose that the stable bundle admits a $D\phi_t$-invariant continuous splitting $E^s = E^s_- \oplus E^s_+$ such that vectors in $E^s_+$ are contracted strictly faster (under the forward flow) than vectors in $E^s_-$. Assume that $E^s_+$ is integrable, and let $W^s_+$ denote the resulting "fast stable" foliation of $M$, whose leaves are smooth submanifolds tangent to $E^s_+$.

Describe (classify) all Borel probability measures on $M$ that are invariant and ergodic under the holonomy action of the foliation $W^s_+$ — i.e., the transverse-quasi-invariant measures on $M$ which are invariant under the equivalence relation generated by lying in the same leaf of $W^s_+$, and which are ergodic for this equivalence relation.

This is intended as a nonlinear analog of Ratner's theorem on classification of measures invariant under unipotent flows.

representations.normalized:
Let $G$ be a connected Lie group, $\Gamma \subset G$ a lattice, and $U = \{u(t) : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$ a one-parameter Ad-unipotent subgroup of $G$ (i.e., $\mathrm{Ad}(u(t))$ is a unipotent linear operator on the Lie algebra of $G$ for every $t$). By Ratner's theorem, for every $x \in G/\Gamma$ such that the orbit $Ux$ is dense in $G/\Gamma$, the continuous orbit $\{u(t)x : t \in [0,T]\}$ becomes equidistributed in $G/\Gamma$ (with respect to the $G$-invariant probability measure) as $T \to \infty$.

Prove (or disprove) that for every such $G$, $\Gamma$, $U$, and every $x \in G/\Gamma$ with $\overline{Ux} = G/\Gamma$, the discrete sparse orbit $\{u(t_n) x : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is equidistributed in $G/\Gamma$ when $t_n$ is any of the following sequences:
1. $t_n = \lfloor n^\alpha \rfloor$ for a fixed real $\alpha > 1$;
2. $t_n = \lfloor P(n) \rfloor$ for a fixed non-constant polynomial $P(x) \in \mathbb{R}[x]$;
3. $t_n = p_n$, the $n$-th prime number.

Here equidistribution means that for every $f \in C_c(G/\Gamma)$,
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f(u(t_n)x) \;\longrightarrow\; \int_{G/\Gamma} f\, d\mu \quad \text{as } N \to \infty,$$
where $\mu$ is the $G$-invariant probability measure on $G/\Gamma$.

The problem (a question of Margulis) is known in several special cases but remains open in full generality. Partial results include: equidistribution along $\lfloor n^{1+\gamma}\rfloor$ for small $\gamma > 0$ and along primes in horocycle flows on $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\Gamma$ (Venkatesh; Sarnak–Ubis; Tanis–Vishe), and recent polynomial effective equidistribution results (Lindenstrauss–Mohammadi–Wang and others) that give some sparse equidistribution applications. Let $G$ be a connected Lie group, $\Gamma\subset G$ a lattice, and $\mu$ the $G$-invariant Haar probability measure on $G/\Gamma$. Let $V\subset G$ be a connected Ad-unipotent subgroup (i.e., $\operatorname{Ad}(v)$ is a unipotent linear operator on the Lie algebra of $G$ for every $v\in V$), equipped with a Haar measure $dv$, and write $\operatorname{Vol}(A)=\int_A dv$ for measurable $A\subset V$. Fix $x\in G/\Gamma$ such that the orbit $Vx$ is dense in $G/\Gamma$.

By Ratner's theorem (in the form due to Ratner and Dani–Margulis), for any Følner-type "good" sequence of bounded measurable subsets $A_n\subset V$ with $\operatorname{Vol}(A_n)\to\infty$ and any $f\in C_c(G/\Gamma)$,
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{\operatorname{Vol}(A_n)}\int_{A_n} f(vx)\,dv \;=\; \int_{G/\Gamma} f\,d\mu.$$

Problem: Establish this convergence with an effective (quantitative) error term. More precisely, identify a natural class of "good" sequences $\{A_n\}$ in $V$ (e.g., balls with respect to a fixed left-invariant Riemannian metric on $V$, or boxes in suitable coordinates), and prove that there exist constants $C=C(f,x,G,\Gamma,V)>0$ and $\delta=\delta(G,\Gamma,V)>0$ such that
$$\left|\frac{1}{\operatorname{Vol}(A_n)}\int_{A_n} f(vx)\,dv \;-\; \int_{G/\Gamma} f\,d\mu\right| \;\le\; C\,\mathcal{S}(f)\,\operatorname{Vol}(A_n)^{-\delta},$$
where $\mathcal{S}(f)$ is an appropriate Sobolev-type norm of $f$, with explicit dependence of $C$ on $x$ (for instance via the height/injectivity radius of $x$).

$$U = \{u \in G : a^{-n} u a^{n} \to e \text{ as } n \to +\infty\}$$
be its expanding horospherical subgroup in $G$. Fix a point $x_0 \in L/\Lambda$ such that the orbit $G x_0$ is dense in $L/\Lambda$. Let $\gamma : [0,1] \to U$ be a real-analytic curve, and let $\nu$ be the pushforward of Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$ under the map $t \mapsto \gamma(t) x_0$. Let $\lambda$ denote the (normalized) Haar measure on $L/\Lambda$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the curve $\gamma$ under which the translated measures $a^n \nu$ converge in the weak-$*$ topology to $\lambda$ as $n \to \infty$.

Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer and let $G = \mathrm{SO}(n,1)$, viewed as a connected real Lie group acting by left translations on a finite-volume homogeneous space $L/\Gamma$, where $L$ is a connected real Lie group containing $G$ as a closed subgroup and $\Gamma \subset L$ is a lattice. Fix a one-parameter $\mathbb{R}$-diagonalizable subgroup $\{a_t\}_{t \geq 0} \subset G$ whose expanding horospherical subgroup $U^+$ in $G$ is nontrivial, and let $\varphi : I \to U^+$ be a smooth (or analytic) curve defined on a compact interval $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ which is "generic" in the sense that its image is not contained in any proper subvariety arising from a non-trivial intermediate subgroup (so that the corresponding hypothesis used in Shah's theorem for $L = \mathrm{SO}(m,1)$, $m > n$, is satisfied).

For a fixed point $x_0 \in L/\Gamma$, consider the family of probability measures $\mu_t$ on $L/\Gamma$ obtained by pushing forward the normalized Lebesgue measure on $I$ under the map $s \mapsto a_t \varphi(s) x_0$.

Question: Does $\mu_t$ converge, as $t \to \infty$, in the weak-$*$ topology to the unique $G$-invariant probability measure supported on the closure of the $G$-orbit $G x_0$ in $L/\Gamma$, for every connected real Lie group $L$ containing $G = \mathrm{SO}(n,1)$ (and not only for $L = \mathrm{SO}(m,1)$ with $m > n$)?

Suppose $G$ acts continuously and linearly on $V$, and let $p \in V$ be a point whose stabilizer $\{g \in G : gp = p\}$ is finite. For each $T > 0$, define the "representation ball"
$$R_T = \{ g \in G : \|gp\| < T \},$$
which has finite Haar measure (assume this), and let $\lambda_T$ be the normalized restriction of Haar measure to $R_T$ (a probability measure on $G$).

Let $\Gamma \subset G$ be a lattice, and let $\pi : G \to G/\Gamma$ be the natural projection. Define $\mu_T = \pi_* \lambda_T$, the pushforward probability measure on $G/\Gamma$.

Determine the weak-$*$ limit of $\mu_T$ on $G/\Gamma$ as $T \to \infty$: does the limit exist, and if so, identify it explicitly (e.g., as the $G$-invariant probability measure on $G/\Gamma$, or as a measure supported on a proper homogeneous subspace, in terms of $G$, $V$, the action, and $p$).

For a real number α and a positive integer N, define the (normalized) pair correlation function of the sequence (αn² mod 1)_{n=1}^{N} on an interval [a,b] ⊂ ℝ by
   R_2([a,b], N, α) := (1/N) · #{ 1 ≤ m ≠ n ≤ N : αn² − αm² ∈ (1/N)·[a,b] + ℤ }.
A real number α is called badly approximable (by rationals) if there exists a constant c > 0 such that |α − p/q| > c/q² for every rational p/q.

Question: Is it true that for every badly approximable α ∈ ℝ and every a < b in ℝ,
   R_2([a,b], N, α) → b − a as N → ∞ ?

Let $\mathbb{H} = \{z = x+iy : y>0\}$ denote the upper half-plane with hyperbolic metric, on which $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ acts by Möbius transformations. Let $\Gamma = \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$, let $X = \Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H}$ be the modular surface, and let $T^1(X)$ be its unit tangent bundle, identified with $\Gamma\backslash\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. Let $\lambda$ denote the Liouville (Haar) probability measure on $T^1(X)$. For $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $y>0$, define the horocycle element
$$u_y(t) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & t \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} y^{1/2} & 0 \\ 0 & y^{-1/2} \end{pmatrix},$$
viewed as a point in $T^1(X)$ via the projection $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R}) \to \Gamma\backslash\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. A real number $\alpha$ is called badly approximable by rationals if there exists $c>0$ such that $|\alpha - p/q| \geq c/q^2$ for every $p/q \in \mathbb{Q}$. Fix constants $0 < c_1 < c_2$. Consider continuous functions $f : T^1(X) \to \mathbb{C}$ that satisfy a prescribed growth condition at the cusp ensuring all averages below are well defined (e.g., $|f(g)| \ll y(g)^{1-\delta}$ for some $\delta>0$, where $y(g)$ is the imaginary part of the base point of $g$).

Prove or disprove: for every such $f$ and every badly approximable $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$,
$$\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^M f\bigl(u_y(\alpha m)\bigr) \;\longrightarrow\; \int_{T^1(X)} f\, d\lambda$$
as $M \to \infty$, uniformly in $y$ with $c_1 M^{-2} \leq y \leq c_2 M^{-2}$.

Let $X = \Gamma \backslash G/K$ be a finite-volume Riemannian locally symmetric space of noncompact type, where $G$ is a connected semisimple real Lie group with finite center and no compact factors, $K \subset G$ is a maximal compact subgroup, and $\Gamma \subset G$ is a torsion-free lattice. A flat in $X$ is a connected, complete, totally geodesic immersed submanifold whose induced sectional curvature vanishes identically; a maximal flat has dimension equal to the real rank of $G$. A compact flat in $X$ is a flat (of any dimension $\ge 1$) whose image in $X$ is a compact immersed submanifold, equipped with the induced Riemannian volume.

For $T > 0$, let $N(X, T)$ denote the number of compact (maximal) flats in $X$ of volume at most $T$. Determine the asymptotic behavior of $N(X, T)$ as $T \to \infty$: produce an explicit function $f(T)$ such that
$$N(X, T) \sim f(T) \quad \text{as } T \to \infty,$$
expressed in terms of the geometric and arithmetic invariants of $X$ (such as the real rank, the root system, and the covolume of $\Gamma$).

representations.normalized:
Let $G$ be a connected semisimple real Lie group of real rank at least $2$, let $A\subset G$ be a maximal $\mathbb{R}$-split Cartan subgroup, and let $\Gamma\subset G$ be a torsion-free uniform lattice. A compact flat in $X:=\Gamma\backslash G$ is a closed orbit $F = \Gamma g A \subset X$ that is compact; each such $F$ carries a finite $A$-invariant Haar measure, and we denote by $\mathrm{Vol}(F)$ its volume and by $\mu_F$ the corresponding $A$-invariant probability measure supported on $F$.

For $T>0$, let $\mathcal{F}(T) := \{ F : F \text{ is a compact flat in } X \text{ with } \mathrm{Vol}(F) < T \}$, assumed finite for every $T$. Define the two families of finite Borel measures on $X$:
$$\nu_T := \sum_{F\in\mathcal{F}(T)} \mathrm{Vol}(F)\,\mu_F, \qquad \overline{\nu}_T := \frac{1}{\#\mathcal{F}(T)} \sum_{F\in\mathcal{F}(T)} \mu_F,$$
normalized so as to be probability measures (i.e.\ $\nu_T$ is divided by $\sum_{F\in\mathcal{F}(T)}\mathrm{Vol}(F)$).

Question: As $T\to\infty$, do $\nu_T$ and $\overline{\nu}_T$ converge in the weak-$*$ topology to the normalized $G$-invariant Haar probability measure $m_X$ on $X = \Gamma\backslash G$?

representations.normalized:
Let $G$ be a semisimple real algebraic group defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, let $\Gamma \subset G$ be a noncocompact arithmetic lattice, and let $A \subset G$ be a maximal $\mathbb{R}$-split torus. Let $D \subset A$ be a closed subgroup. A trajectory $\{d \cdot x\Gamma : d \in D\}$ in $G/\Gamma$ is called divergent if the map $D \to G/\Gamma$, $d \mapsto d \cdot x\Gamma$, is proper (i.e. the orbit eventually leaves every compact subset of $G/\Gamma$). A divergent trajectory is called obvious if its divergence can be detected from a finite collection of algebraic ($\mathbb{Q}$-rational) data, namely from the divergence in $\mathbb{R}$ of evaluations of $\mathbb{Q}$-characters of suitable $\mathbb{Q}$-parabolic subgroups along the orbit. Let $\mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$ denote the $\mathbb{Q}$-rank of $G$. Establish the following three statements:

(1) If $\dim D > \mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$, then there are no divergent $D$-orbits in $G/\Gamma$.

(2) If $\dim D = \mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$, then every divergent $D$-trajectory in $G/\Gamma$ is obvious.

(3) If $\dim D < \mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$, then there exist non-obvious divergent $D$-trajectories in $G/\Gamma$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The three-part conjecture has been partially resolved. Part (1) was established by Weiss, showing that any diagonalizable subgroup admitting a divergent trajectory has dimension at most $\mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$. Part (3) (existence of non-obvious divergent trajectories when $\dim D < \mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$) has been established in a modified form via work proving non-obvious divergent trajectories under dimension constraints relative to $\mathbb{Q}$-factors. Part (2) (classification of divergent trajectories as obvious when $\dim D = \mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}} G$) is known in $\mathbb{Q}$-rank two (Tomanov–Weiss, and rank-two arithmetic homogeneous spaces) but the general case remains open.

Let $G$ be a connected Lie group, $\Gamma \subset G$ a lattice, and $A \subset G$ a closed connected abelian subgroup with $\dim A \geq 2$. Fix a left-invariant Riemannian metric on $A$, let $A_T \subset A$ denote the closed ball of radius $T$ about the identity, and let $\lambda$ denote Haar measure on $A$. A one-parameter subgroup of $A$ is a continuous homomorphism $D : \mathbb{R} \to A$ (identified with its image). For $x \in G/\Gamma$, the orbit $Dx$ is said to be divergent in $G/\Gamma$ if the map $t \mapsto D(t)x$ is proper, i.e. eventually leaves every compact subset of $G/\Gamma$.

Suppose $x \in G/\Gamma$ has the property that for every one-parameter subgroup $D$ of $A$, the orbit $Dx$ is not divergent in $G/\Gamma$. Must there exist a compact set $K \subset G/\Gamma$ such that
$$\limsup_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{\lambda(A_T)} \lambda\bigl(\{a \in A_T : ax \in K\}\bigr) > 0\, ?$$

representations.normalized:
Let $n\ge 2$ and consider the homogeneous space $X=\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{Z})$. Let $A\subset\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})$ denote the subgroup of positive diagonal matrices (a maximal $\mathbb{R}$-split Cartan subgroup), and consider the Weyl chamber flow, i.e. the action of $A$ on $X$ by left translations.

For $n=2$, the geodesic flow on $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ admits two classical symbolic codings of its closed orbits (equivalently, conjugacy classes of hyperbolic elements of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$):
(i) the "geometric coding," obtained from a Bowen–Series / boundary-expansion construction associated with a fundamental domain for the Fuchsian group, producing a subshift whose sequences record successive sides of the fundamental domain crossed by the geodesic; and
(ii) the "arithmetic coding," obtained from Gauss's reduction theory of indefinite binary quadratic forms and the minus (or plus) continued fraction expansion, producing a sofic/Markov coding intrinsic to $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$.

Problem. Construct genuine analogs of the geometric coding and of the arithmetic coding for the Weyl chamber flow (the action of the full positive diagonal subgroup $A$) on $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{Z})$ for $n\ge 3$. That is, produce symbolic systems (with explicit alphabets and admissibility rules) together with coding maps that conjugate the $A$-action (or a suitable cross-section of it) to these symbolic systems, generalizing the geometric and arithmetic codings known in the rank-one case $n=2$.

representations.normalized:
Consider a triangle $T \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with interior angles $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3$ (satisfying $\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3=\pi$). The billiard flow on $T$ is the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of $T$, where a point particle moves in straight lines inside $T$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at the boundary. This flow preserves the Liouville measure (the product of Lebesgue measure on $T$ with the uniform measure on the unit circle of directions).

Call a real number $\theta$ Diophantine modulo $2\pi$ if there exist constants $C>0$ and $\tau \geq 0$ such that for every nonzero integer $q$ and every integer $p$,
$$\left| \frac{\theta}{2\pi} - \frac{p}{q} \right| \geq \frac{C}{|q|^{2+\tau}}.$$

Question: Does there exist a triangle whose three angles $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3$ are all Diophantine modulo $2\pi$ and whose billiard flow is ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Ergodicity of polygonal billiards with Diophantine angles is regarded as one of the central open problems in the dynamics of polygonal billiards. While ergodicity is known to hold for a residual (dense $G_\delta$) set of polygons (Kerckhoff–Masur–Smillie, Zemlyakov–Katok), no explicit triangle—let alone one with Diophantine angles—has been shown to be ergodic, and no general approach is known. The problem appears still open as of recent surveys.

representations.normalized:
Consider the billiard flow in a planar polygon $P$: a point particle moves at unit speed inside $P$ along straight lines and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at the boundary. The phase space is the unit tangent bundle of $P$ (with directions identified at the boundary by the reflection law), equipped with the Liouville measure (the product of Lebesgue measure on $P$ and the uniform measure on directions), which is invariant under the flow. The flow is said to be weakly mixing if it has continuous spectrum on the orthogonal complement of the constants in $L^2$ of the Liouville measure.

(a) Does there exist a polygon $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ whose billiard flow is weakly mixing with respect to the Liouville measure?

(b) In particular, are the "Vorobets billiards" — polygons constructed as fast Liouville-type approximations by rational polygons designed to produce strong ergodic behavior — weakly mixing?

Part (a) was answered affirmatively: it has been proved that there exists a residual (dense G-delta) set of non-rational polygons whose billiard flow is weakly mixing with respect to the Liouville measure (Chaika–Forni, "Weakly Mixing Polygonal Billiards", arXiv:2003.00890, 2020). However, whether the specific Vorobets billiards are weakly mixing does not appear to be settled in the literature, so part (b) remains open.

For integers n ≥ 2 and k ≥ 1, a finite word w ∈ Σ* is called a strongly k-abelian n-th power if w can be written as a concatenation w = u_1 u_2 ⋯ u_n with |u_1| = |u_2| = ⋯ = |u_n| and u_i ≡_k u_j for all 1 ≤ i, j ≤ n.

For fixed integers k ≥ 1, n ≥ 2, and an alphabet Σ of size q ≥ 2, determine (exactly or asymptotically as N → ∞) the following two counting functions:

(a) The number f(N) of words w ∈ Σ^N that contain some strongly k-abelian n-th power as a factor.

(b) The number g(N) of words w ∈ Σ^N that are themselves strongly k-abelian n-th powers.

Let $k \geq 2$ be an integer and let $G = \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})^k$. Let
$$U^+ = \left\{\begin{pmatrix} 1 & * \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\right\}^k \subset G, \qquad U^- = \left\{\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ * & 1 \end{pmatrix}\right\}^k \subset G$$
be the subgroups of upper-triangular and lower-triangular unipotent elements, both isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^k$. A lattice $\Lambda$ in $U^\pm \cong \mathbb{R}^k$ is called irreducible if it is not contained in any proper sum of coordinate subspaces (equivalently, no finite-index subgroup of $\Lambda$ splits as a product of lattices in coordinate subgroups). Let $\Gamma^+$ be an irreducible lattice in $U^+$ and $\Gamma^-$ an irreducible lattice in $U^-$.

Assume that the subgroup $\langle \Gamma^+, \Gamma^- \rangle$ of $G$ generated by $\Gamma^+ \cup \Gamma^-$ is discrete. Prove or disprove: $\langle \Gamma^+, \Gamma^- \rangle$ is an arithmetic lattice in $G$.

representations.normalized:
Let $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$ denote the space of real $m\times n$ matrices. A matrix $Y\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$ is called very well approximable (VWA) if there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that the system of inequalities
$$\|Y\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{p}\|^{m} \le \|\mathbf{q}\|^{-n-\varepsilon}$$
has infinitely many solutions $(\mathbf{p},\mathbf{q})\in\mathbb{Z}^{m}\times(\mathbb{Z}^{n}\setminus\{0\})$, where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes a fixed norm. (Equivalently, $Y$ has Diophantine exponent strictly greater than $n/m$.) For $n=1$ this recovers the usual notion of a VWA vector in $\mathbb{R}^{m}$.

For a smooth (e.g. $C^{\infty}$) map of vectors $f:U\to\mathbb{R}^{N}$ defined on a connected open set $U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{k}$, one says that $f$ is nondegenerate at $x_{0}\in U$ if there exists $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ such that the partial derivatives of $f$ at $x_{0}$ of order at most $\ell$ span $\mathbb{R}^{N}$, and $f$ is nondegenerate if it is nondegenerate at almost every $x_{0}\in U$. A classical theorem asserts that whenever $f:U\to\mathbb{R}^{N}$ is nondegenerate, almost every point of $f(U)$ (with respect to Lebesgue measure pushed forward from $U$) fails to be VWA.

Problem. Formulate reasonable and verifiable conditions on a smooth map
$$f:U\subset\mathbb{R}^{k}\longrightarrow M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$$
that generalize the notion of nondegeneracy of vector-valued maps and that imply the following conclusion: for Lebesgue-almost every $x\in U$, the matrix $f(x)\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$ is not very well approximable. In particular, identify checkable geometric/algebraic conditions on $f$ (or on its image submanifold of $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$) under which the pushforward of Lebesgue measure on $U$ by $f$ is an extremal measure on $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$.

Substantial progress has been made. Aka, Breuillard, Rosenzweig, and de Saxcé (GAFA 2018, "Diophantine approximation on matrices and Lie groups") formulate a criterion for extremality of analytic submanifolds of $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$ in terms of algebraic (representation-theoretic) obstructions, showing that the almost-sure Diophantine exponent of an analytic submanifold depends only on its Zariski closure, and giving an effective computation in the rational case. Further work (e.g. Beresnevich–Kleinbock on quantitative non-divergence, and recent papers on systems of small linear forms and twisted approximation on manifolds) provides additional sufficient conditions. However, a fully general clean "nondegeneracy" condition encompassing all known cases for arbitrary smooth maps into $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$ does not yet appear settled in full generality, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question concerns a logarithmically strengthened version of Littlewood's conjecture: whether there exist α, β with q(log q)^{2-ε} ⟨qα⟩⟨qβ⟩ bounded below. Gallagher's theorem shows the set of such pairs has Lebesgue measure zero, but no explicit pair is known. Recent surveys on Littlewood's conjecture (Bugeaud–Moshchevitin, Beresnevich–Velani, Badziahin–Pollington–Velani) discuss this and related strengthenings as open problems; no construction or disproof appears in the literature.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

This is a well-known conjecture of G. Margulis (equivalent in the $n=3$ case to a problem of Cassels and Swinnerton-Dyer) that every bounded orbit of the full diagonal group on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{Z})$ is closed (equivalently, compact). Let $Q$ be a nondegenerate indefinite quadratic form in $d \geq 3$ real variables, and assume that $Q$ is not a scalar multiple of a quadratic form with rational coefficients. By the Oppenheim conjecture (theorem of Margulis), the set of values $\{Q(x) : x \in \mathbb{Z}^d \setminus \{0\}\}$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$; in particular, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ with $0 < |Q(x)| < \varepsilon$.

Provide an effective bound: exhibit an explicit function $T = T(\varepsilon, Q)$ (depending in a quantitatively controlled way on $\varepsilon$ and on natural invariants of $Q$, such as its norm and a Diophantine measure of irrationality) such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ with
$$0 < |Q(x)| < \varepsilon \quad \text{and} \quad \|x\| < T(\varepsilon, Q).$$

The Oppenheim conjecture itself was proved by Margulis (1987), but the original proof is ineffective. Effective bounds have been obtained in special cases: Lindenstrauss–Margulis established an effective estimate for ternary (d=3) irrational indefinite quadratic forms with logarithmic dependence, and subsequent work (Bourgain, Ghosh-Gorodnik-Nevo, and others) has produced effective results for generic or Diophantine forms. $$M_Q(\alpha,\beta) \;=\; \inf_{(x,y) \in \mathbb{Z}^2} |Q(x+\alpha,\, y+\beta)|,$$

where $\Sigma(Q)$ denotes the set of pairs $(\alpha,\beta) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ at which $M_Q$ achieves the global supremum $m(Q)$. Let $K_Q$ denote the splitting field of $Q$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, i.e. the real quadratic field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{b^2-4ac})$.

\begin{enumerate}

\end{enumerate}

Katok constructed a smooth Finsler (non-reversible) metric on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ whose geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle is ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure and possesses exactly two closed (prime) geodesics. Consider the quantization of this geodesic flow (for example, via a sequence of semiclassical operators or Laplace-type operators whose principal symbol generates the flow), and the associated sequence of normalized eigenfunctions $\{\psi_n\}$ with eigenvalues tending to infinity. A "scar" is said to occur along a closed orbit $\gamma$ if some subsequence of the microlocal lifts (Wigner measures) of $\{\psi_n\}$ has a weak-* limit that is not the Liouville measure and assigns positive mass to $\gamma$ (equivalently, the eigenfunctions concentrate, in phase space, on $\gamma$ along the subsequence).

Question: In Katok's Finsler 2-sphere example, do the two closed geodesics correspond to scars, i.e., is there a sequence of eigenfunctions whose microlocal limits charge these closed orbits, despite the classical ergodicity of the geodesic flow?

Katok constructed a smooth Finsler (non-reversible) metric on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ whose geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle is ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure and possesses exactly two closed (prime) geodesics. Consider the quantization of this geodesic flow (for example, via a sequence of semiclassical operators or Laplace-type operators whose principal symbol generates the flow), and the associated sequence of normalized eigenfunctions $\{\psi_n\}$ with eigenvalues tending to infinity. A "scar" is said to occur along a closed orbit $\gamma$ if some subsequence of the microlocal lifts (Wigner measures) of $\{\psi_n\}$ has a weak-* limit that is not the Liouville measure and assigns positive mass to $\gamma$ (equivalently, the eigenfunctions concentrate, in phase space, on $\gamma$ along the subsequence).

Question: In Katok's Finsler 2-sphere example, do the two closed geodesics correspond to scars, i.e., is there a sequence of eigenfunctions whose microlocal limits charge these closed orbits, despite the classical ergodicity of the geodesic flow?

status_assertions.value: open_status:unknown

A web search yields work on Katok's Finsler 2-sphere example, on its ergodicity, and on the existence of exactly two closed geodesics (Bangert–Long), as well as general quantum ergodicity results, but no source directly establishes or refutes the existence of quantum scars on the two closed geodesics in this particular example. The status appears to be unresolved in the accessible literature.

Let $\{\varphi_i\}_{i\ge 1}$ be an orthonormal basis of $L^2(X, dV)$ consisting of eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $X$, with eigenvalues $\lambda_i \to \infty$. For each $i$, define the probability measure
$$\mu_i := |\varphi_i(x)|^2\, dV(x)$$
on $X$. Prove or disprove: $\mu_i \to dV$ weakly as $i \to \infty$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The Quantum Unique Ergodicity conjecture of Rudnick–Sarnak remains open in general for compact negatively curved manifolds. In the arithmetic setting (compact arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces from quaternion algebras, and the modular surface), the conjecture for Hecke eigenfunctions was established by Lindenstrauss (2006) and Soundararajan (for the modular surface, completing the non-compact case). Significant entropy-based partial results in the general case are due to Anantharaman and collaborators, but the full conjecture for arbitrary negatively curved manifolds is unresolved.

Consider a sequence $\{\phi_n\}$ of $L^2$-normalized joint eigenfunctions of $\mathbb{D}(G/K)$ and $\mathcal{H}$ such that the eigenvalues of (some/all of) the differential operators tend to infinity. The conjecture is established in several settings: Lindenstrauss proved it for congruence quotients of the hyperbolic plane (with Soundararajan ruling out escape of mass in the non-compact case), Holowinsky–Soundararajan handled the holomorphic case, and Shem-Tov–Silberman (2022/2025) proved it for products of hyperbolic 2- and 3-spaces. In the general higher-rank arithmetic setting the conjecture remains open.

representations.normalized:
Let $\mathbb{H}^2$ denote the upper half-plane with its standard hyperbolic metric, and let $\Gamma \subset \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ be a noncocompact arithmetic lattice (for example, a congruence subgroup of $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$). Let $X = \Gamma \backslash \mathbb{H}^2$, equipped with the induced hyperbolic Riemannian volume measure $V$. Let $\{\phi_i\}_{i \geq 1}$ be an orthonormal sequence of joint eigenfunctions of the Laplacian and of all Hecke operators on $X$, with Laplace eigenvalues tending to infinity, and let $\mu_i = |\phi_i|^2\, dV$ be the associated probability measures on $X$.

Prove that for every pair of compactly supported continuous functions $f, g \in C_c(X)$ with $\int_X g\, dV \neq 0$,
$$\frac{\int_X f\, d\mu_i}{\int_X g\, d\mu_i} \;\longrightarrow\; \frac{\int_X f\, dV}{\int_X g\, dV} \qquad \text{as } i \to \infty.$$

Equivalently, show that no mass of the sequence $\{\mu_i\}$ escapes to the cusps and that the measures $\mu_i$ equidistribute with respect to the normalized hyperbolic volume on test functions of compact support.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The question is the non-escape-of-mass statement that, combined with Lindenstrauss's measure rigidity, yields arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity on noncocompact arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces. The needed non-escape of mass for Hecke–Maass cusp forms on such surfaces was established by Soundararajan, which together with Lindenstrauss's theorem completes AQUE in this setting. The problem is therefore considered solved for arithmetic surfaces.

Let $(X,g)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold of negative sectional curvature, normalized so that $\mathrm{Vol}(X)=1$. Let $\{\varphi_i\}_{i\ge 1}$ denote an orthonormal basis of $L^2(X)$ consisting of real-valued eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator $-\Delta_g$, with eigenvalues $\lambda_i \to \infty$, and normalized so that $\int_X \varphi_i^2\,d\mathrm{Vol} = 1$.

Prove or disprove that for a generic such metric $g$, the values of the eigenfunctions are asymptotically Gaussian distributed with respect to the Riemannian volume; that is, for every pair of real numbers $a<b$,
$$\mathrm{Vol}\big(\{x\in X : a \le \varphi_i(x) \le b\}\big) \;\longrightarrow\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_a^b e^{-t^2/2}\,dt \qquad \text{as } i\to\infty.$$

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The conjecture is a form of Berry's random wave heuristic for eigenfunctions on negatively curved (or Anosov) manifolds. Recent work (e.g., Ingremeau's "Unimodal value distribution of Laplace eigenfunctions," 2019) establishes related partial results (such as unimodality of value distributions under a gradient-weighted measure and local weak Gaussian limits), but the full Gaussian value distribution under Riemannian volume remains an open conjecture for generic negatively curved compact manifolds.

representations.normalized:
Let $X$ be a compact Riemannian manifold of negative sectional curvature, and let $\Delta$ be the (positive) Laplace–Beltrami operator on $X$. Let $\{\varphi_i\}_{i\geq 1}$ be an orthonormal basis of $L^2(X)$ consisting of eigenfunctions of $\Delta$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_i\to\infty$. Let $S^*X$ denote the unit cosphere bundle with its normalized Liouville measure $\lambda$, and let $(g^t)_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ be the geodesic flow on $S^*X$. For a symbol $a\in C_c^{\infty}(S^*X,\mathbb{R})$, let $\mathrm{Op}(a)$ denote a standard semiclassical/pseudodifferential quantization of $a$. Define
$$\xi_i(a) := \lambda_i^{1/4}\,\big|\langle \mathrm{Op}(a)\varphi_i,\varphi_i\rangle\big|,$$
and the classical autocorrelation
$$V(a) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\!\!\int_{S^*X} a(xg^t)\,a(x)\,d\lambda(x)\,dt.$$
Assume that $\int_{S^*X} a\,d\lambda = 0$. For a "generic" compact negatively curved Riemannian manifold $X$, prove or disprove that:
(1) $\displaystyle \frac{1}{N(\lambda)}\sum_{\lambda_i\leq\lambda}\xi_i(a)^2 \to V(a)$ as $\lambda\to\infty$, where $N(\lambda)=\#\{i:\lambda_i\leq\lambda\}$;
(2) for every interval $I\subset\mathbb{R}$,
$$\frac{1}{N(\lambda)}\,\#\Big\{\lambda_i\leq\lambda : V(a)^{-1/2}\,\xi_i(a)\in I\Big\} \;\longrightarrow\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_I e^{-t^2/2}\,dt.$$

The conjectured Gaussian distribution of quantum variance matrix elements for generic negatively curved manifolds (in the spirit of Feingold–Peres) remains open. Partial results exist (e.g., variance asymptotics by Luo–Sarnak, Zelditch, and CLT for matrix elements in arithmetic settings such as Maass–Hecke cusp forms), but for general generic negatively curved compact manifolds no proof is known.

representations.normalized:
Let $T \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a triangle, and consider the billiard flow on $T$: a point particle moves in straight lines inside $T$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at the boundary. Consider the Laplace–Dirichlet (or Neumann) eigenvalue problem
$$-\Delta \varphi_n = \lambda_n \varphi_n \text{ in } T, \qquad \varphi_n|_{\partial T}=0,$$
with $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions $\varphi_n$ and $\lambda_n \to \infty$. A quantum limit is any weak-$*$ limit point on $T$ (or on the unit cotangent bundle, via microlocal lifts) of the sequence of probability measures $|\varphi_{n_k}(x)|^2\,dx$ along subsequences $\lambda_{n_k}\to\infty$.

A periodic orbit of the billiard flow is a closed trajectory of finite length; it gives rise to a singular invariant measure supported on the corresponding closed curve in $T$ (or on the lift of this curve in phase space). A quantum limit is said to be "scarred" on (or "supported on") a periodic orbit if its support is contained in that closed orbit (equivalently, the limit measure assigns full mass to the orbit).

Question: For a triangular billiard $T$, do there exist quantum limits whose support is contained in a periodic orbit of the billiard flow? Equivalently, do periodic orbits in triangular billiards give rise to scars in the strict sense of producing quantum limit measures supported on those orbits?

representations.normalized:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a polygonal billiard, i.e., a compact connected planar domain whose boundary $\partial P$ is a finite union of line segments. Consider the Dirichlet (or Neumann) Laplacian $-\Delta$ on $P$, whose spectrum consists of eigenvalues $0 < \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \cdots \to \infty$ with corresponding $L^2$-normalized real eigenfunctions $\varphi_n$ satisfying $-\Delta \varphi_n = \lambda_n \varphi_n$. For each $n$, lift $\varphi_n$ to a distribution on the unit cotangent bundle $S^*P$ via its microlocal lift, obtaining a probability measure $\mu_n$ on $S^*P$. A probability measure $\mu$ on $S^*P$ is called a quantum limit if there is a subsequence $n_k \to \infty$ such that $\mu_{n_k} \to \mu$ weakly. Every quantum limit is invariant under the billiard flow on $S^*P$.

Problem: Classify all quantum limits of eigenfunctions of an arbitrary polygonal billiard $P$. That is, characterize the set of all such weak-$*$ limit measures, both for rational polygons (those whose interior angles are rational multiples of $\pi$) and for general polygons.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem appears to remain open in full generality. Marklof and Rudnick (2012) established quantum ergodicity for rational polygons, showing a density-one subsequence of eigenfunctions equidistributes in configuration space, but a complete classification of all quantum limits — including possible exceptional (scarring) sequences and the situation for general (irrational) polygons — has not been achieved. $$N_T((a,b),(c,d)) := \#\Big\{(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in(\mathbb{Z}^2)^3 : a<Q(x_1)-Q(x_2)<b,\ c<Q(x_2)-Q(x_3)<d,\ x_i\neq x_j\text{ for }i\neq j,\ \|x_i\|<T\Big\},$$
where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb{R}^2$. Determine the limiting distribution of the set
$$\{(Q(x_1)-Q(x_2),\,Q(x_2)-Q(x_3)) : x_i\in\mathbb{Z}^2,\ x_i\neq x_j\text{ for }i\neq j\}\subset\mathbb{R}^2,$$
that is, find the asymptotic behavior of $N_T((a,b),(c,d))$ as $T\to\infty$ (after appropriate normalization), thereby describing the triple-spacing/correlation statistics of the values of $Q$ at lattice points.

Let $\mathrm{Sh}_K(G,X)$ be a Shimura variety associated to a Shimura datum $(G,X)$ and a compact open subgroup $K \subset G(\mathbb{A}_f)$, viewed as a quasi-projective variety over $\mathbb{C}$. A special subvariety of $\mathrm{Sh}_K(G,X)$ is an irreducible component of the image of a Shimura subvariety map $\mathrm{Sh}_{K'}(H,X_H) \to \mathrm{Sh}_K(G,X)$ associated to a Shimura sub-datum $(H,X_H)$ of $(G,X)$, possibly translated by a Hecke correspondence. A special point is a special subvariety of dimension zero; equivalently, it is the image of a point $x \in X$ whose Mumford–Tate group is a torus.

Prove or disprove: for any set $\Sigma$ of special points in $\mathrm{Sh}_K(G,X)$, the Zariski closure of $\Sigma$ is a finite union of special subvarieties.

Equip $S(\mathbb{C})$ with its canonical probability measure $\mu_S$ induced by the $G(\mathbb{R})^+$-invariant probability measure on the symmetric domain (the normalized Haar/hyperbolic measure). For a special point $x\in S$, let $O(x)$ denote its Galois orbit under $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/E)$ (where $E$ is the reflex field), and let $\delta_{O(x)}$ be the uniform probability measure supported on $O(x)$.

Let $\{x_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of special points of $S$ such that for every proper special subvariety $Z\subsetneq S$, one has $x_n\notin Z$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Prove or disprove: as $n\to\infty$, the measures $\delta_{O(x_n)}$ converge weakly to $\mu_S$.

The conjecture (equidistribution of generic Galois orbits of special points on Shimura varieties) is a well-known refinement of the André–Oort conjecture due to Clozel–Ullmo. Let $\mathbb{H}^2 = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \mathrm{Im}(z) > 0\}$ denote the upper half-plane, on which $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ acts by Möbius transformations, and let $Y = \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) ackslash \mathbb{H}^2$ denote the modular curve, equipped with the hyperbolic probability measure $d\mu_{\mathrm{hyp}} =  rac{3}{\pi}  rac{dx\, dy}{y^2}$ on a fundamental domain.

A point $z \in \mathbb{H}^2$ is called a special point (or CM point) if $z$ is a quadratic irrational; equivalently, $z$ is a fixed point of some element of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ of trace zero, and corresponds to an elliptic curve with complex multiplication by an order in an imaginary quadratic field. To each negative fundamental discriminant $D < 0$ one associates the finite set $\Lambda_D \subset Y$ of special points of discriminant $D$, whose cardinality is the class number $h(D)$.

It is known (theorem of Duke, building on partial results of Linnik) that the uniform probability measures $\mu_D =  rac{1}{|\Lambda_D|} \sum_{z \in \Lambda_D} \delta_z$ converge weak-$*$ to $\mu_{\mathrm{hyp}}$ as $D 	o -\infty$ through fundamental discriminants. Duke's proof proceeds via subconvex bounds for $L$-functions and modular forms.

Problem. Give a proof of the equidistribution statement
$$\mu_D \xrightarrow{\;w^*\;} \mu_{\mathrm{hyp}} \qquad 	ext{as } D 	o -\infty,$$
using only ergodic-theoretic methods (for instance, measure rigidity for diagonal or torus actions on homogeneous spaces, joinings, or unipotent dynamics), without appealing to subconvexity of $L$-functions.

An ergodic-theoretic approach to equidistribution of CM/special points was developed by Linnik (under a splitting hypothesis) and extended by Einsiedler, Lindenstrauss, Michel, and Venkatesh, who used measure rigidity for torus actions on homogeneous spaces to give ergodic-theoretic proofs of equidistribution of toral/CM packets (under mild auxiliary splitting conditions), and the unconditional result is by Duke. Let $X$ be an instance space and let $C \subseteq \{0,1\}^X$ be a concept class. A compatibility notion is a function $\chi : C \times \mathcal{P}(X) \to [0,1]$, where $\mathcal{P}(X)$ denotes a class of probability distributions on $X$; the quantity $\chi(h,D)$ measures how compatible a hypothesis $h \in C$ is with an unlabeled data distribution $D$ (for instance, $1-\chi(h,D)$ might equal the probability that $h$ cuts through a high-density region, or some other unlabeled-data-based regularizer).

For a distribution $D$ on $X$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, define the reduced class
$$C_{D,\chi}(\varepsilon) \;=\; \{\, h \in C : 1 - \chi(h, D) \le \varepsilon \,\}.$$
Assume the learning model is realizable and compatible: there is an unknown target concept $c^* \in C$ with $\chi(c^*, D) = 1$, and the learner receives i.i.d. labeled examples $(x, c^*(x))$ with $x \sim D$, together with an arbitrary amount of i.i.d. unlabeled examples drawn from $D$.

Information-theoretically, given sufficient unlabeled data one can restrict attention to $C_{D,\chi}(\varepsilon)$, so that
$$m(\varepsilon, \delta) \;=\; O\!\left( \tfrac{1}{\varepsilon}\bigl( \log |C_{D,\chi}(\varepsilon)| + \log(1/\delta) \bigr) \right)$$
labeled examples suffice (with an analogous VC-dimension bound for infinite classes) to output, with probability at least $1-\delta$, a hypothesis of error at most $\varepsilon$.

Question: For interesting choices of the concept class $C$ and the compatibility notion $\chi$, does there exist a computationally efficient learning algorithm (running in time polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$, $\log(1/\delta)$, and the natural representation size of $C$) whose labeled-sample complexity is polynomial in $m(\varepsilon, \delta)$ above, while using polynomially many unlabeled examples?

Setup. Fix a positive integer n and consider examples in the Boolean cube X = {0,1}^n. A two-sided disjunction is a pair h = (h^+, h^-) where h^+ and h^- are each monotone disjunctions (OR-functions) over some subsets of the n variables. The classification rule associated with h uses only h^+: an example x is labeled +1 if h^+(x) = 1 and -1 otherwise. The hypothesis h is said to be compatible with a distribution D over X if, for every x in the support of D,
    h^+(x) = ¬ h^-(x),
i.e., the positive and negative classes are both representable by OR-functions on D. Let C denote the class of two-sided disjunctions over {0,1}^n equipped with this compatibility notion.

Semi-supervised PAC model. The learner is given (i) an unlabeled sample drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution D over X, and (ii) a labeled sample drawn i.i.d. from D and labeled by some unknown target h* ∈ C that is compatible with D. For parameters ε, δ ∈ (0,1), the learner must output a hypothesis whose error with respect to (D, h*) is at most ε with probability at least 1-δ. The compatibility-filtered sample complexity is the labeled-sample size required to ε-cover, in the standard PAC sense, the subclass of C consisting of those hypotheses that are compatible with D (which can in principle be estimated using the unlabeled sample).

Problem. Decide whether there exists a learning algorithm for C in the above semi-supervised PAC model that
  (a) runs in time polynomial in n, 1/ε, and 1/δ, and
  (b) uses a number of labeled examples that matches the compatibility-filtered sample complexity for C up to factors polynomial in n, 1/ε, and log(1/δ),
while using a polynomial number of unlabeled examples.

For an example x ∈ {0,1}^n, write p(x) = (number of indices i ∈ P with x_i = 1)/|P| and q(x) = (number of indices i ∈ N with x_i = 1)/|N| (fractions of positive and negative indicators that are "on" in x).

Target concepts. A target concept is specified by a partition (P,N) as above. Given a distribution D over {0,1}^n, the target labels examples as follows:
 • x is labeled +1 if p(x) ≥ 0.6 and q(x) ≤ 0.4;
 • x is labeled −1 if p(x) ≤ 0.4 and q(x) ≥ 0.6.
We assume D is supported on examples satisfying one of these two conditions (i.e., the target is consistent on the support of D).

Semi-supervised PAC framework. The learner receives (i) an arbitrarily large pool of unlabeled examples drawn i.i.d. from D and (ii) m labeled examples drawn i.i.d. from D and labeled by the target. For inputs ε, δ ∈ (0,1), the learner must output, with probability at least 1−δ, a hypothesis h whose error under D is at most ε.

Notion of compatibility. A partition (P,N) is called compatible with D if D is concentrated on the union of the two margin sets above (every example in the support satisfies one of the two inequalities). Let χ(D) denote the set of partitions compatible with D; intuitively, when this set is small, few labeled examples should be required to identify the target among compatible hypotheses.

Question. Does there exist an algorithm that, given polynomially many unlabeled examples, runs in time polynomial in n, 1/ε, 1/δ, and uses a number of labeled examples polynomial in log|χ(D)|, 1/ε, 1/δ (matching, up to polynomial factors, the labeled sample complexity suggested by the size of the compatible search space), to PAC-learn the class of two-sided-majority-with-margins concepts described above?

Setup. Fix $n \ge 1$ and let the instance space be $\{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}^n$. Let $C$ be the class of monotone (or general) Boolean disjunctions on $n$ variables; for $h \in C$ and a pair $x = (x_1, x_2)$ define the prediction by $h(x) := h(x_1)$, and say that $h$ is compatible with $x$ iff $h(x_1) = h(x_2)$.

Distributional assumption. Let $D$ be an unknown distribution over $\{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}^n$ with the property that there exists a target disjunction $h^* \in C$ that is fully compatible with $D$, i.e. $\Pr_{(x_1,x_2)\sim D}[h^*(x_1) = h^*(x_2)] = 1$. Equivalently, every pair drawn from $D$ consists of two positive examples or of two negative examples (under $h^*$).

Learning model. The learner receives an i.i.d. sample of unlabeled pairs from $D$ together with an i.i.d. labeled sample $(x,h^*(x))$ from $D$. Given parameters $\varepsilon, \delta \in (0,1)$, the learner must output, with probability at least $1-\delta$, a hypothesis $\hat h$ such that $\Pr_{(x_1,x_2)\sim D}[\hat h(x_1) \ne h^*(x_1)] \le \varepsilon$.

Information-theoretic baseline. Let $m^*(\varepsilon,\delta,n)$ denote the labeled sample complexity achievable (ignoring computation) by restricting to disjunctions consistent with the unlabeled pairs (i.e., disjunctions $h$ for which $h(x_1)=h(x_2)$ for all observed unlabeled pairs) and applying standard compatibility-based PAC bounds.

Question. Does there exist a learning algorithm running in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon,1/\delta)$ that uses $\mathrm{poly}(m^*(\varepsilon,\delta,n))$ labeled examples (and $\mathrm{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon,1/\delta)$ unlabeled pairs) and that, with probability at least $1-\delta$, outputs a hypothesis with error at most $\varepsilon$ in the model above?

Co-training setting. Let $X_1, X_2 \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be two "views" of an instance space, and consider a target concept given by a pair of homogeneous linear separators $h_1, h_2$ such that for the relevant distribution $D$ on labeled pairs $((x_1, x_2), y) \in X_1 \times X_2 \times \{-1,+1\}$, with probability 1 the labels agree: $\mathrm{sign}(h_1 \cdot x_1) = \mathrm{sign}(h_2 \cdot x_2) = y$. The learner receives a large sample of unlabeled pairs $(x_1, x_2)$ drawn i.i.d. from the marginal of $D$ on $X_1 \times X_2$ (possibly together with a small amount of labeled data), and must output, in time polynomial in $d, 1/\varepsilon, 1/\delta$, hypotheses whose joint error on $D$ is at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.

Known facts: (i) the consistency problem for arbitrary distributions over pairs is NP-hard; (ii) efficient algorithms exist in the special case where $x_1$ and $x_2$ are conditionally independent given the label $y$.

Question. Identify a nontrivial relaxation of the conditional-independence-given-the-label assumption on the joint distribution of $(x_1, x_2)$ under which one can still give a computationally efficient (polynomial-time) PAC-style co-training algorithm that learns a pair of linear separators to arbitrarily small error.

Background and setup. Fix an instance space X and a concept class C of functions c : X → {0,1}. In the semi-supervised PAC learning model, a target concept c* ∈ C and an unknown distribution D over X are fixed. A learner receives two samples drawn i.i.d. from D: an unlabeled sample U of size m_u, and a labeled sample L of size m_l (each example in L is labeled by c*). Given ε, δ ∈ (0,1), the learner must output a hypothesis h with err_D(h) := Pr_{x ∼ D}[h(x) ≠ c*(x)] ≤ ε, with probability at least 1 − δ.

A compatibility notion is a function χ : C × Δ(X) → [0,1] (where Δ(X) is the set of distributions on X) that measures how compatible a hypothesis is with the marginal distribution D, with the assumption that χ(c*, D) is close to 1 (or above a known threshold τ). Given an unlabeled sample U, one defines an empirical compatibility χ̂(·, U), and the unlabeled-data-filtered version of the class is

  C_{χ,τ}(U) := { c ∈ C : χ̂(c, U) ≥ τ − γ }

for an appropriate slack γ. The labeled sample complexity in this filtered model can be bounded in terms of an effective complexity measure of C_{χ,τ}(U) (for example, its VC dimension or a uniform-convergence-based measure), which can be much smaller than the corresponding measure of C itself when χ is informative about D.

Problem. Exhibit additional pairs (C, χ) — beyond known examples — for which all of the following hold simultaneously:

1. There exists a non-trivial compatibility notion χ such that the χ-compatibility of c* with respect to D is bounded away from arbitrary by a known constant τ, and such that the effective complexity of C_{χ,τ}(U) is provably smaller than that of C (i.e., χ genuinely uses the unlabeled distribution to shrink the search space).

2. There is a computationally efficient algorithm (running in time polynomial in the relevant parameters, including 1/ε, 1/δ, and the description size of concepts in C) that, given an unlabeled sample of size polynomial in these parameters together with a labeled sample whose size matches (up to polynomial factors) the labeled sample complexity dictated by the effective complexity of C_{χ,τ}(U), outputs a hypothesis h with err_D(h) ≤ ε with probability at least 1 − δ.

3. In particular, the resulting labeled sample complexity is asymptotically smaller than the best known efficient supervised PAC learner for C, demonstrating that unlabeled data is provably leveraged by an efficient algorithm.

The task is to identify and analyze such new pairs (C, χ), or to prove obstructions to their existence under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions.

The problem as posed is a broad research direction asking for new efficient semi-supervised PAC learners with provable labeled-sample savings via compatibility notions. While individual special cases (e.g., for linear separators with margin compatibility, or certain co-training settings) have been studied since the introduction of the Balcan–Blum framework, the general question of identifying new (C, χ) pairs admitting efficient learners with reduced labeled complexity remains an ongoing research program with no comprehensive resolution. We did not find a single result that closes the broad problem.

Let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices. The (planar) crossing number $\mathrm{cr}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum, over all drawings of $G$ in the plane with vertices represented by distinct points and edges by continuous curves joining their endpoints (such that no edge passes through a vertex other than its endpoints, no two edges sharing an endpoint cross, and no two edges cross more than once), of the number of pairs of edges that cross.

Determine whether, for every integer $n \geq 1$,
$$\mathrm{cr}(K_n) \;=\; \frac{1}{4}\left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-3}{2} \right\rfloor.$$

Known as Guy's conjecture. The formula is a proven upper bound (Hill; Blažek–Koman). Equality has been verified for n ≤ 12 (Guy for small n; Pan–Richter 2007 for n = 11, 12), which by parity also gives n = 13. For general n the conjecture remains open; the best known lower bound is cr(K_n) ≥ 0.8594 Z(n).

A drawing of the complete graph $K_n$ in the plane is a representation in which each vertex is mapped to a distinct point of the plane and each edge is represented by a simple Jordan arc connecting its endpoints, such that no arc passes through a vertex other than its endpoints and any two arcs share only finitely many points (each shared interior point being a proper crossing). For each vertex $v$ of $K_n$, the rotation at $v$ induced by such a drawing is the cyclic order of the edges incident to $v$ obtained by reading them off in the clockwise direction in a small neighborhood of $v$. The rotation system of the drawing is the collection of these cyclic local rotations, one at each vertex.

Problem. Characterize exactly which assignments of cyclic permutations $\pi_v$ of the edges incident to $v$, taken over all vertices $v$ of $K_n$, can occur as the rotation system of some drawing of $K_n$ in the plane.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Recent work on simple drawings of $K_n$ has provided partial characterizations: a pre-rotation system is drawable as a simple drawing of $K_n$ if and only if certain small (4-, 5-, and 6-element) induced subconfigurations are drawable, and SAT-based enumeration has been used to study and characterize realizable rotation systems. A complete and concise combinatorial characterization for all $n$ remains an active research topic, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

This is Zarankiewicz's crossing number conjecture. It is known to hold whenever $\min(m,n) \le 6$, and has been verified for $K_{7,7}, K_{7,8}, K_{7,9}, K_{7,10}, K_{8,8}, K_{8,9}, K_{8,10}$. The Zarankiewicz formula is known to be an upper bound, and the best known lower bound asymptotically gives at least about 83% of the conjectured value. The general conjecture remains open.

representations.normalized:
Let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices. The (ordinary) crossing number $\operatorname{cr}(K_n)$ is the minimum number of pairwise crossings of edges, taken over all drawings of $K_n$ in the plane in which vertices are distinct points and edges are simple curves joining their endpoints, with the property that no three edges meet at a common interior point and any two edges share at most one point. The rectilinear (geometric) crossing number $\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(K_n)$ is defined analogously, but only drawings in which every edge is a straight-line segment are allowed (so the $n$ vertices are placed as points in general position in the plane and edges are the $\binom{n}{2}$ line segments joining them).

Determine the two limits
$$\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(K_n)}{n^4} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(K_n)}{\operatorname{cr}(K_n)}.$$
(Equivalently, since $\operatorname{cr}(K_n)/\binom{n}{4}$ is known to tend to a constant, determine the rectilinear crossing constant $\nu^* := \lim_{n\to\infty} \overline{\operatorname{cr}}(K_n)/\binom{n}{4}$ and the ratio of the two asymptotic constants.)

Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the free monoid of finite words over $\Sigma$. Fix an integer $n \geq 2$ and let $X = \{u_1, v_1, v_2, \dots, v_n\}$ be a set of unknowns (variables). Consider the infinite system of word equations
$$E = \{\,u_1^i \;=\; v_1^i\, v_2^i \cdots v_n^i \;:\; i \geq 0\,\}$$
over the unknowns $X$, where each equation asserts equality in the free monoid after substituting words from $\Sigma^*$ for the unknowns. Two systems of word equations on $X$ are called equivalent if they have exactly the same set of solutions (i.e., the same set of morphisms $X^* \to \Sigma^*$ satisfying every equation).

Question: Does there exist a subsystem $E' \subseteq E$ consisting of exactly three equations such that $E'$ is equivalent to $E$? Equivalently, can the entire infinite system $E$ be replaced by some three of its own equations without changing the solution set?

$$E = \{\,u_1^i \;=\; v_1^i\, v_2^i \cdots v_n^i \;:\; i \geq 0\,\}$$
over the unknowns $X$, where each equation asserts equality in the free monoid after substituting words from $\Sigma^*$ for the unknowns. Two systems of word equations on $X$ are called equivalent if they have exactly the same set of solutions (i.e., the same set of morphisms $X^* \to \Sigma^*$ satisfying every equation).

Question: Does there exist a subsystem $E' \subseteq E$ consisting of exactly three equations such that $E'$ is equivalent to $E$? Equivalently, can the entire infinite system $E$ be replaced by some three of its own equations without changing the solution set?

status_assertions.value: open_status:unknown

The general compactness theorem (Ehrenfeucht's conjecture, proved by Albert–Lawrence and Guba) implies the system is equivalent to some finite subsystem, but no explicit upper bound on the number of equations needed is known in general, even for three-unknown systems. Surveys on independent systems of word equations indicate the specific question of equivalence to a three-equation subsystem of this family remains an open problem with no published resolution found.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The equality of the rectilinear and ordinary crossing numbers for all complete bipartite graphs K_{m,n} is a long-standing conjecture closely tied to Zarankiewicz's conjecture. Surveys on crossing numbers and recent papers establishing bounds (e.g., cr̄(K_{n,n}) ≥ 0.987·Z(n,n) + o(n^4)) treat it as open; neither the rectilinear nor the ordinary crossing number of K_{m,n} is known in general, and no proof of their equality is known.

A drawing of a simple graph $G$ in the plane is called a *thrackle drawing* if every edge is drawn as a simple (Jordan) arc, any two edges meet in exactly one point (which is either a common endpoint or a proper transversal crossing), and no two edges share more than one point. A graph is said to be *thrackleable* if it admits a thrackle drawing.

Prove or disprove the following: every thrackleable graph $G$ on $n$ vertices satisfies
$$|E(G)| \le |V(G)| = n.$$

A drawing of a simple graph $G$ in the plane is called a *thrackle drawing* if every edge is drawn as a simple (Jordan) arc, any two edges meet in exactly one point (which is either a common endpoint or a proper transversal crossing), and no two edges share more than one point. A graph is said to be *thrackleable* if it admits a thrackle drawing.

Prove or disprove the following: every thrackleable graph $G$ on $n$ vertices satisfies
$$|E(G)| \le |V(G)| = n.$$

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Conway's thrackle conjecture remains open. The best known upper bounds are linear in n but strictly larger than n: Fulek–Pach gave roughly 1.428n, improved by Goddyn–Xu to about 1.4n, then to ~1.393n by Xu, and a recent bound around 1.3984n has been announced. The conjectured equality |E| ≤ n has not been established in general.

A drawing of a finite simple graph $G$ in the plane is called good if (i) every edge is a simple arc whose endpoints are the images of its incident vertices, (ii) no edge passes through a vertex other than its endpoints, (iii) any two edges share at most one interior point, where they cross transversally, (iv) no three edges share an interior point, and (v) two edges sharing a common endpoint do not cross. For such a drawing $D$, let $\mathrm{cr}(D)$ denote the number of pairs of edges that cross. The maximum crossing number of $G$ is
$$\mathrm{cr}^{M}(G) := \max_{D} \mathrm{cr}(D),$$
where the maximum is over all good drawings $D$ of $G$ in the plane.

Prove or disprove: for every finite simple graph $G$ and every subgraph $H$ of $G$,
$$\mathrm{cr}^{M}(H) \le \mathrm{cr}^{M}(G).$$

Say that a simple graph $G$ triangulates a (closed) surface $S$ if $G$ admits a 2-cell embedding into $S$ in which every face is bounded by a triangle (3-cycle). Determine whether the following holds:

(a) There exists a constant $c \in (0,1)$ such that every simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices satisfying $\delta(G) \ge cn$ and $|E(G)| \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$ triangulates some closed orientable surface.

(b) There exists a constant $c \in (0,1)$ such that every simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices satisfying $\delta(G) \ge cn$ and $|E(G)| \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$ triangulates some closed non-orientable surface.

Here $\delta(G)$ denotes the minimum degree of $G$. In each case, the question is whether such a constant $c$ exists (the constants in (a) and (b) may differ).

Let $\Sigma=\{0,1,2\}$ be a ternary alphabet, and let $\Sigma^{\omega}$ denote the set of (right-)infinite words over $\Sigma$. A finite or infinite word is called square-free if it contains no factor of the form $xx$ with $x$ a nonempty word.

Given two infinite words $u,w\in\Sigma^{\omega}$ and an infinite binary sequence $\beta\in\{L,R\}^{\omega}$ in which both letters $L$ and $R$ occur infinitely often, define the shuffle $u\triangleleft_{\beta} w$ as the unique infinite word obtained by reading, for each $n\ge 1$, the next unread letter of $u$ if $\beta_n=L$ and the next unread letter of $w$ if $\beta_n=R$.

Question: Is it true that for every infinite ternary square-free word $u\in\Sigma^{\omega}$, there exist an infinite ternary square-free word $w\in\Sigma^{\omega}$ and an infinite sequence $\beta\in\{L,R\}^{\omega}$ (with both $L$ and $R$ occurring infinitely often) such that
$$u \;=\; u\triangleleft_{\beta} w\,?$$

For a graph $G$, let $\tilde{\gamma}(G)$ denote its non-orientable genus, i.e., the smallest $k\ge 1$ such that $G$ embeds in the non-orientable surface $N_k$ obtained from the sphere by attaching $k$ crosscaps. Say that $G$ is a minimal obstruction to embedding in $N_k$ if $G$ does not embed in $N_k$ but every proper subgraph of $G$ does.

Does there exist a graph $G$ with the property that for every edge $e\in E(G)$,
$$\tilde{\gamma}(G-e)=\tilde{\gamma}(G)-2\,?$$
Equivalently, does there exist a graph that is simultaneously a minimal obstruction to embedding in two distinct non-orientable surfaces $N_{k}$ and $N_{k+1}$?

The spindle (or pinched sphere) is the pseudosurface obtained from the 2-sphere by identifying two distinct points to a single pinch point. A graph G is said to embed in the spindle if it has a topological embedding in this pseudosurface (edges are interior-disjoint arcs, vertices are mapped to distinct points other than at the pinch point unless one wishes to allow it as a vertex, and any passage through the pinch point is treated as a vertex). The class of graphs embeddable in the spindle is closed under taking minors, so it has a (finite) set of minor-minimal forbidden graphs (excluded minors): graphs G such that G does not embed in the spindle but every proper minor of G does.

Problem. Determine the complete list of all minor-minimal graphs that do not embed in the spindle pseudosurface.

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite undirected graph (loops and multiple edges allowed). A bridge (cut-edge) of $G$ is an edge whose removal increases the number of connected components. Call $G$ bridgeless if it has no bridges. A cycle in $G$ is a connected $2$-regular subgraph. A cycle double cover of $G$ is a multiset (collection) $\mathcal{C}=\{C_1,C_2,\dots,C_k\}$ of cycles of $G$ such that every edge $e\in E$ belongs to exactly two of the cycles $C_i$ (counted with multiplicity).

Prove or disprove: every bridgeless graph admits a cycle double cover.

A cycle double cover of $G$ is a multiset (collection) $\mathcal{C}=\{C_1,C_2,\dots,C_k\}$ of cycles of $G$ such that every edge $e\in E$ belongs to exactly two of the cycles $C_i$ (counted with multiplicity).

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The cycle double cover conjecture, attributed to Szekeres (1973) and Seymour (1979), remains an outstanding open problem in graph theory. Partial results are known (e.g., for graphs with a Hamiltonian path, for graphs with no Petersen minor by Robertson–Seymour–Thomas-type arguments, and reductions to cubic bridgeless graphs / snarks), but the general conjecture is unresolved as of recent surveys.

A 2-cell embedding of a finite graph $G$ in a closed surface $\Sigma$ is an embedding $G \hookrightarrow \Sigma$ such that every connected component of $\Sigma \setminus G$ (a face) is homeomorphic to an open disk. The boundary walk of a face is the closed walk in $G$ traced by its boundary. Say that an embedding is a circular (or strong) embedding if, for every face, this boundary walk is a simple cycle of $G$ (no repeated vertices or edges).

Prove or disprove: every 2-connected finite graph $G$ admits a 2-cell embedding in some closed surface such that the boundary of every face is a simple cycle of $G$.

Let P denote the Petersen graph, i.e. the unique 3-regular graph on 10 vertices whose vertex set is the collection of 2-element subsets of {1,2,3,4,5} with two vertices adjacent iff the subsets are disjoint. For any graph H, let L(H) be its line graph, whose vertices are the edges of H and in which two vertices are adjacent iff the corresponding edges of H share an endpoint. A graph homomorphism from a graph X to a graph Y is a map f: V(X) → V(Y) such that whenever uv ∈ E(X), one has f(u)f(v) ∈ E(Y). A graph is called bridgeless if it has no edge whose removal disconnects a connected component, and cubic if every vertex has degree 3.

Prove or disprove: for every bridgeless cubic graph G, there exists a graph homomorphism from L(G) to L(P).

A graph is called cubic if every vertex has degree exactly 3, and bridgeless if it contains no edge whose removal disconnects the graph. A perfect matching of a graph G is a set of edges M ⊆ E(G) such that every vertex of G is incident with exactly one edge of M. A multiset {M_1, M_2, …, M_k} of perfect matchings is said to cover each edge exactly twice if, for every edge e ∈ E(G), the number of indices i ∈ {1, …, k} with e ∈ M_i is exactly 2.

Prove or disprove: For every bridgeless cubic graph G, there exists a multiset of six perfect matchings M_1, …, M_6 of G such that each edge of G belongs to exactly two of the matchings (counted with multiplicity).

The conjecture (attributed to Grünbaum and Nash-Williams) that every 4-connected toroidal graph is Hamiltonian remains open. status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The conjecture that every 4-connected planar graph contains a homeomorphically irreducible spanning tree (HIST) remains open. Recent work (e.g., a 2024 paper on HIST-critical graphs and related Malkevitch-type conjectures) investigates the problem and makes partial progress, but does not provide a full resolution. status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The conjecture (originally posed by Lovász and Plummer in 1975) has been disproved. Chen, Enomoto, Ozeki, and Tsuchiya (2015) constructed an infinite family of 5-connected (hence 4-connected) plane triangulations with no spanning Halin subgraph; the smallest such example has 512 vertices. Follow-up work ("Plane Triangulations Without a Spanning Halin Subgraph II") provides further counterexamples.

The four-colour theorem states: for every finite loopless planar graph $G$, there exists a proper vertex colouring $c: V(G) \to \{1,2,3,4\}$ such that $c(u) \neq c(v)$ whenever $uv \in E(G)$. Equivalently, the regions of any planar map can be coloured with at most four colours so that any two regions sharing a boundary arc receive different colours.

All known proofs of this theorem reduce the problem to checking a large but finite set of "reducible configurations" forming an "unavoidable set", and this case analysis has only been carried out with the aid of computer verification (originating with the 1976 proof and refined in later proofs).

Problem: Produce a proof of the four-colour theorem that does not rely on computer verification, i.e., a proof whose every step can be checked by hand by a human mathematician in a reasonable amount of time.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

No human-checkable proof of the four-colour theorem is known as of 2026. All accepted proofs (Appel–Haken 1976; Robertson–Sanders–Seymour–Thomas 1997; Gonthier's 2005 Coq formalization) rely on computer verification of a large set of reducible configurations. Finding a non-computer proof remains a widely cited open problem.

representations.original:
Let $T$ be a triangulation of the torus, i.e., a simple graph embedded on the torus $S^1\times S^1$ so that every face is bounded by exactly three edges. A Grünbaum colouring of $T$ is an assignment $c:E(T)\to\{1,2,3\}$ of one of three colours to each edge such that for every face, the three edges on its boundary receive three distinct colours. 

Question: Does every triangulation of the torus admit a Grünbaum colouring?

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Grünbaum's original conjecture (every simple triangulation of an orientable surface has a Grünbaum colouring) is known to be false in general — counterexamples exist on orientable surfaces of genus ≥ 5 — but it remains open for surfaces of genus 1 through 4. For the torus specifically, partial results are known: Albertson, Alpert, Belcastro and Haas (2010) proved that every triangulation $G$ of the torus with chromatic number $\chi(G)\neq 5$ admits a Grünbaum colouring, and Kotrbčík–Nakamoto–Noguchi–Ozeki–Vodopivec et al. showed every even triangulation of the torus has a Grünbaum colouring. The general question for arbitrary triangulations of the torus appears to still be open.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The thickness t(G) of a finite simple graph G is defined as the minimum number of planar subgraphs of G whose union (as edge sets) equals the edge set of G. For positive integers r and s, let K_{r,s} denote the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes r and s, having rs edges joining every pair of vertices in different parts.

Determine t(K_{r,s}) for every pair of positive integers (r,s). In particular, decide whether the formula
   t(K_{r,s}) = ⌈ rs / (2(r+s−2)) ⌉
holds for all r,s ≥ 2, and resolve the cases where r and s are both odd that are not covered by the known constructions.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The thickness of K_{r,s} was determined by Beineke, Harary and Moon (1964) for all cases where at least one of r,s is even, and the conjectured formula ⌈rs/(2(r+s−2))⌉ is believed to hold in general. Recent works have settled additional families but a complete determination is still open.

Let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices. A geometric drawing of a graph $G$ in the plane consists of placing the vertices as distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and drawing each edge as the straight-line segment between its endpoints. A geometric $k$-layer drawing of $G$ is a geometric drawing together with a partition of the edge set into $k$ classes (layers) such that, on the same fixed vertex point set, the edges in each individual layer form a planar straight-line drawing (i.e., no two edges of the same layer cross). The geometric thickness $\bar{\theta}(G)$ is the minimum $k$ for which such a drawing exists.

Determine $\bar{\theta}(K_n)$ as a function of $n$; that is, find a closed-form expression (or otherwise exactly characterize) the geometric thickness of the complete graph on $n$ vertices.

Determine $\bar{\theta}(K_n)$ as a function of $n$; that is, find a closed-form expression (or otherwise exactly characterize) the geometric thickness of the complete graph on $n$ vertices.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The exact geometric thickness of $K_n$ remains open. Known bounds give $\lceil n/5.646 + 0.342\rceil \le \bar{\theta}(K_n) \le \lceil n/4\rceil$, and exact values have been established only for small $n$ (n ≤ 12 and n ∈ {15,16}). No closed-form formula for general $n$ is known.
