Well-posedness is known under various structural hypotheses: the DiPerna–Lions theory (Sobolev $W^{1,1}_{\rm loc}$ vector fields with bounded divergence), Ambrosio's extension to $BV_{\rm loc}$ vector fields with bounded divergence, and further refinements (nearly incompressible $BV$, suitable moduli of continuity, SBD, etc.). Let $d\ge 2$ and $T>0$. Consider a time-dependent vector field $b:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ of singular-integral form
$$b_t(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} K(x-y)\,dF_t(y),$$
where $K:\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ is a standard Calderón–Zygmund singular-integral kernel (i.e. $K$ is smooth away from the origin, homogeneous of degree $-d$, has zero average on spheres centered at the origin, and the convolution operator $f\mapsto K*f$ is bounded on $L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1<p<\infty$), and $F_t$ is, for almost every $t\in[0,T]$, a finite $\mathbb{R}^d$-valued Radon measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $t\mapsto\|F_t\|_{\mathcal{M}}$ integrable on $[0,T]$. Assume in addition the usual growth bound on $b$ and the bound $\mathrm{div}\,b_t\in L^1((0,T);L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d))$.

Question: Can the well-posedness and stability theory of the regular Lagrangian flow associated with the ODE $\dot{X}_t(x)=b_t(X_t(x))$, $X_0(x)=x$ — known when $F_t\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)^d$ — be extended to the case in which $F_t$ is allowed to be a (signed vector) Radon measure? Such an extension would in particular cover vector fields of bounded variation (BV) and of bounded deformation (BD), via the elliptic-PDE representation of $\nabla b$ (or its symmetric part) as a singular integral of a measure.

The fully integrable case ($F_t\in L^1$) is the Bouchut–Crippa theorem. Subsequent work by Bohun–Bouchut–Crippa on Lagrangian flows with anisotropic regularity treats vector fields where some components have derivatives that are singular integrals of measures (motivated by Vlasov–Poisson with measure density), giving partial progress. Further work by Nguyen and others (including a 2025 paper on Lagrangian flows for very singular integral vector fields) advances the theory in specific singular kernel settings. A complete extension to general measure data $F_t$ covering arbitrary BV/BD vector fields does not appear to be available, so the problem is partially solved.

Setting. Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $U \subset X$ be the closed unit ball. Consider a linear control system
$$\dot y(t) = A y(t) + u(t), \qquad y(0)=y_0,$$
where $A$ generates a strongly continuous semigroup on $X$ (or, in the finite-dimensional analogue, $A$ is a bounded operator on $X$) and the admissible controls are measurable functions $u:[0,T]\to U$. Given a target $y_1\in X$ reachable from $y_0$, a time-optimal control is an admissible $u^*$ defined on $[0,T^*]$, with $T^*$ the minimal time at which $y_1$ is reachable, that steers $y_0$ to $y_1$.

A time-optimal control $u^*$ is said to satisfy the Pontryagin maximum principle on a subinterval $[\alpha,\beta]\subset[0,T^*]$ if there exists a nonzero functional $\xi\in X^*$ such that for almost every $t\in[\alpha,\beta]$,
$$\langle \xi, e^{(T^*-t)A^*} u^*(t)\rangle = \sup_{v\in U}\langle \xi, e^{(T^*-t)A^*} v\rangle.$$
The control $u^*$ is called strongly singular on $[\alpha,\beta]$ if the maximum principle fails on $[\alpha,\beta]$. The control $u^*$ is called hypersingular if it is strongly singular on every subinterval $[\alpha,\beta]$ with $0\le \alpha<\beta\le T^*$.

It is known that in the space $X=c_0$ hypersingular time-optimal controls exist, but uniqueness of time-optimal controls fails there. It is also known that in a Hilbert space (and more generally in strictly convex reflexive spaces) time-optimal controls, when they exist, are unique.

Problem. Construct a linear control system on a Hilbert space $X$ (or more generally on a Banach space in which time-optimal controls are unique) which admits a hypersingular time-optimal control, or else prove that no such example exists.

Setup. Let $\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ denote the space of bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. For a bounded operator $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$, the $n$-th approximation number is
$$a_n(T)=\inf\{\|T-F\|:F\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}(F)<n\},\qquad n\in\mathbb{N},$$
and the $n$-th Weyl number is
$$x_n(T)=\sup\{a_n(TA):A\in\mathcal{L}(\ell_2,X),\ \|A\|\le 1\}.$$
For $1\le r<\infty$ define the Lorentz-type Weyl operator ideal
$$\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}:=\{T:\ \|T\|^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}:=\sup_{n\ge 1}n^{1/r}x_n(T)<\infty\},$$
and consider its approximation-number companion
$$(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}:=\{T:\ T\in\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}\ \text{and}\ \sup_{n\ge1}n^{1/r}a_n(T)<\infty\},$$
viewed as an operator ideal on the class of all Banach spaces.

A trace on an operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is a linear functional $\tau$ defined on the components $\mathfrak{A}(X,X)$ (for all Banach spaces $X$) such that
(i) $\tau(S\circ T)=\tau(T\circ S)$ whenever both compositions belong to $\mathfrak{A}$, and
(ii) $\tau(x'\otimes x)=\langle x,x'\rangle$ for rank-one operators $x'\otimes x$.

On the sequence space
$$d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0):=\{\xi=(\xi_n)_{n\ge0}:\ \sup_{n\ge1}n^{1/r}\xi^*_n<\infty\},$$
where $\xi^*$ is the decreasing rearrangement of $|\xi|$, consider the dyadic shift $S_+$ acting by
$$(S_+\xi)_n=\xi_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\quad\text{(or the analogous block-doubling shift)},$$
and call a linear form $\varphi$ on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ "$2^{-1/r}S_+$-invariant" if $\varphi(2^{-1/r}S_+\xi)=\varphi(\xi)$ for every $\xi\in d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

It is known that every $2^{-1/r}S_+$-invariant linear form on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ induces, via a standard construction, a trace on $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$.

Problem. For every $1\le r<\infty$, prove that every trace on $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ arises in this way from some $2^{-1/r}S_+$-invariant linear form on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$; equivalently, show that there are no other traces on $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ beyond those obtained from this construction.

Setup. Let $\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ denote the space of bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. For a bounded operator $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$, the $n$-th approximation number is
$$a_n(T)=\inf\{\|T-F\|:F\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}(F)<n\},\qquad n\in\mathbb{N},$$
and the $n$-th Weyl number is
$$x_n(T)=\sup\{a_n(TA):A\in\mathcal{L}(\ell_2,X),\ \|A\|\le 1\}.$$
For $1\le r<\infty$ define the Lorentz-type Weyl operator ideal
$$\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}:=\{T:\ \|T\|^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}:=\sup_{n\ge 1}n^{1/r}x_n(T)<\infty\},$$
and consider its approximation-number companion
$$(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}:=\{T:\ T\in\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}\ \text{and}\ \sup_{n\ge1}n^{1/r}a_n(T)<\infty\},$$
viewed as an operator ideal on the class of all Banach spaces.

A trace on an operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is a linear functional $\tau$ defined on the components $\mathfrak{A}(X,X)$ (for all Banach spaces $X$) such that
(i) $\tau(S\circ T)=\tau(T\circ S)$ whenever both compositions belong to $\mathfrak{A}$, and
(ii) $\tau(x'\otimes x)=\langle x,x'\rangle$ for rank-one operators $x'\otimes x$.

On the sequence space
$$d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0):=\{\xi=(\xi_n)_{n\ge0}:\ \sup_{n\ge1}n^{1/r}\xi^*_n<\infty\},$$
where $\xi^*$ is the decreasing rearrangement of $|\xi|$, consider the dyadic shift $S_+$ acting by
$$(S_+\xi)_n=\xi_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\quad\text{(or the analogous block-doubling shift)},$$
and call a linear form $\varphi$ on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ "$2^{-1/r}S_+$-invariant" if $\varphi(2^{-1/r}S_+\xi)=\varphi(\xi)$ for every $\xi\in d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

It is known that every $2^{-1/r}S_+$-invariant linear form on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ induces, via a standard construction, a trace on $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$.

Problem. For every $1\le r<\infty$, prove that every trace on $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ arises in this way from some $2^{-1/r}S_+$-invariant linear form on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$; equivalently, show that there are no other traces on $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ beyond those obtained from this construction.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is stated as an explicit open problem in a recent survey on traces of operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces. General web search did not locate any subsequent publication classifying all traces on the ideal $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$; the topic is part of an active program but no resolution was found.

Let $\mathfrak{A}$ be a quasi-Banach operator ideal (in the sense of Pietsch: a class of bounded linear operators between arbitrary Banach spaces, closed under composition with bounded operators on either side, containing the finite-rank operators, and equipped with a complete quasi-norm). For a quasi-Banach (shift-monotone) sequence ideal $\mathfrak{x}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ — that is, a linear subspace of the space of scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that is invariant under the forward and backward shift operators, complete in a given quasi-norm, and such that the quasi-norm is monotone with respect to shifts — one defines the approximation-type operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{x}}$ as the class of operators $T : X \to Y$ between Banach spaces for which the sequence of approximation numbers (or, more generally, the sequence of $\mathfrak{A}$-approximation numbers) $\bigl(a_n^{\mathfrak{A}}(T)\bigr)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$, defined by
$$a_n^{\mathfrak{A}}(T) = \inf\{\|T-L\|_{\mathfrak{A}} : L\in\mathfrak{A}(X,Y),\ \operatorname{rank}(L)\le n\},$$
belongs to $\mathfrak{x}(\mathbb{N}_0)$, equipped with the natural induced quasi-norm.

Prove that, for every quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ and every pair of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals $\mathfrak{x}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and $\mathfrak{y}(\mathbb{N}_0)$, there exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ such that the iterated APP-construction collapses to a single step:
$$\bigl(\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{x}}\bigr)^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{y}} \;=\; \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{z}}.$$
Equivalently, identify (and describe explicitly) such a sequence ideal $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ in terms of $\mathfrak{x}$ and $\mathfrak{y}$, with equality of the associated quasi-norms up to equivalence.

The question is posed as an explicit open problem in Pietsch's list of open problems on traces of operator ideals over Banach spaces. Searches for a published resolution of the reiteration identity $(\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{x}})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{y}} = \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{z}}$ for general quasi-Banach operator ideals and shift-monotone sequence ideals did not yield a solution; related work treats approximation spaces and reiteration in restricted (e.g., Hilbert space, or specific sequence-ideal) settings but does not establish the general Banach-space version. Let $\Lambda=(\lambda_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of nonnegative real numbers with $\lambda_0=0$ and $\lambda_n\to\infty$. Consider entire Dirichlet series of the form
$$F(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n e^{z\lambda_n},$$
and define
$$M(x,F)=\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|F(x+it)|, \qquad \mu(x,F)=\max_{n\geq 0}|a_n|e^{x\lambda_n}.$$
Let $L$ denote the class of continuous, positive, nondecreasing functions on $[x_0,\infty)$ tending to $+\infty$, and let $L_0\subset L$ denote the subclass of those $h\in L$ satisfying the additional regularity condition that $\ln h(x)$ is concave (slowly varying type) with $h(x+O(1))\sim h(x)$.

For $\psi\in L$, let $S_\psi(\Lambda)$ denote the class of entire Dirichlet series $F$ as above such that $\#\{n: a_n\neq 0\}=+\infty$ and
$$|a_n|\leq \exp\{-\lambda_n\psi(\lambda_n)\} \quad \text{for all sufficiently large } n.$$

Assume $h\in L_0$ and that the regularity conditions
\begin{align}
&\text{(i)} \quad \int^{\infty}\frac{dx}{x\,\psi(x)}<\infty, \\
&\text{(ii)} \quad \ln h(x) \text{ is comparable to a suitable inverse function of } \psi
\end{align}
hold, so that for every $F\in S_\psi(\Lambda)$ there exist constants $c>0$ and $x_0\in\mathbb{R}$ with
$$M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\, h(cx) \quad \text{for all } x\geq x_0.$$

Determine the sharp (smallest possible) value of the constant $c>0$ for which this inequality is guaranteed to hold for every $F\in S_\psi(\Lambda)$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture is widely regarded as one of the central open problems in low-dimensional topology. Freedman (1982) settled the topological case in dimension four, but the smooth case remains unresolved. Recent (2025) preprints proposing proofs have not been accepted by the community, and standard references such as Wikipedia and the Open Problem Garden list the problem as open.

Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on vertex set $V(G)$ with $|V(G)| \ge 4$. For each vertex $v \in V(G)$, let $G - v$ denote the vertex-deleted subgraph obtained by removing $v$ and all edges incident to it. Define the deck-set of $G$ to be
$$\mathcal{S}(G) = \{[G-v] : v \in V(G)\},$$
where $[G-v]$ denotes the isomorphism class of $G-v$, and where $\mathcal{S}(G)$ is considered as a set (so isomorphic vertex-deleted subgraphs are identified and multiplicities are discarded).

A graph $G$ is said to be set-reconstructible if every finite simple graph $H$ with $\mathcal{S}(H) = \mathcal{S}(G)$ is isomorphic to $G$.

Question: Is every finite simple graph on at least four vertices set-reconstructible? Equivalently, do there exist non-isomorphic finite simple graphs $G$ and $H$, each with at least four vertices, such that $\mathcal{S}(G) = \mathcal{S}(H)$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The order spectrum of hypohamiltonian graphs is now completely known. Such graphs exist precisely for n = 10, 13, 15, 16, and for every n ≥ 18; no hypohamiltonian graph exists for n ∈ {3,…,9, 11, 12, 14, 17}. In particular, the existence question for n = 17 has been settled negatively via exhaustive computer enumeration (Aldred–McKay–Wormald and subsequent verifications).

Consider the lubrication (slender-jet) approximation for a viscous liquid jet falling from a nozzle under gravity, surface tension, and inertia. Let h(x,t) > 0 denote the outer free-surface radius of the axisymmetric jet and let v(x,t) denote the leading-order axial velocity, where x is the axial coordinate and t is time. After non-dimensionalization with density ρ, dynamic viscosity μ, surface tension coefficient σ, and gravitational acceleration g, the reduced one-dimensional system obtained by asymptotic expansion of the three-dimensional axisymmetric Navier–Stokes free-surface equations takes the form

  ∂_t(h^2) + ∂_x(h^2 v) = 0,
  ρ (∂_t v + v ∂_x v) = -σ ∂_x κ(h) + (3μ / h^2) ∂_x(h^2 ∂_x v) + ρ g,

where κ(h) is the leading-order mean-curvature term in the slender-jet approximation (for example κ(h) = 1/h − ∂_xx h / (1+(∂_x h)^2)^{3/2}, or a standard reduction thereof), posed on a suitable axial interval with boundary conditions modeling a nozzle at one end and a free end below.

Prove analytically that, for an appropriate class of smooth initial data with h > 0, there exists a finite time T* < ∞ at which the solution develops a pinch-off singularity, i.e.

  liminf_{t → T*-} inf_x h(x,t) = 0,

corresponding to droplet breakup. The goal is a rigorous mathematical proof (not merely numerical or asymptotic evidence) that this reduced lubrication system produces a finite-time zero of h.

Consider a Hele-Shaw cell modeled as the following two-dimensional incompressible Darcy free-boundary problem. Let Ω(t) ⊂ ℝ² be a bounded, possibly multiply-connected open set occupied by a viscous fluid at time t ≥ 0, with smooth boundary Γ(t) = ∂Ω(t). The fluid pressure p(·,t) : Ω(t) → ℝ satisfies

  Δp = 0 in Ω(t),
  p = σ κ on Γ(t),

where σ > 0 is the surface tension coefficient and κ denotes the (signed) curvature of Γ(t). The interface Γ(t) is transported by the Darcy velocity v = −∇p; equivalently, the normal velocity of Γ(t) is V_n = −∂p/∂n, where n is the outward unit normal.

Question: Does there exist a smooth initial domain Ω(0) which is connected such that the resulting evolution Ω(t) develops, in finite time T < ∞, a topological singularity at which Ω(t) pinches off, i.e. lim_{t↑T} Ω(t) breaks into two (or more) disjoint connected components? Prove or disprove the occurrence of such finite-time topology change for this surface-tension-driven Hele-Shaw flow.

Consider the one-dimensional lubrication approximation describing the thickness h(z,t) > 0 of a thin neck of fluid in a Hele-Shaw cell, governed by the fourth-order degenerate parabolic equation
  h_t + (h · h_{zzz})_z = 0,
for z in a bounded interval (say [-1,1]) with suitable boundary conditions enforcing a pressure jump, and smooth positive initial data h(·,0). It is known (and expected) that for sufficiently large pressure jump such solutions pinch off, i.e. there exists a finite or infinite time T* with inf h(z,t) → 0 as t → T*.

Prove that, for the approximation to remain self-consistent, the spatial regularity of h is preserved up to the breakup time; specifically, show that the first spatial derivative h_z remains uniformly bounded on the time interval [0, T*), i.e.
  sup_{t ∈ [0, T*)} ‖h_z(·,t)‖_{L^∞} < ∞.

Consider the fourth-order degenerate thin-film equation
  h_t + (m(h) h_{xxx})_x = 0,    x ∈ Ω(t) ⊂ ℝ, t > 0,
for a nonnegative film height h(x,t) ≥ 0, where the mobility m(h) ≥ 0 vanishes at h = 0 (typical examples include m(h) = h^n with n > 0, derived from the lubrication approximation of surface-tension-driven flow of a thin viscous film on a solid substrate). Assume the film has compact support so that Ω(t) = {x : h(x,t) > 0} is a bounded open set, and let the moving contact line be the boundary ∂Ω(t) where h = 0 and the equation degenerates.

Determine which boundary conditions must be imposed at the moving contact line ∂Ω(t) (in addition to h = 0 there) so that the resulting free-boundary problem is both physically meaningful (consistent with the underlying fluid-mechanical model of a contact line on a solid substrate, including treatment of the classical no-slip stress singularity) and mathematically well posed (admitting a unique solution depending continuously on the data, in an appropriate class of nonnegative weak or classical solutions). In particular, specify a complete set of contact-line conditions (e.g. prescribing the contact angle |h_x|, a kinematic law for the speed of ∂Ω(t), or a flux condition) that yields a well-posed evolution for general mobilities m(h) and general wetting regimes (complete and partial wetting).

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The general question of the correct contact-line boundary conditions for degenerate fourth-order thin-film equations remains an active research area, but substantial partial progress has been made. Well-posedness has been established in several regimes: with prescribed contact angle h=0, |h_x|=const in partial wetting (Knüpfer, Giacomelli–Knüpfer–Otto, Gnann and collaborators) and for the perfect-wetting (zero contact angle) regime (e.g. Gnann–Petrache 2023/2025) for broad classes of mobilities. A fully general, physically and mathematically definitive prescription valid across all mobility exponents and wetting regimes, including slippage models, is not yet complete.

Existence of nonnegative weak solutions for the thin-film equation with mobility h^n is classical, but uniqueness and full well-posedness for general nonnegative initial data remain open. Well-posedness results have been obtained in restricted regimes: near self-similar/traveling-wave profiles, in the perfect-wetting regime for n ∈ (1,3/2) ∪ (3/2,3), and for data close to flat or stationary states. A complete well-posedness theory for arbitrary nonnegative data is not available, so the problem is partially solved.

\[
\partial_t h + \partial_x\!\big(h^{n}\,\partial_x^{3} h\big) = 0, \qquad x\in\mathbb{R},\ t>0,
\]
where $n>0$ is a fixed exponent (mobility $m(h)=h^{n}$), with nonnegative, compactly supported initial datum $h_0\in L^{1}(\mathbb{R})$ of finite mass $M=\int_{\mathbb{R}} h_0\,dx>0$. Let $h(\cdot,t)\ge 0$ denote a weak (e.g. energy/entropy) solution preserving mass. For each admissible $n$ there exists a unique nonnegative, compactly supported, mass-$M$ self-similar source-type solution of the form
\[
h_*(x,t)=t^{-\alpha}\,F\!\big(x\,t^{-\alpha}\big),\qquad \alpha=\tfrac{1}{n+4},
\]
where $F$ is the corresponding self-similar profile.

Question: For every admissible $n>0$, does the weak solution $h(\cdot,t)$ converge as $t\to\infty$ to the source-type self-similar solution $h_*(\cdot,t)$ of the same mass (in a suitable norm, e.g. $L^1(\mathbb{R})$, after rescaling to self-similar variables)?

Consider the Cauchy problem on the real line for the fourth-order degenerate thin-film equation
\[
\partial_t h + \partial_x\!\big(h^{n}\,\partial_x^{3} h\big) = 0, \qquad x\in\mathbb{R},\ t>0,
\]
where $n>0$ is a fixed exponent (mobility $m(h)=h^{n}$), with nonnegative, compactly supported initial datum $h_0\in L^{1}(\mathbb{R})$ of finite mass $M=\int_{\mathbb{R}} h_0\,dx>0$. Let $h(\cdot,t)\ge 0$ denote a weak (e.g. energy/entropy) solution preserving mass. For each admissible $n$ there exists a unique nonnegative, compactly supported, mass-$M$ self-similar source-type solution of the form
\[
h_*(x,t)=t^{-\alpha}\,F\!\big(x\,t^{-\alpha}\big),\qquad \alpha=\tfrac{1}{n+4},
\]
where $F$ is the corresponding self-similar profile.

Question: For every admissible $n>0$, does the weak solution $h(\cdot,t)$ converge as $t\to\infty$ to the source-type self-similar solution $h_*(\cdot,t)$ of the same mass (in a suitable norm, e.g. $L^1(\mathbb{R})$, after rescaling to self-similar variables)?

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

For the linear-mobility case n=1, convergence of strong/entropy solutions with compactly supported initial data on the real line to the unique source-type self-similar profile has been proved (Carrillo–Toscani; Carlen–Ulusoy), with explicit (slow) rates in L^1 and H^1 via asymptotic equipartition of the excess energy. For general mobility exponents n and for general weak solutions, the question is not fully settled; results are available only in restricted regimes, so the problem appears partially solved.

Consider the fourth-order degenerate parabolic equation modeling a thin viscous film driven by surface tension in two spatial dimensions:
  h_t + ∇·( f(h) ∇Δh ) = 0,    x ∈ Ω ⊂ ℝ², t > 0,
where h(x,t) ≥ 0 denotes the film height, f(h) = |h|^n with mobility exponent n > 0, and Ω is either a bounded domain (with suitable no-flux/zero-contact-angle boundary conditions) or the torus 𝕋². Initial data h(x,0) = h₀(x) ≥ 0 is prescribed with h₀ ∈ H¹(Ω).

Develop an analytical theory for this two-dimensional problem addressing the following items:
(a) Existence of nonnegative weak (and, where possible, strong) solutions for the full range of mobility exponents n > 0.
(b) Regularity properties of weak solutions, including higher Sobolev regularity, positivity sets, and propagation of the support.
(c) Rupture phenomena: determine for which exponents n finite-time singularities (touch-down of h to zero) can occur, and characterize the local structure (e.g. self-similar profiles) of such singularities.
(d) Long-time asymptotic behavior of global solutions, including convergence to equilibria (constants, droplets) and convergence rates.

Specifically, extend the one-dimensional theory of nonnegative weak solutions, entropy/energy dissipation estimates, finite-speed-of-propagation results, and rupture analysis to the genuinely two-dimensional setting.

For an irrational real number $\alpha$, consider the quadratic polynomial
$$P_\alpha(z) = e^{2\pi i \alpha} z + z^2.$$
The Bruno series of $\alpha$ is defined by $B(\alpha) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \frac{\log q_{n+1}}{q_n}$, where $p_n/q_n$ are the convergents of the continued fraction expansion of $\alpha$; the number $\alpha$ is called a Bruno number if $B(\alpha) < \infty$. By a theorem of Bruno and Yoccoz, $\alpha$ is a Bruno number if and only if $P_\alpha$ is analytically linearizable near $0$, i.e., there is a holomorphic injection $\varphi$ from a neighborhood of $0$ in $\mathbb{C}$ to $\mathbb{C}$ with $\varphi(0)=0$, $\varphi'(0)=1$, and $\varphi^{-1} \circ P_\alpha \circ \varphi(z) = e^{2\pi i \alpha} z$. Let $S_\alpha$ denote the maximal such linearization domain (the Siegel disk of $P_\alpha$ around $0$).

Question: Does there exist a Bruno number $\alpha$ such that the boundary $\partial S_\alpha \subset \mathbb{C}$ is a $C^\infty$ embedded circle (i.e., a $C^\infty$ submanifold of $\mathbb{C}$ diffeomorphic to $S^1$)?

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The problem has been solved affirmatively. Avila, Buff, and Chéritat ("Siegel disks with smooth boundaries", Acta Mathematica 193 (2004), 1–30) proved the existence of a (dense uncountable) set of irrational numbers $\alpha$ (necessarily Bruno, since linearization requires the Bruno condition by Yoccoz) such that $P_\alpha$ has a Siegel disk with $C^\infty$ smooth boundary; a result of this kind had earlier been announced by Pérez-Marco (1993).

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The global shape (curvature and topology) of the universe's spatial sections remains an open problem in cosmology. Current CMB and large-scale structure observations (Planck, WMAP) constrain spatial curvature to be very close to zero but cannot determine the topology; various candidates (flat infinite, 3-torus, Poincaré dodecahedral space, etc.) remain consistent with data.

Let $n\geq 1$ and fix $\alpha\in\mathbb{T}^n=\mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$ satisfying a Diophantine condition: there exist $\gamma>0$ and $\tau\geq n-1$ such that $|k\cdot\alpha-m|\geq \gamma|k|^{-\tau}$ for all $k\in\mathbb{Z}^n\setminus\{0\}$ and $m\in\mathbb{Z}$. Let $C^\infty_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$ denote the Fréchet space of smooth real-valued functions on $\mathbb{T}^n$ with zero Haar integral. For $\varphi\in C^\infty_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$, define the exact symplectic diffeomorphism
$$F_\varphi : T^*\mathbb{T}^n\cong \mathbb{T}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{T}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n,\qquad F_\varphi(\theta,r)=\bigl(\theta+r,\; r+\tfrac{\partial\varphi}{\partial\theta}(\theta+r)\bigr).$$
Let $U_\alpha\subset C^\infty_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$ be the set of $\varphi$ for which $F_\varphi$ admits a smooth invariant torus $T_{\alpha,\varphi}$ given as the graph of a smooth map $\psi:\mathbb{T}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$, such that the restriction $F_\varphi|_{T_{\alpha,\varphi}}$ is smoothly conjugate to the translation $R_\alpha:\theta\mapsto\theta+\alpha$. Endow $C^\infty_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$ with its usual $C^\infty$ topology.

Question: Is the boundary $\partial U_\alpha$ of $U_\alpha$ in $C^\infty_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$ a locally flat $C^k$-submanifold for some integer $k\geq 0$?

Herman's positive entropy conjecture was proved by Pierre Berger and Dimitry Turaev (arXiv:1704.02473, published in Annales/Comm. Math. circles). They showed that any area-preserving C^r-diffeomorphism of a 2-surface with an elliptic fixed point can be C^r-perturbed (for 1 ≤ r ≤ ∞) to one with a chaotic island of positive metric entropy, which in particular yields C^∞-perturbations of the identity on the disk with positive metric entropy.

Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold equipped with either a smooth volume form $\omega^n$ (volume case) or a smooth symplectic form $\omega$ (symplectic case). Denote by $\mathcal{G}^\infty_*(M)$ the space of $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms of $M$ preserving the chosen structure (volume-preserving in the first case, symplectic in the second), endowed with the $C^1$ topology.

For $f\in\mathcal{G}^\infty_*(M)$ and a periodic point $p$ of period $\pi(p)$, let $\lambda_1(p)\le\dots\le\lambda_{\dim M}(p)$ denote the Lyapunov exponents of $Df^{\pi(p)}(p)$. A diffeomorphism $f$ is said to have uniformly positive stable Lyapunov exponents along periodic orbits if there exist constants $c>0$ and an index $0<k<\dim M$ such that for every hyperbolic periodic point $p$ of $f$, the stable Lyapunov exponents at $p$ satisfy $\lambda_i(p)\le -c$ for $i=1,\dots,k$ (and, in the symplectic case, $\lambda_{\dim M+1-i}(p)\ge c$ correspondingly). Let $SE^\infty_*$ denote the set of all such diffeomorphisms in $\mathcal{G}^\infty_*(M)$.

Recall that an $f$-invariant compact set $\Lambda\subset M$ admits a dominated splitting if there is a continuous $Df$-invariant decomposition $T_\Lambda M=E\oplus F$ with $E,F$ nontrivial, and constants $C>0$, $0<\lambda<1$ such that for every $x\in\Lambda$ and every $n\ge 0$,
$$\|Df^n|_{E(x)}\|\cdot\|Df^{-n}|_{F(f^n(x))}\|\le C\lambda^n.$$

Question: Is the set
$$\{f\in\mathcal{G}^\infty_*(M): f\text{ admits a dominated splitting on all of }M\}$$
$C^1$-dense in $SE^\infty_*$?

Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold equipped with either a smooth volume form or a smooth symplectic form, and let $G^\infty_*(M)$ denote, respectively, the space of $C^\infty$ volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ or the space of $C^\infty$ symplectomorphisms of $M$, endowed with the $C^\infty$ topology. For $f\in G^\infty_*(M)$ and $x\in M$, let $\lambda_1(f,x)\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_{\dim M}(f,x)$ denote the Lyapunov exponents of $f$ at $x$ (defined almost everywhere with respect to the invariant volume). Say that $f$ has nonzero Lyapunov exponents stably if there is a $C^\infty$-neighborhood $\mathcal U$ of $f$ in $G^\infty_*(M)$ such that for every $g\in\mathcal U$ all Lyapunov exponents of $g$ are nonzero on a set of full volume (in the symplectic case, all $\dim M$ exponents are nonzero almost everywhere). Let $SE^\infty_*\subset G^\infty_*(M)$ be the set of such diffeomorphisms.

On the complement $G^\infty_*(M)\setminus SE^\infty_*$ (with its induced topology, which is a Baire space on any sufficiently regular open subset), decide which of the following two alternatives holds:

(A) There is a residual (dense $G_\delta$) subset $\mathcal R\subset G^\infty_*(M)\setminus SE^\infty_*$ such that every $f\in\mathcal R$ has vanishing Lyapunov exponents (and, in particular, vanishing metric entropy) almost everywhere; or

(B) There exists a nonempty open subset $\mathcal U\subset G^\infty_*(M)\setminus SE^\infty_*$ and a constant $c>0$ such that the metric entropy $h_{\mathrm{vol}}(g)\ge c$ for every $g\in\mathcal U$.

Let $n \geq 2$. Consider $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ equipped with the standard symplectic form $\omega = \sum_{i=1}^n dx_i \wedge dy_i$. For a smooth compact connected hypersurface $M \subset \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ (so $\dim M = 2n-1$), the characteristic line field on $M$ is the kernel of the restriction $\omega|_M$; at each $p \in M$ this is a 1-dimensional subspace of $T_pM$. Any nowhere-vanishing smooth vector field spanning this line field generates the characteristic flow on $M$ (well-defined up to time reparametrization), and its orbits are the leaves of the characteristic foliation.

The characteristic flow is called minimal if every one of its orbits is dense in $M$.

Question: Does there exist, for some $n \geq 2$, a smooth compact connected hypersurface $M^{2n-1} \subset \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ whose characteristic flow is minimal?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem of finding a smooth compact hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ ($n\geq 2$) whose characteristic flow is minimal does not appear to have been resolved. Related work concerns hypersurfaces without closed characteristics (Hermann, Ginzburg) and contact-type cases (Weinstein conjecture, Viterbo), but no construction or obstruction for a minimal characteristic flow on a compact hypersurface in Euclidean space appears in the standard literature.

Let $M^n$ be a compact connected oriented smooth manifold of dimension $n \geq 3$ with Euler characteristic $\chi(M^n) = 0$, equipped with a smooth volume form $\Omega$. A smooth vector field $X$ on $M^n$ is called $\Omega$-divergence-free if the Lie derivative $\mathcal{L}_X \Omega = 0$ (equivalently, the flow of $X$ preserves $\Omega$). Since $\chi(M^n) = 0$, the space of nowhere-vanishing smooth vector fields on $M^n$ is non-empty, and it decomposes into homotopy classes under homotopies through nowhere-vanishing vector fields.

Question: In every homotopy class of nowhere-vanishing smooth vector fields on $M^n$, does there exist a representative $X$ that is $\Omega$-divergence-free and whose flow has no periodic orbit?

Let $(M^{2n}, \omega)$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$ whose Euler characteristic satisfies $\chi(M^{2n}) = 0$, and assume that $M^{2n}$ does not fiber smoothly over the circle $S^1$. A symplectic vector field on $(M^{2n}, \omega)$ is a smooth vector field $X$ whose flow preserves $\omega$, equivalently $\mathcal{L}_X \omega = 0$. Let $N(M, \omega)$ denote the minimum, taken over all symplectic vector fields $X$ on $(M^{2n}, \omega)$, of the number of zeros of $X$.

Prove or disprove: every symplectic diffeomorphism $\varphi : M^{2n} \to M^{2n}$ that is smoothly homotopic to the identity has at least one fixed point, and in fact has at least $N(M, \omega)$ fixed points.

Let $\mathbb{T}^n = \mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$ and let $T^*\mathbb{T}^n$ denote its cotangent bundle, endowed with the canonical symplectic structure. Consider a Hamiltonian $H: T^*\mathbb{T}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ that is a $C^\infty$-small perturbation of an integrable Tonelli Hamiltonian $H_0(q,p)=\tfrac{1}{2}\langle A p, p\rangle$ (with $A$ a positive definite symmetric matrix), and let $(f^H_t)_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ denote the Hamiltonian flow generated by $H$. For a fixed cohomology class (or rotation vector), Mather's variational principle produces ergodic action-minimizing probability measures supported on the energy level $H^{-1}(1)$; call any such measure an ergodic minimizing measure $\mu$ in the sense of Mather, and write $\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$ for its support.

Question: Is it true that for a $C^\infty$-generic Hamiltonian $H$ (in the sense of a residual subset in the $C^\infty$ topology) near $H_0$, and for a generic ergodic Mather-minimizing measure $\mu$, the restricted flow $f^H_t|_{\mathrm{supp}(\mu)}$ on $H^{-1}(1)$ is a hyperbolic flow (i.e., $\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$ is a uniformly hyperbolic invariant set for the flow)?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of generic hyperbolicity of supports of Mather-minimizing measures for generic Tonelli Hamiltonians on $T^*\mathbb{T}^n$ remains open in general. Partial results exist: Le Calvez established uniform hyperbolicity of generic Aubry-Mather sets for exact symplectic twist maps (essentially the $n=1$ / surface case); Arnaud and others have shown C^1-regularity results when Lyapunov exponents vanish; and there are results showing that perturbations can make the Mather set consist of hyperbolic periodic orbits in certain settings. No full resolution in arbitrary dimension was located.

Let $m, n$ be fixed positive integers. Let $F_m$ denote the free group on $m$ free generators $x_1, \dots, x_m$. An element $w \in F_m$ is called primitive if it belongs to some free generating set of $F_m$ (equivalently, $w$ is the image of $x_1$ under some automorphism of $F_m$).

Let $G$ be a group equipped with an ordered generating $m$-tuple $(g_1, \dots, g_m)$, and assume $G$ is either a finite group, a residually finite group, or a profinite group (in the profinite case the tuple is required to generate $G$ topologically). For every primitive element $w \in F_m$, impose the relation
$$w(g_1, \dots, g_m)^n = 1.$$

Note that this relation is imposed only on values of primitive words, not on all elements of $G$.

Question: Must $G$ be soluble-by-finite? More precisely, do there exist functions $d = d(m,n)$ and $i = i(m,n)$, depending only on $m$ and $n$, such that $G$ contains a soluble normal subgroup of derived length at most $d(m,n)$ and index at most $i(m,n)$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem is presented as a conjecture in the context of variants of the restricted Burnside problem, where periodicity is imposed only on primitive-word values rather than all elements. While Zelmanov solved the classical restricted Burnside problem (1989–91), the primitive-word variant asking for soluble-by-finite structure with bounds depending on m and n appears to remain open; no resolution was located in the available sources.

Let $(M^n, g)$ be a smooth $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with metric $g$. The number $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$ equals the number of independent components of a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor in dimension $n$, and is the natural target dimension associated with the local isometric embedding problem (the Janet–Cartan dimension).

Problem. Develop an effective criterion or decision procedure that, given the metric $g$ on $M^n$ (for instance presented in local coordinates or via its components in some atlas), determines whether there exists an isometric embedding (or immersion) of $(M^n, g)$ into some Riemannian manifold $N$ of dimension $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$. Here "isometric embedding" means a smooth map $f : M^n \to N$ such that $f^* g_N = g$, where $g_N$ denotes the metric on $N$. The criterion should be effective in the sense that it can be checked by a finite procedure applied to the components of $g$ and their derivatives.

The Greisen–Zatsepin–Kuzmin (GZK) limit is a theoretical upper bound (approximately 5 × 10^19 eV) on the energy of cosmic-ray protons that can reach Earth from extragalactic sources. It arises because protons with energies above this threshold lose energy via inelastic interactions with cosmic microwave background photons (predominantly through pion photoproduction) over cosmological propagation distances of order 50–100 Mpc. Observations by experiments such as Fly's Eye, AGASA, the Pierre Auger Observatory, and the Telescope Array have nevertheless detected cosmic-ray events with energies well above this limit (including the so-called "Oh-My-God" particle at ~3 × 10^20 eV), while no astrophysical accelerators capable of producing such energies have been definitively identified within the GZK horizon around Earth.

Provide a physically consistent explanation, supported by an underlying theoretical model and observational evidence, for the following two questions:
(a) What are the astrophysical sources and acceleration mechanisms responsible for cosmic rays observed at energies at or above ~10^20 eV, given the apparent absence of sufficiently energetic accelerators in the local universe?
(b) How can cosmic rays emitted by distant (extragalactic) sources arrive at Earth with energies above the GZK limit—either by identifying a viable propagation/composition scenario consistent with the GZK suppression, or by establishing new physics (e.g., violations of Lorentz invariance, new particles, or exotic top-down production mechanisms) that modifies or evades the GZK cutoff?

The origin of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and the apparent presence of events above the GZK cutoff remain open problems. Recent detections (e.g., the 244 EeV "Amaterasu" particle reported by the Telescope Array in 2023) and 2025 review articles confirm that no definitive sources or acceleration mechanism have been identified, and several competing explanations (heavy nuclei composition, local sources, Lorentz-invariance violation, top-down models) are still under active investigation.

Let $n \geq 3$. A smooth closed differential $k$-form $\varphi$ on Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ (or on the round sphere $S^n$) is called a calibration if, at every point, its restriction to every oriented tangent $k$-plane is at most the Riemannian volume of that plane. An oriented $k$-dimensional submanifold $M$ is said to be calibrated by $\varphi$ if $\varphi$ restricted to each tangent space of $M$ equals the volume form of $M$. Every calibrated submanifold is volume-minimizing in its homology class, hence in particular minimal.

Recall the classical Weierstrass representation: every simply connected minimal surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ admits a conformal parametrization
$$X(\zeta) = \mathrm{Re} \int_{\zeta_0}^{\zeta} \left( \tfrac{1}{2}(1-g^2)\, f,\ \tfrac{i}{2}(1+g^2)\, f,\ f g \right) dz,$$
where $f$ is a holomorphic function and $g$ a meromorphic function on a domain in $\mathbb{C}$, satisfying suitable compatibility conditions. This formula gives an explicit parametric construction producing a large class of minimal surfaces from free holomorphic data.

Question: Does there exist an explicit construction, analogous to the Weierstrass representation, that produces every calibrated minimal submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^n$ (and of $S^n$) from free analytic/holomorphic data, and which exhibits a large class of such submanifolds in arbitrary dimension and codimension?

Partial Weierstrass-type representations exist for special classes of calibrated submanifolds (e.g., special Lagrangians, associative/coassociative submanifolds, holomorphic curves) and recent work constructs new explicit families using complex-valued harmonic morphisms and eigenfunctions. However, no general explicit construction producing all calibrated minimal submanifolds of $\mathbb{R}^n$ or $S^n$ analogous to the Weierstrass representation is known; the underlying PDEs are generally too complicated for explicit solution. The general question appears still open.

Berger's theorem states that the holonomy group of an irreducible, simply connected, non-symmetric Riemannian manifold (M, g) of dimension n must be one of the following subgroups of O(n), referred to as the special (or restricted) holonomy groups:
- SO(n) (generic case),
- U(m) with n = 2m (Kähler manifolds),
- SU(m) with n = 2m (Calabi–Yau manifolds),
- Sp(m) with n = 4m (hyperkähler manifolds),
- Sp(m)·Sp(1) with n = 4m (quaternion-Kähler manifolds),
- G_2 with n = 7,
- Spin(7) with n = 8.

The problem is: classify, up to isometry (and equivalently up to diffeomorphism type with the relevant geometric structure), all compact Riemannian manifolds whose Riemannian holonomy group is one of these special (i.e., non-generic) groups. In particular, give a complete classification of compact manifolds for each entry of Berger's list, including the exceptional cases G_2 and Spin(7), and the Ricci-flat Kähler (Calabi–Yau) case.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Berger's list constrains the possible special holonomy groups, and many compact examples have been constructed (notably Joyce's compact G_2 and Spin(7) manifolds, and Calabi–Yau manifolds via Yau's theorem). However, a full classification of compact Riemannian manifolds with special holonomy remains open: e.g., the diffeomorphism classification of compact G_2 and Spin(7) manifolds, and the classification of Calabi–Yau and hyperkähler manifolds in higher dimensions, are all active and unresolved problems.

Let $M$ be a connected complex manifold of complex dimension $n$, that is, a smooth manifold equipped with an integrable almost complex structure $J : TM \to TM$ with $J^2 = -\mathrm{id}$. A Hermitian metric on $M$ is a Riemannian metric $g$ that is compatible with $J$ in the sense that $g(JX, JY) = g(X,Y)$ for all real tangent vectors $X, Y$. The associated fundamental $2$-form $\omega$ is defined by $\omega(X,Y) = g(JX, Y)$. The pair $(g, J)$ (equivalently, $\omega$) is called a Kähler structure on $M$ if $\omega$ is closed, i.e.\ $d\omega = 0$. The manifold $M$ is said to admit a Kähler structure if there exists such a metric $g$ on $M$.

Problem. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions, intrinsic to the complex manifold $M$, for $M$ to admit a Kähler structure.

The pair $(g, J)$ (equivalently, $\omega$) is called a Kähler structure on $M$ if $\omega$ is closed, i.e.\ $d\omega = 0$. Problem. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions, intrinsic to the complex manifold $M$, for $M$ to admit a Kähler structure.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

No general necessary-and-sufficient intrinsic characterization is known for when a complex manifold admits a Kähler structure. Many necessary conditions are classical (e.g., even odd Betti numbers, the $\partial\bar\partial$-lemma, formality in the compact case) and various sufficient conditions exist (projectivity via Kodaira embedding, Moishezon plus suitable cohomology classes), but no complete criterion is established. The problem is generally regarded as open.

A Calabi–Yau n-fold is a compact Kähler manifold X of complex dimension n with vanishing first Chern class (equivalently, admitting a Ricci-flat Kähler metric and a nowhere-vanishing holomorphic n-form). Mirror symmetry is the empirically observed phenomenon that Calabi–Yau n-folds come in pairs (X, X^∨) such that the symplectic geometry (A-model) of X is equivalent to the complex geometry (B-model) of X^∨, and vice versa; concrete shadows of this include the interchange of Hodge numbers h^{p,q}(X) = h^{n-p,q}(X^∨), the enumerative predictions of Candelas–de la Ossa–Green–Parkes relating Gromov–Witten invariants of X to period integrals on X^∨, Kontsevich's homological mirror symmetry equivalence D^b Fuk(X) ≃ D^b Coh(X^∨), and the Strominger–Yau–Zaslow proposal that mirror pairs admit dual special Lagrangian torus fibrations.

Problem: Provide a mathematically complete and conceptually satisfactory geometric explanation of mirror symmetry for Calabi–Yau manifolds. Concretely, give a precise construction that, for an arbitrary compact Calabi–Yau n-fold X, produces a mirror Calabi–Yau n-fold X^∨ together with a geometric correspondence (for instance via dual special Lagrangian torus fibrations, or via a suitable degeneration / non-archimedean / family Floer construction) from which the predicted equivalences — including the Hodge number exchange, the equality of A-model (Gromov–Witten) invariants of X with B-model (variations of Hodge structure / period) invariants of X^∨, and the homological mirror symmetry equivalence between the derived Fukaya category of X and the derived category of coherent sheaves on X^∨ — can be derived as theorems.

A fully general, mathematically complete geometric explanation of mirror symmetry for Calabi–Yau manifolds remains open. The Strominger–Yau–Zaslow (SYZ) conjecture, which provides the leading geometric framework, has no agreed-upon precise statement and has only been proved in special cases (e.g., toric Calabi–Yau manifolds, del Pezzo and rational elliptic surfaces, log Calabi–Yau surfaces). Let $A=(a_{ij})$ be an $n\times n$ real matrix. For an index set $\alpha\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$, denote by $A[\alpha]$ the principal minor of $A$ corresponding to rows and columns indexed by $\alpha$, and let $|\alpha|$ denote the cardinality of $\alpha$. Define the normalized principal minor sums
$$c_j(A) \;=\; \frac{1}{\binom{n}{j}}\sum_{|\alpha|=j} A[\alpha], \qquad j=0,1,\dots,n,$$
with the convention $c_0(A)=1$.

Recall the following definitions:
- $A$ is called a $\tau$-matrix if for every nonempty index set $\alpha\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ and every $i\in\alpha$, one has $A[\alpha]\cdot A[\alpha\setminus\{i\}\cup\{i\}] \ge$ (the usual $\tau$ inequality between adjacent principal minors holds); equivalently, $A$ satisfies all the $\tau$-inequalities relating principal minors indexed by sets differing by one element in the standard way.
- $A$ is called a GKK matrix (Gantmacher–Krein–Koteljanskii) if every principal minor of $A$ is positive and $A$ satisfies the Koteljanskii (Hadamard–Fischer type) inequalities $A[\alpha\cup\beta]\,A[\alpha\cap\beta] \le A[\alpha]\,A[\beta]$ for all index sets $\alpha,\beta\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$.
- $A$ is called (positive) stable if every eigenvalue of $A$ lies in the open right half-plane $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re}(z)>0\}$.

Question: Suppose $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix that is simultaneously GKK, $\tau$, and (positive) stable. Must $A$ satisfy Newton's inequalities
$$c_j(A)^2 \;\ge\; c_{j-1}(A)\,c_{j+1}(A) \qquad \text{for every } j=1,\dots,n-1\,?$$

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \ge 2$) be a bounded Lipschitz domain representing the reference configuration of an elastic body. A deformation is a map $u : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^n$, and its gradient $\nabla u(x)$ takes values in the set $M^{n\times n}$ of real $n\times n$ matrices. Let $M^{n\times n}_+ = \{A \in M^{n\times n} : \det A > 0\}$.

A stored-energy function is a Borel measurable function $W : M^{n\times n} \to [0,\infty]$ satisfying:
(i) (Orientation preservation / non-interpenetration on the energy level) $W(A) = +\infty$ whenever $\det A \le 0$;
(ii) (Singular determinant condition) $W(A) \to +\infty$ as $\det A \to 0^+$, uniformly on bounded subsets of $M^{n\times n}_+$;
(iii) (Quasiconvexity) $W$ is quasiconvex on $M^{n\times n}_+$ in the sense of Morrey: for every $A \in M^{n\times n}_+$ and every $\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $A + \nabla\varphi(x) \in M^{n\times n}_+$ a.e.,
$$\int_\Omega W(A + \nabla \varphi(x))\,dx \ge W(A)\,|\Omega|;$$
(iv) (Coercivity) there exist $p \ge 1$ and constants $c > 0$, $b \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $W(A) \ge c|A|^p + b$ for all $A \in M^{n\times n}$.

Consider the energy
$$I(u) = \int_\Omega W(\nabla u(x))\,dx$$
on an admissible class $\mathcal{A}$ of deformations consisting of maps $u \in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ satisfying a prescribed Dirichlet boundary condition $u = u_0$ on a portion $\partial\Omega_1 \subset \partial\Omega$ of positive surface measure (with $u_0$ chosen so that $\mathcal{A}$ is nonempty and $\inf_{\mathcal{A}} I < \infty$).

Prove (or disprove) that under hypotheses (i)–(iv) the functional $I$ attains its infimum on $\mathcal{A}$; equivalently, that there exists $u^* \in \mathcal{A}$ with $I(u^*) = \inf_{u \in \mathcal{A}} I(u)$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem is a long-standing open question. It is widely known as Ball's problem of existence of minimizers in nonlinear elastostatics under quasiconvexity together with the singular behavior of $W$ at $\det A = 0^+$. Polyconvex existence theory (Ball, 1977) handles a stronger convexity hypothesis, and partial results exist (e.g., relaxation results, existence with cavitation/fracture, and special cases), but the general quasiconvex case with the singular determinant constraint remains unresolved as of recent surveys.

Let $W:\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+\to \mathbb{R}$ be a stored-energy function for a hyperelastic body, where $\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+$ denotes the set of $3\times 3$ matrices with positive determinant. Recall the following notions:

(i) $W$ is polyconvex if there exists a convex function $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}\times \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}\times \mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}$ such that $W(A)=\Phi(A,\operatorname{cof} A,\det A)$ for all $A\in \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+$, where $\operatorname{cof} A$ is the cofactor matrix.

(ii) $W$ is quasiconvex (in the sense of Morrey) at $A\in\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+$ if for every bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^3$ and every $\varphi\in W_0^{1,\infty}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3)$ with $A+\nabla\varphi\in \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+$ a.e.,
$$\int_\Omega W(A+\nabla\varphi(x))\,dx \ge W(A)\,|\Omega|.$$

For an isotropic material, frame indifference and isotropy imply that $W$ admits the singular-value representation $W(A)=\Phi(v_1,v_2,v_3)$, where $v_1,v_2,v_3$ are the singular values of $A$, and this representation has been used to formulate verifiable conditions for polyconvexity and quasiconvexity.

Problem: Develop practical, verifiable criteria, or constructive methods, for deciding polyconvexity and quasiconvexity of stored-energy functions $W$ in the anisotropic setting—that is, when $W$ is invariant only under a proper subgroup $G\subsetneq SO(3)$ acting on the reference configuration (so the isotropic singular-value representation is not available)—covering a useful class of anisotropic materials (for instance transversely isotropic, orthotropic, cubic, tetragonal, trigonal, monoclinic, or triclinic symmetries).

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem of finding practical criteria for polyconvexity and quasiconvexity of anisotropic stored-energy functions remains an active and largely open area. Partial constructions of polyconvex anisotropic energies based on structural tensors exist for transverse isotropy, orthotropy and cubic symmetry, while triclinic, monoclinic, tetragonal and trigonal cases remain problematic. Quasiconvexity in particular has no general verifiable criterion even in the isotropic case, and no systematic anisotropic treatment is known.

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2$ or $3$) be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary $\partial \Omega = \overline{\partial_1\Omega} \cup \overline{\partial_2\Omega}$, where $\partial_1\Omega$ and $\partial_2\Omega$ are disjoint relatively open subsets on which displacement (Dirichlet) and traction (Neumann) boundary conditions are imposed respectively. Let $W : \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ be a stored-energy density (smooth on the set of matrices with positive determinant, polyconvex or quasiconvex, satisfying $W(F) \to \infty$ as $\det F \to 0^+$, and coercive in an appropriate Sobolev space sense). Consider the elastic energy
$$I(y) = \int_\Omega W(Dy(x))\, dx - \langle \text{loads}, y\rangle,$$
defined on admissible deformations $y : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^n$ with $y = y_0$ on $\partial_1\Omega$, $\det Dy > 0$ a.e. Assume the existence of a global minimizer $y^* \in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ of $I$.

Determine geometric and analytic conditions on $W$, $\Omega$, the boundary data, and the loads under which $y^*$ is $C^\infty$ in $\Omega$ and $C^\infty$ up to the boundary except possibly near points of $\overline{\partial_1\Omega} \cap \overline{\partial_2\Omega}$ where displacement and traction boundary regions meet.

The smoothness of global minimizers of nonlinear elastic energies is a long-standing open problem repeatedly highlighted by Ball and others. Only partial regularity results for general quasiconvex functionals (Evans, Kristensen–Mingione, etc.) are known, and these do not apply directly under the determinant-blow-up condition typical in elasticity. No general resolution has been reported.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2$ or $3$) be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary, and let $W:\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}_+\to[0,\infty)$ be a stored-energy function (where $\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}_+$ denotes matrices with positive determinant). Assume $W$ satisfies growth conditions strong enough to ensure that every deformation $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ with finite total energy
$$E(u)=\int_\Omega W(\nabla u(x))\,dx<\infty$$
is (Hölder) continuous on $\overline\Omega$; e.g.\ $W(F)\ge c|F|^p$ for some $p>n$, possibly together with polyconvexity, frame indifference, isotropy, and $W(F)\to\infty$ as $\det F\to 0^+$.

Consider the variational problem of minimizing $E(u)$ over an admissible class $\mathcal{A}$ of deformations satisfying prescribed boundary or topological constraints. The Lavrentiev phenomenon is said to occur if
$$\inf_{u\in\mathcal{A}}E(u)\ <\ \inf_{u\in\mathcal{A}\cap C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)}E(u),$$
i.e.\ if smooth admissible deformations cannot approximate the infimum in energy.

Question: Under such continuity-forcing growth conditions on $W$, can the Lavrentiev phenomenon occur in elastostatics, in particular:
(a) for the problem with mixed displacement/traction (Dirichlet–Neumann) boundary conditions on disjoint portions of $\partial\Omega$, even in two space dimensions; and
(b) when the energy concentration causing the gap is associated with a singularity in the interior of $\Omega$ rather than on the boundary?

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The basic question—whether the Lavrentiev phenomenon can occur in elastostatics under growth conditions forcing finite-energy deformations to be continuous—has been answered affirmatively: a 2D example with smooth, polyconvex, frame-indifferent, isotropic stored-energy density of p>2 growth, with W(F)→∞ as det F→0+, was constructed (2023), and further neo-Hookean examples in 2D and 3D exhibiting a Lavrentiev gap with continuous a.e.-injective deformations have appeared. The refinements concerning mixed boundary conditions and interior singularities are addressed in part by the neo-Hookean dipole-type singularity construction in 3D, but the original mixed-boundary-condition variant (in particular in 2D) does not appear fully resolved in the literature, so the overall problem is partially solved.

The question is a longstanding open problem in the calculus of variations and nonlinear elasticity. The question of whether minimizers of polyconvex elastic energies admit a uniform positive lower bound on the Jacobian determinant is a long-standing problem in nonlinear elasticity, originating in Ball's list of open problems. No general result establishing or refuting uniform positivity under broad reasonable growth conditions appears in the literature; only partial results in special settings (e.g., regularity under additional hypotheses, or near-identity deformations) are known. Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary, representing the reference configuration of a hyperelastic body, and let $W : \Omega \times \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ be a polyconvex stored-energy function satisfying standard coercivity and growth conditions, with $\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+$ denoting the matrices with positive determinant. Consider the constrained minimization problem of Ciarlet–Nečas type: minimize the elastic energy
$$E(u) = \int_\Omega W(x, \nabla u(x))\,\mathrm{d}x$$
over the class of admissible deformations
$$\mathcal{A} = \Bigl\{ u \in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3) : \det\nabla u > 0 \text{ a.e.,}\ \int_\Omega \det\nabla u(x)\,\mathrm{d}x \le \mathrm{vol}(u(\Omega)),\ u|_{\Gamma_0} = u_0 \Bigr\}$$
(with $p > 3$, prescribed boundary data $u_0$ on a portion $\Gamma_0 \subset \partial\Omega$), the integral inequality being the Ciarlet–Nečas global injectivity condition that allows boundary self-contact but prevents interpenetration.

Provide a rigorous justification of this minimization formulation (or a suitable modification thereof) as a model of smooth frictionless self-contact. Specifically, prove that for a minimizer $u^*$:
(a) the tangential components of the Cauchy stress vector vanish on the deformed self-contact set (no friction);
(b) the free boundary separating the regions of self-contact from the non-contact region is regular (e.g., smooth or locally a $C^1$ hypersurface) under appropriate smoothness hypotheses on $W$ and on the data;
(c) construct admissible variations supported in a neighborhood of the self-contact region needed to derive the corresponding Euler–Lagrange/variational inequality conditions.

Let Ω ⊂ ℝ^3 be a bounded open set with sufficiently regular boundary that is homeomorphic to the closed unit ball. Consider a homogeneous hyperelastic body occupying Ω in its reference configuration, with stored-energy function W : M^{3×3}_+ → ℝ defined on the set of 3×3 matrices with positive determinant. Assume W is strictly polyconvex, i.e. there exists a strictly convex function G : M^{3×3} × M^{3×3} × (0,∞) → ℝ such that
   W(F) = G(F, cof F, det F)   for all F ∈ M^{3×3}_+,
where cof F denotes the cofactor matrix of F. Given a smooth boundary datum u_0 : ∂Ω → ℝ^3, consider deformations u : Ω → ℝ^3 with det ∇u > 0 satisfying the pure displacement boundary condition u = u_0 on ∂Ω, and the equilibrium equations
   div(DW(∇u)) = 0   in Ω.

Question: Either prove that, among sufficiently smooth (e.g. C^2 up to the boundary) equilibrium solutions u with det ∇u > 0 and u|_{∂Ω} = u_0, there is at most one; or exhibit a counterexample (a strictly polyconvex W, a domain Ω homeomorphic to a ball, and boundary data u_0 admitting at least two distinct smooth equilibrium solutions).

The problem appears to remain open in the stated generality. Uniqueness is known only under restrictive assumptions: F. John established uniqueness for smooth deformations with uniformly small strains, and K. Zhang showed that for small displacements from a stress-free state the smooth solution obtained by the implicit function theorem is the unique global minimizer. Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain representing the reference configuration of an elastic body, and let $W:\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}\to[0,\infty]$ be a stored-energy density satisfying the standard assumptions of nonlinear elastostatics: frame indifference $W(RF)=W(F)$ for all $R\in SO(3)$, material symmetry, $W(F)\to\infty$ as $\det F\to 0^+$, $W(F)=\infty$ if $\det F\le 0$, and suitable polyconvexity/coercivity ensuring existence of minimizers in the classical pure elastic setting.

For a deformation $y:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^3$ in a space of special functions of bounded variation (so that the approximate gradient $Dy$ exists a.e. and the jump set $S_y$ is a countably $\mathcal{H}^{2}$-rectifiable subset of $\Omega$), and for a surface energy density $\psi:\mathbb{R}^3\times \mathbb{R}^3\times S^2\to [0,\infty)$ (depending on the one-sided traces $y^\pm$ and the unit normal $\nu_y$ to $S_y$), define the Griffith-type variational fracture energy
$$
I(y)=\int_{\Omega} W(Dy)\,dx+\int_{S_y}\psi(y^+,y^-,\nu_y)\,d\mathcal{H}^{2},
$$
subject to prescribed Dirichlet boundary data on a portion of $\partial\Omega$.

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded domain occupied (in a reference configuration) by a hyperelastic body, and let $\varphi : \Omega \times [0,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^3$ denote the deformation, with deformation gradient $F = \nabla \varphi$ required to satisfy $\det F > 0$. Assume a stored-energy function $W : M^{3\times 3}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ that is frame-indifferent and polyconvex (or, more generally, satisfies standard constitutive hypotheses of nonlinear elasticity, including $W(F) \to \infty$ as $\det F \to 0^+$), and let the first Piola–Kirchhoff stress be $S(F) = \partial W / \partial F$.

Consider the equations of motion of nonlinear elastodynamics
$$\rho_0\, \varphi_{tt} = \operatorname{div} S(\nabla \varphi) + b \quad \text{in } \Omega \times (0,\infty),$$
where $\rho_0 > 0$ is the reference mass density and $b$ is a given body force, supplemented by mixed boundary conditions
$$\varphi = \varphi_0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega_D \times (0,\infty), \qquad S(\nabla\varphi)\, n = t_N \text{ on } \partial\Omega_N \times (0,\infty),$$
with $\partial\Omega = \overline{\partial\Omega_D} \cup \overline{\partial\Omega_N}$, and initial data
$$\varphi(\cdot,0) = \varphi_0, \qquad \varphi_t(\cdot,0) = v_0.$$
One may equally consider the corresponding isothermal thermoelastic or thermoviscoelastic systems obtained by coupling the above with the balance of energy and a constitutive law for the heat flux, supplemented by appropriate thermal boundary and initial conditions.

Problem. For a suitably formulated such initial–boundary value problem, prove the global existence and uniqueness of a solution (in an appropriate weak or measure-valued sense compatible with the constitutive assumptions and ensuring $\det \nabla \varphi > 0$ a.e. for all $t > 0$), for arbitrary smooth initial data of finite energy.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Global existence and uniqueness for the initial–boundary value problem of three-dimensional nonlinear elastodynamics (and its thermo(visco)elastic counterparts) is widely regarded as a major open problem. Only local-in-time existence, small-data global existence (e.g. results of Sideris and others for the Cauchy problem in unbounded domains with null conditions), and special one-dimensional or viscoelastic regularized cases are known. No general global well-posedness theorem in the polyconvex finite-elasticity setting is available.

Consider a dynamic theory of nonlinear elasticity for a body occupying a reference configuration $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ (a bounded, sufficiently regular domain), with deformation $y:\Omega 	imes [0,\infty) 	o \mathbb{R}^3$ governed by a system of evolution equations of the form
\[
\rho\, y_{tt} = \operatorname{Div}\, S(\nabla y) + \text{(dissipative terms)} ,
\]
where $S = \partial W/\partial F$ is the Piola–Kirchhoff stress derived from a stored-energy function $W:\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying standard frame-indifference, polyconvexity or quasiconvexity, and coercivity assumptions, together with suitable boundary conditions (e.g., mixed displacement/traction) and dissipation (e.g., viscous, viscoelastic of rate type, or thermomechanical coupling giving a ballistic free energy $\Psi$).

Assume that a global-in-time solution theory has been established in an appropriate function space $X$, generating a (possibly multivalued) semiflow $\{S(t)\}_{t\ge 0}$ on $X$.

Develop a qualitative theory of the dynamics of this semiflow by establishing the following:

1. Convergence of trajectories: characterize which initial data $y_0 \in X$ produce solutions $S(t)y_0$ whose $\omega$-limit sets consist of equilibria (stationary solutions of the elastostatic problem $\operatorname{Div}\,S(\nabla y) = 0$ with the given boundary data), and describe the modes of convergence.

2. Basins of attraction: for each (stable) equilibrium $\bar y$, determine the structure of its basin of attraction $\mathcal{B}(\bar y) = \{y_0 \in X : S(t)y_0 \to \bar y\}$.

3. Invariant manifolds: construct local stable, unstable, and center manifolds at equilibria, and clarify their regularity and persistence.

4. Global attractors: prove existence and characterize the structure (e.g., finite Hausdorff/fractal dimension, gradient structure) of a global attractor $\mathcal{A} \subset X$ for the semiflow.

5. Energy minimization along orbits: determine whether dynamic orbits realize local minimizing sequences for the ballistic free energy functional $\Psi$ — that is, whether for generic initial data the trajectory $t \mapsto S(t)y_0$ provides a minimizing sequence (in an appropriate local sense) for $\Psi$ over an admissible class, and characterize the limiting microstructures (e.g., Young measures) that may emerge when classical minimizers fail to exist.

Provide answers to (1)–(5) under explicit and physically reasonable hypotheses on $W$, the dissipation mechanism, and the boundary conditions.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

This is a long-standing programmatic open problem in nonlinear elastodynamics. Partial results exist for special cases (viscoelasticity of rate type, one-dimensional models, gradient-flow approximations, quasistatic limits), but no comprehensive qualitative dynamics theory covering convergence to equilibria, basins of attraction, invariant manifolds, global attractors, and minimizing-orbit properties for ballistic free energy is available in the general 3D nonlinear elasticity setting. The problem remains open.

representations.normalized:
Consider a hyperelastic body occupying a bounded reference domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ with Lipschitz boundary, governed by a stored-energy function $W:\Omega\times M^{3\times 3}_+\to\mathbb{R}$ (with $M^{3\times 3}_+$ the $3\times 3$ matrices of positive determinant). The total elastic energy of a deformation $y:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^3$ is
$$E(y)=\int_\Omega W(x,\nabla y(x))\,dx,$$
subject to suitable boundary conditions (e.g. $y=\bar y$ on a part $\partial\Omega_1$ of $\partial\Omega$ and prescribed traction or zero traction on the remainder). The dynamic equations of motion are
$$\rho\, y_{tt} = \operatorname{Div}\bigl(D_F W(x,\nabla y)\bigr) + b(x,t),\qquad x\in\Omega,\; t>0,$$
together with the chosen boundary conditions and initial data $y(\cdot,0)=y_0$, $y_t(\cdot,0)=y_1$. Assume $W$ is polyconvex and satisfies natural growth and frame-indifference hypotheses sufficient for existence of equilibria as minimizers of $E$.

An equilibrium $\bar y$ (a critical point of $E$) is called Lyapunov stable for the dynamic equations if for every neighborhood $U$ of $(\bar y,0)$ in a chosen function-space topology there exists a neighborhood $V\subset U$ such that every weak solution $(y(\cdot,t),y_t(\cdot,t))$ with $(y_0,y_1)\in V$ remains in $U$ for all $t\ge 0$; asymptotically stable if in addition $(y(\cdot,t),y_t(\cdot,t))\to(\bar y,0)$ as $t\to\infty$. Recall a deformation $\bar y$ is a local minimizer of $E$ in a topology $\tau$ if $E(\bar y)\le E(y)$ for all admissible $y$ in some $\tau$-neighborhood of $\bar y$.

Problem. Develop rigorous criteria for the dynamic stability and instability of equilibria in nonlinear elasticity. In particular:
(a) Identify which notions of local minimizer of $E$ (e.g. strong $L^\infty$ local minimizers, $W^{1,p}$ local minimizers for various $p$, quasiconvex-at-the-boundary local minimizers) suffice to imply Lyapunov, respectively asymptotic, stability of the corresponding equilibrium for the dynamic equations above.
(b) Provide verifiable conditions on $W$ and $\bar y$ under which a non-minimizing equilibrium (or a local minimizer that fails some appropriate quasiconvexity condition) is dynamically unstable, with a rigorous justification of the instability.

Consider a crystalline solid modeled as a discrete configuration of atoms occupying, in a reference state, the lattice $\varepsilon \mathbb{Z}^d \cap \Omega$ (or a more general Bravais/multilattice) inside a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, where $\varepsilon>0$ is the interatomic spacing. To each deformation $y:\varepsilon\mathbb{Z}^d\cap\Omega \to \mathbb{R}^d$ associate a discrete energy $E_\varepsilon(y)$ derived from one of the following atomistic descriptions:
(i) a quantum many-body Schrödinger Hamiltonian for nuclei and electrons;
(ii) a Kohn–Sham or Hartree–Fock density-functional energy;
(iii) a Thomas–Fermi (or Thomas–Fermi–von Weizsäcker) functional;
(iv) a classical interatomic potential energy $E_\varepsilon(y)=\sum_{i} V_i\bigl(\{y(x_j)-y(x_i)\}_{j}\bigr)$ involving pair, three-body, or many-body interactions (e.g. Lennard–Jones, embedded-atom, Stillinger–Weber).

Address rigorously the following three coupled questions.

1. (Derivation of continuum elasticity.) For each class of atomistic model above, identify a continuum elastic energy functional
$$E(u)=\int_\Omega W(\nabla u(x))\,dx$$
(or its appropriate non-simple/higher-gradient generalization) and a function space $X$ of admissible deformations $u:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^d$ such that $E_\varepsilon \xrightarrow{\Gamma} E$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$ in a suitable topology, and characterize the stored-energy density $W$ (e.g. via the Cauchy–Born rule $W(F)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N^d}\min E_{\rm cell}(F\cdot\,\cdot\,)$) together with its domain of validity (small strains, frame indifference, material symmetry, possible loss of validity under large or non-rank-one strains).

2. (Limits of true minimizers.) Let $y_\varepsilon$ be a sequence of (almost) minimizers of $E_\varepsilon$ subject to prescribed boundary or loading data. Determine the limiting functional $\mathcal{F}$ and function space $X^*$ (which may differ from $X$ above and may incorporate defects: dislocations, cracks, grain boundaries, or plastic slip) such that, up to subsequence, $y_\varepsilon \to u$ in $X^*$ and $u$ minimizes $\mathcal{F}$, and identify the mechanism by which microstructure, defects, or singular measures arise in $\mathcal{F}$.

3. (Quasicontinuum coupling.) Formulate quasicontinuum-type atomistic-to-continuum coupling schemes (energy-based, force-based, blended, or ghost-force-free variants) in which the atomistic energy is retained in a small subdomain while a Cauchy–Born continuum approximation is used elsewhere, and establish: (a) consistency (truncation/coupling error), (b) stability of the linearized coupled operator uniformly in $\varepsilon$ and in the size of the atomistic region, and (c) optimal a priori and a posteriori error estimates between the coupled solution and the fully atomistic minimizer in the presence of typical defects (point defects, dislocations, cracks).

Provide a unified rigorous theory, valid for at least one of the model classes (i)–(iv), that simultaneously answers (1), (2), and (3).

Significant partial results exist: Γ-convergence derivations of nonlinear elasticity from pair interactions (Alicandro–Cicalese, Friesecke–Theil), rigorous plate theory (Friesecke–James–Müller), Cauchy–Born validity in small-strain regimes (E–Ming, Conti–Dolzmann–Kirchheim–Müller), and convergence/error analyses of quasicontinuum methods (Ortner, Luskin, Süli, and collaborators), including blended force-based schemes for multilattices with defects. However, a unified rigorous derivation starting from quantum, DFT, or Thomas–Fermi models, a complete characterization of limits of true atomistic minimizers in the presence of generic defects, and a fully general convergence theory for atomistic/continuum coupling remain open active research areas.

Consider a continuum model of an elastic solid occupying a reference domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$, whose deformations $y:\Omega\times[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}^3$ are governed by a stored-energy functional
$$ E[y] = \int_\Omega W(\nabla y(x),\theta(x))\,dx, $$
where $\theta$ is temperature and $W:\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a frame-indifferent multi-well energy density whose set of energy-minimizing gradients $K(\theta)=\{F:W(F,\theta)=\min W(\cdot,\theta)\}$ corresponds to distinct martensitic variants (so that $W$ is, in general, non-quasiconvex). Material points may also satisfy a dynamical evolution law of the form
$$ \rho\, y_{tt} = \mathrm{Div}\, T(\nabla y, \nabla y_t,\theta) + f, $$
augmented by a kinetic relation governing the motion and nucleation of phase interfaces.

For such a material undergoing phase transformations that exhibit fine microstructure (rapidly oscillating gradient fields taking values close to $K(\theta)$):

(a) Provide a rigorous mathematical explanation, within a suitably formulated dynamical theory incorporating interface kinetics, of why fine microstructure forms, rather than merely characterizing it as a non-attainment phenomenon for the static energy functional.

(b) Predict the resulting morphology of the microstructure (length scales, geometric patterns of the laminates or more complex arrangements, and their dependence on boundary conditions, loading history, and kinetics).

(c) Determine the effective macroscopic material response on scales much larger than the microstructural length scale: in particular, identify a well-posed homogenized/relaxed dynamical theory whose solutions describe the observed average behavior of materials with such microstructure.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is a long-standing open program in the mathematical theory of martensitic phase transformations and nonlinear elasticity. While partial results exist (quasiconvex envelopes, Young measure characterizations of laminates, rigidity results, and special dynamical models with interface kinetics), no general dynamical theory predicting microstructure formation and macroscopic effective behavior is known. It is presented as an open problem in recent surveys.

representations.normalized:
Setting. Consider a thermoelastic single crystal in three dimensions undergoing a diffusionless (displacive) phase transformation at a critical temperature θ_c. Let M^{3×3} denote the set of real 3×3 matrices and M^{3×3}_+ the subset of matrices with strictly positive determinant. Suppose ψ : M^{3×3}_+ × ℝ → [0,∞) is a frame-indifferent stored-energy density (so ψ(RA,θ) = ψ(A,θ) for every R ∈ SO(3)) which is materially symmetric under the cubic point group, and which for each temperature θ attains its minimum value 0. Define the set of energy-minimizing deformation gradients at temperature θ by

   K(θ) := { A ∈ M^{3×3}_+ : ψ(A,θ) = 0 }.

For a compact set K ⊂ M^{3×3}, its quasiconvexification K^{qc} is defined as

   K^{qc} := { A ∈ M^{3×3} : f(A) ≤ sup_{B ∈ K} f(B) for every quasiconvex f : M^{3×3} → ℝ },

where f : M^{3×3} → ℝ is quasiconvex if for every bounded open Ω ⊂ ℝ^3, every A ∈ M^{3×3}, and every φ ∈ W^{1,∞}_0(Ω;ℝ^3),

   ∫_Ω f(A + ∇φ(x)) dx ≥ |Ω| f(A).

For the cubic-to-tetragonal case at and below θ_c, one has explicitly
   K(θ) = SO(3) U_1(θ) ∪ SO(3) U_2(θ) ∪ SO(3) U_3(θ)    for θ < θ_c,
   K(θ_c) = SO(3) ∪ SO(3) U_1(θ_c) ∪ SO(3) U_2(θ_c) ∪ SO(3) U_3(θ_c),
where U_i(θ) = diag(η_2, η_2, η_2) with the entry η_1 in the i-th diagonal position (η_1, η_2 > 0 temperature-dependent stretch parameters with η_1 ≠ η_2 for θ < θ_c, and η_1 = η_2 = 1 at θ = θ_c giving the austenite identity).

Problem. Determine the quasiconvexification K(θ)^{qc} explicitly for all θ ≤ θ_c, in particular for the cubic-to-tetragonal three-well case (and the four-well case at θ = θ_c that also includes SO(3)).

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem is widely regarded as open. While the two-well quasiconvexification (relevant to e.g. orthorhombic-to-monoclinic transitions) has been computed via minors relations, the three-well cubic-to-tetragonal case—and the four-well case including SO(3) at θ = θ_c—remains unresolved. Partial results, such as characterizing rank-one connections between SO(3) and K(θ)^{qc} (Ball–Carstensen) and other structural properties, are known, but a complete explicit description of K(θ)^{qc} is not available.
